18:1: Surat Al-Kahf It is Meccan Mention of what was mentioned about its merits and the ten verses from the beginning to the end and that it is a protection from the Antichrist Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Al-Bara` say: A man was reciting Surat Al-Kahf and there was a beast in the house, and it began to scatter. He looked and saw that a mist or cloud had covered it, so he mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Recite, so-and-so, for it is tranquility that descends with the Qur’an or was revealed for the Qur’an. They both included it in the two Sahihs on the authority of Shu`bah on his authority. This man who was reciting it was Asid ibn Al-Hudayr, as mentioned previously in the interpretation of Surat Al-Baqarah. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Hisham ibn Yahya told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi Al-Ja`d, on the authority of Ma`dan ibn Abi Talhah, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda`, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever memorizes ten verses from the beginning of Surat Al-Kahf will be protected from the Antichrist. Narrated by Muslim, Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa’i and Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Qatadah on his authority. Al-Tirmidhi’s wording is: Whoever memorizes three verses from the beginning of Surat Al-Kahf. He said: Hasan Sahih. Another way - Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Qatadah, I heard Salim bin Abi al-Ja`d narrating on the authority of Ma`dan on the authority of Abu al-Darda`, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever recites the last ten verses of Surat al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Antichrist. It is possible that Salim heard it from Thawban and Abu al-Darda`. Ahmad said: Husayn told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Zaban ibn Fayid told us, on the authority of Sahl ibn Mu’adh ibn Anas al-Juhani, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Whoever recites the beginning of Surat al-Kahf and the end, it will be a light for him from his feet to his head, and whoever recites it all, it will be a light for him between the heavens and the earth.” Ahmad is the only one who narrated it and they did not include it. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated in his interpretation with a strange chain of transmission on the authority of Khalid ibn Sa’id ibn Abi Maryam, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites Surat al-Kahf on Friday, a light will shine for him from beneath his feet to the clouds of the sky, illuminating him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will be forgiven between the two Fridays.” This hadith is questionable in its being attributed to the Prophet, but the best way to classify it is to stop. Thus, Imam Saeed bin Mansour narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Hisham bin Bashir on the authority of Abu Hashim on the authority of Abu Majlaz on the authority of Qais bin Abbad on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, that he said: Whoever recites Surat Al-Kahf on Friday, a light will shine for him that will extend between him and the Ancient House. Thus it was reported by Al-Thawri on the authority of Abu Hashim on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri. Al-Hakim included it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Al-Mu’ammal, Al-Fudayl ibn Muhammad Al-Sha’rani told us, Na’eem ibn Hammad told us, Hisham told us, Abu Hashim told us on the authority of Abu Majlaz on the authority of Qais ibn Abbad, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Whoever recites Surat Al-Kahf on Friday, a light will shine for him between him and the two Fridays. Then he said: This is a hadith with a sound chain of transmission, and they did not include it. Thus Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in his Sunan on the authority of Al-Hakim. Then Al-Bayhaqi said: Yahya ibn Kathir narrated it on the authority of Shu’bah on the authority of Abu Hashim with his chain of transmission that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites Surat Al-Kahf as it was revealed, it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection. And in Al-Mukhtara by Al-Hafiz Al-Dhiya’ Al-Maqdisi on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mus’ab on the authority of Manzur ibn Zayd ibn Khalid Al-Juhani, on the authority of Ali ibn Al-Husayn on the authority of his father on the authority of Ali. It was narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever recites Surat Al-Kahf on Friday will be protected from every trial for eight days, and if the Antichrist emerges, he will be protected from him. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful It was mentioned at the beginning of the interpretation that the Almighty praises His Holy Self at the beginnings and ends of matters, for He is the Praised One in every situation, and to Him is praise in the first and the last. For this reason, He praised Himself for sending down His Noble Book to His Noble Messenger Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, for it is the greatest blessing that God bestowed upon the people of the earth, for He brought them out with it from darkness into the light, as He made it a straight Book, in which there is no crookedness or deviation, but rather it guides to a straight, clear, evident path, a warner to the disbelievers and a bearer of good tidings to the believers. For this reason, He said: And He has not made it crooked, meaning He did not make it crooked or inclined, but rather He made it straight and upright. For this reason, He said: straight, meaning upright, to warn of a severe punishment from Him, meaning to those who oppose Him, deny Him, and do not believe in Him, He warns them of a severe punishment, an immediate punishment in this world and a deferred punishment in the hereafter, from Him, meaning from God, who does not punish as He punishes, and does not bind as He binds, and to give good tidings to the believers. That is, by this Qur’an, those who have confirmed their faith through righteous deeds, for them is a good reward, that is, a beautiful reward from God, abiding therein, in their reward from God, which is Paradise, abiding therein forever, always, without end or cessation. And His statement: And to warn those who say, ‘God has taken a son,’ Ibn Ishaq said: They are the polytheists of the Arabs in their saying, We worship the angels, even though they are the daughters of God. “They have no knowledge of it,” meaning of this statement that they invented and fabricated. Nor did their fathers, meaning their ancestors. A great word, accusative of specification, meaning, A great word of theirs. It was said: It is an expression of astonishment, its meaning is greater than their word, as you say: Akram bi Zayd is a man, as some of the Basrans said. Some of the Meccan reciters read it: Kabbar kalimah, as you say: Your saying is great and Your status is great. The meaning according to the reading of the majority is clearer, as this is an exaggeration of their statement and an exaggeration of their slander. For this reason, he said: Kabbar kalimah emanate from their mouths, meaning that it has no basis other than their statement, and they have no evidence for it other than their lies and fabrications. For this reason, he said: They say nothing but a lie. Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned the reason for the revelation of this noble surah, as he said: An old man from Egypt who came to us forty-some years ago told me on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Quraysh sent al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt to the Jewish rabbis in Medina, and they said to them: Ask them about Muhammad and describe his description to them and inform them of his statement, for they are the people of the first book and they have what we do not have of the knowledge of the prophets. So they went out until they came to Medina and asked the Jewish rabbis about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they described to them. His command and some of his words, and they said: You are the people of the Torah and we have come to you to inform us about this companion of ours. He said: So they said to them, Ask him about three things that we command you to do, if he informs you of them then he is a prophet sent to you, otherwise he is a slanderer, so make up your mind about him: Ask him about the youths who passed away in the first era, what was their affair, for they had a strange story? And ask him about a man who traveled and reached the east and west of the earth, what was his report, and ask him about the spirit, what is it? If he tells you that, then he is a prophet, so follow him. If he does not tell you, then he is a man who is lying, so do whatever you want with regard to his affair. So Al-Nadr and Uqbah came until they reached Quraysh and said: O people of Quraysh, we have come to you with a settlement between you and Muhammad. The Jewish rabbis have ordered us to ask him about matters, so inform them of them. So they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, inform us. So they asked him about what they ordered them to do. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: I will inform you tomorrow about what you asked about, and he did not make an exception. So they turned away from him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, remained for fifteen nights without God sending him any revelation about that, nor did Gabriel, peace be upon him, come to him until the people of Mecca became alarmed and said: Muhammad promised us tomorrow, and today we have become fifteen, and he does not inform us of anything about what we asked him about. And until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was saddened by the delay in the revelation from him and he was distressed by what the people of Mecca were saying. Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him from God Almighty with Surat Ashab al-Kahf, in which He reproached him for his sadness over them. And the report of what they asked him about regarding the matter of the young men and the circumambulating man, and the saying of God Almighty: And they ask you about the soul? Say, ‘The soul’ verse.

The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, remained for fifteen nights without God sending him any revelation about that, nor did Gabriel, peace be upon him, come to him until the people of Mecca became alarmed and said: Muhammad promised us tomorrow, and today we have become fifteen, and he does not inform us of anything about what we asked him about. And until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was saddened by the delay in the revelation from him and he was distressed by what the people of Mecca were saying. Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him from God Almighty with Surat Ashab al-Kahf, in which He reproached him for his sadness over them. And the report of what they asked him about regarding the matter of the young men and the circumambulating man, and the saying of God Almighty: And they ask you about the soul? Say, ‘The soul’ verse.
18:6: God Almighty says, comforting His Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, in his grief over the polytheists for abandoning faith and distancing themselves from it, as God Almighty said: So let not your soul perish over them in regret and He said: And do not grieve over them and He said: Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not believe “Bakh’a” means destroying yourself with your grief over them, and for this reason He said: Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over them, if they do not believe in this message meaning the Qur’an out of sorrow He says: Do not destroy yourself with grief. Qatada said: Fight yourself out of anger and grief for them. Mujahid said: Out of impatience. The meaning is similar, that is, do not feel sorry for them, but convey to them the message of God. Whoever is guided, it is for his own sake, and whoever goes astray, it is for his own sake, and do not let yourself be filled with regrets for them. Then God the Almighty informed us that He made this world a transient home decorated with fleeting adornments, and He made it a home of testing, not a home of settlement. He said: Indeed, We have made whatever is on the earth adornment for it that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed. Qatada said on the authority of Abu Nadrah on the authority of Abu Saeed on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Indeed, this world is sweet and green, and God will make you successors in it and see what you do. So beware of this world, and beware of women, for the first trial of the Children of Israel was in women.” Then God the Almighty informed us of its disappearance, annihilation, emptiness, expiration, passing away, and destruction. He said: And indeed, We will make whatever is on it a barren plain. That is, after its adornment, We will turn it into ruin and destruction. We will make everything on it perish. A barren plain that produces no growth or benefit. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the Almighty’s statement: And indeed, We will make that which is upon it a barren plain, meaning: everything on it will perish and be destroyed. Mujahid said: A barren, desolate plain. Qatada said: The plain is the land that has no trees or plants. Ibn Zayd said: The plain is the land that has nothing. Do you not see the statement of the Almighty: Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land and bring forth thereby crops from which their livestock and themselves eat? Then will they not see? Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: And indeed, We will make that which is upon it a barren plain, meaning the earth and that what is upon it will perish and be destroyed, and that the return is to God, so do not despair and do not be saddened by what you hear and see.

18:9: This is a report from God Almighty about the story of the People of the Cave in summary and brevity, then He expanded it after that and said: Or do you think meaning O Muhammad that the People of the Cave and the Inscription were among Our signs, a wonder meaning their matter is not a wonder in Our power and authority, for the creation of the heavens and the earth, the alternation of night and day, the subjugation of the sun, moon, and planets, and other great signs indicating the power of God Almighty, and that He is able to do whatever He wills and nothing is beyond His power, more amazing than the stories of the People of the Cave, as Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Mujahid Or do you think that the People of the Cave and the Inscription were among Our signs, a wonder meaning: There were signs from Our signs that were more amazing than that. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Or do you think that the People of the Cave and the Inscription were, among Our signs, a wonder? He said: What I have given you of knowledge, the Sunnah, and the Book is better than the case of the People of the Cave and the Inscription. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The proofs I have shown to the servants are more amazing than the case of the People of the Cave and the Inscription. As for the Cave, it is the cave in the mountain, and it is the one to which these young men mentioned took refuge. As for the Inscription, Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is a valley near Ayla. This is what Atiyah Al-Awfi and Qatadah said. Ad-Dahhak said: As for the Cave, it is a cave in the valley, and the Inscription is the name of the valley. Mujahid said: The Inscription was their building, and some of them say: It is the valley in which their cave is. Abdul Razzaq said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of Ar-Raqim: Kaab used to claim that it was the village. Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Ar-Raqim is the mountain in which the cave is located. Ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The name of that mountain is Banglos. Ibn Jurayj said: Wahb bin Sulayman told me, on the authority of Shuayb Al-Jubba’i, that the name of the cave mountain is Banglos, and the name of the cave is Haizam, and the dog is Hamran. Abdul Razzaq said: Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Qur’an is known to me except for Hanan, Al-Awah, and Ar-Raqim. Ibn Jurayj said: Amr bin Dinar told me that he heard Ikrimah say: Ibn Abbas said: I do not know what Ar-Raqim is? Is it a book or a building? Ali bin Abi Talhah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Ar-Raqim is the book. Saeed bin Jubair said: Ar-Raqim is a tablet of stones on which they wrote the stories of the People of the Cave, then they placed it at the entrance of the cave. Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: Ar-Raqim is the book. Then he recited: A book marked. This is what is apparent from the verse, and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir. He said: Ar-Raqim is a noun meaning marked, just as someone who is killed is called qatil, and someone who is wounded is called jareeh. And God knows best. And His statement: When the young men took refuge in the cave, they said, ‘Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself and facilitate for us our affair with right guidance.’ God Almighty informs us about those young men who fled with their religion from their people lest they tempt them away from it. So they fled from them and took refuge in a cave in a mountain to hide from their people. So when they entered, they said, asking God Almighty for His mercy and kindness towards them, Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself, meaning, grant us mercy from You with which to have mercy on us and conceal us from our people. And facilitate for us our affair with right guidance, meaning, and decree for us from this affair of ours right guidance, meaning, make our end right guidance, as it came in the hadith, And whatever You decree for us, make its end right guidance. And in Al-Musnad, from the hadith of Busr ibn Artah, from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he used to supplicate, O God, make our end good in all matters, and save us from the disgrace of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. And His statement: So We sealed their ears in the cave for a number of years means We cast sleep upon them when they entered the cave, so they slept for many years, Then We raised them up meaning from their sleep, and one of them went out with dirhams with him to buy them food to eat, as will be explained and detailed. For this reason He said: Then We raised them up that We might know which of the two parties meaning the ones who differed among them had best counted the period of their tarry it was said: a number, and it was said: a limit, for the period is the limit, like His statement: The horse has outpaced the distance

18:13: From here he began to expand and explain the story, so God Almighty mentioned that they were young men, and they were the youth, and they were more accepting of the truth and more guided to the path than the elders who had become arrogant and immersed themselves in the religion of falsehood, and for this reason most of those who responded to God Almighty and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, were young men, and as for the elders of Quraysh, most of them remained in their religion and only a few of them converted to Islam. Thus, the Almighty said about the People of the Cave that they were young men. Mujahid said: It has reached me that some of them had earrings in their ears, meaning rings, so God inspired them with their right guidance and gave them their piety, so they believed in their Lord, meaning they acknowledged His Oneness, and they testified that there is no god but Him. And We increased them in guidance. This verse and others like it were used as evidence by more than one of the imams, such as Al-Bukhari and others who believed that faith increases and differs, and that it increases and decreases. For this reason, the Almighty said: And We increased them in guidance, as He said: And those who were guided, He increased them in guidance and gave them their piety, and He said: As for those who believed, He increased them in faith, and they rejoiced, and He said: That they might increase in faith along with their faith, and other verses indicating this. So when they decided to go and flee from their people, and God chose that for them and informed about that in His statement, And when you have withdrawn from them and what they worship except God, meaning, when you have separated from them and differed from them in your religions in their worship of other than God, then separate from them also in your bodies, “then take refuge in the cave. Your Lord will spread out for you from His mercy,” meaning, He will spread out mercy upon you with which He will cover you from your people, and will prepare for you from your affair, which you are in, ease, meaning, A matter that you may be guided by. Then they fled to the cave and took refuge in it. Their people lost them among them and the king sought them out. It is said that he did not find them and God blinded him to their report, as He did with His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companion Abu Bakr when they took refuge in the Cave of Thawr. The polytheists of Quraysh came in pursuit but they could not find him, even though they passed by him. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when he saw Abu Bakr’s distress in his words: O Messenger of God, if one of them looked at the place where his feet were, he would see us. He said: O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two people with God as their third? And God Almighty said: “If you do not aid him - God has already aided him when those who disbelieved expelled him, one of two, when they were in the cave and he said to his companion, ‘Do not grieve; indeed God is with us.’ So God sent down His tranquility upon him and supported him with soldiers you did not see. And He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of God - that is the highest. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise.” So the story of this cave is more honorable, more sublime, greater and more amazing than the story of the People of the Cave. It has been said that their people overcame them and stopped at the door of the cave which they had entered, and they said: We did not want from them any more punishment than what they did to themselves. So the king ordered the door to be closed over them so that they would perish on the spot, and they did that. There is a consideration in this, and God knows best, for God Almighty has informed us that the sun enters the cave upon them in the morning and evening, as God Almighty said:
18:17: This is evidence that the entrance to this cave was towards the north, because the Almighty informed us that when the sun enters it at sunrise, it deviates from it to the right, meaning the shade shrinks to the right, as Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubayr and Qatadah said. Deviates means inclines, because whenever it rises in the horizon, its rays shrink with its rise until nothing of it remains at noon in such a place. For this reason, He said: And when it sets, it passes them to the left, meaning it enters their cave from the north of its entrance, which is from the east, so it indicates the correctness of what we said. This is clear to whoever contemplates it and has knowledge of the formation and the movement of the sun, moon and planets. Its explanation is that if the entrance to the cave was from the east, nothing would have entered it from it at sunset. If it was from the direction of the qiblah, nothing would have entered it from it at sunrise or at sunset, and the shade would not have deviated to the right or left. If it was from the west, it would not have entered it at sunrise, but after noon, and it would not have remained in it until sunset. So what is clear is that We mentioned it, thank God. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said: If you lend them, you will leave them. God the Almighty has informed us of this and wanted us to understand and ponder it. He did not tell us in which country on earth this cave is located, as there is no benefit for us in it and no legal purpose. Some commentators have taken it upon themselves to mention different opinions about it. It was mentioned earlier from Ibn Abbas that he said: It is near Ayla. Ibn Ishaq said: It is near Nineveh. It was also said: In the land of the Romans. It was said: In the land of Balqa, and God knows best which land of God it is, and if we had a religious interest in it, God Almighty and His Messenger would have guided us to it, for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have not left anything that brings you closer to Paradise and distances you from the Fire except that I have informed you of it. So God Almighty informed us of its description, but He did not inform us of its location, for He said: And you will see the sun when it rises, declining from their cave. Malik said on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam: It inclines to the right, and when it sets, it passes them by on the left, while they are in an open space thereof, meaning in a wide space inside it such that it does not hit them, for if it hit them, it would burn their bodies and clothes. Ibn Abbas said: That is from the signs of God, as He guided them to this cave in which He made them alive, and the sun and wind enter upon them in it to preserve their bodies. For this reason, God Almighty said: That is from the signs of God, then He said: He whom God guides is the one who is guided, the verse, meaning He is the one who guided these young men to guidance from among their people, for he whom God guides is guided, and he whom He misguides There is no guide for him.
18:18: Some scholars have mentioned that when God struck their ears with sleep, they did not close so that they would not quickly decay. If they remained exposed to the air, it would be better for them to remain. For this reason, God Almighty said: And you think them awake while they are asleep. It has been mentioned about the wolf that he sleeps, closing one eye and opening the other, then opening this one and closing the other while he is asleep, as the poet said: He sleeps with one eye and protects himself from calamities with the other, so he is awake and asleep. God the Almighty said: And We turn them to the right and to the left. Some of the Salaf said: They turn twice a year. Ibn Abbas said: If they were not turned, the earth would have eaten them. His statement: And their dog stretching out his forelegs at the entrance. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr and Qatadah said: The entrance is the courtyard. Ibn Abbas said: At the door. It was said: At the ground, which is the dirt. The correct view is that it is at the courtyard, which is the door. From this is the statement of God the Almighty: It is closed upon them, meaning closed and locked. It is said: And he was seen and he was seen. Their dog lay down at the door as is the custom of dogs. Ibn Jurayj said: He guards the door for them. This is from his nature and disposition, as he lies down at their door as if he is guarding them. He was sitting outside the door, because angels do not enter a house in which there is a dog, as mentioned in the Sahih, nor a picture, nor a person in a state of ritual impurity, nor an unbeliever, as mentioned in the hasan hadith. Their dog was covered by their blessing, so he was afflicted with what afflicted them from sleeping in that state. This is the benefit of keeping company with the report, because this dog became mentioned, reported and important. It was said that he was a hunting dog of one of them, and this is more likely. It was also said that he was the dog of the king’s cook, and he agreed with them on religion and his dog accompanied him. God knows best. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated in the biography of Hammam bin Al-Walid Al-Dimashqi: Sadaqah bin Omar Al-Ghasani told us, Ibad Al-Manqari told us, I heard Al-Hasan Al-Basri say: The name of Abraham’s ram, peace be upon him, was Jarir, the name of Solomon’s hoopoe, peace be upon him, was Anqaz, the name of the dog of the Companions of the Cave was Qatmir, the name of the calf of the Children of Israel that they worshipped was Bahamut, Adam, peace be upon him, descended in India, Eve in Jeddah, Satan settled in Bisan, and the serpent in Isfahan. It was mentioned earlier that Shu’ayb Al-Jubba’i called him Hamran, and they differed about his color based on statements that have no basis, no benefit, no evidence, and no need for them. Rather, they are among the things that are forbidden, and their basis is a guess at the unseen. And the Almighty’s saying: If you had looked at them, you would have turned away from them in flight and been filled with terror of them. That is, the Almighty cast awe upon them such that no one would look at them without fearing them because of the awe and terror they were clothed in, so that no one would come near them and no hand would touch them, until the Book reaches its term and their sleep that the Blessed and Exalted has willed for them ends, because of the wisdom, conclusive proof, and vast mercy He has in that.
18:19: God Almighty says, just as We put them to sleep, We resurrected them with their bodies, hair, and eyesight intact. They had not lost anything of their condition or appearance, and that was after three hundred and nine years. For this reason, they asked each other, How long did you stay? meaning, how long did you sleep? They said, We have stayed a day or part of a day, because they entered the cave at the beginning of the day, and they woke up at the end of the day. That is why they realized this and said, Or part of a day. They said, Your Lord knows best how long you have stayed, meaning, God knows best about your situation. It was as if they had some hesitation due to their long sleep, but God knows best. Then they turned to what was most important to them at that time, which was their need for food and drink. They said, Then send one of you with your silver, meaning, this is your silver. That is because they had taken dirhams with them from their homes because they needed them, so they gave some of it in charity and some of it remained. That is why they said, Then send one of you with this silver to the city, meaning, the city from which you had left. The alif and lam are for the covenant. Then let him see which of them has the best food, meaning, the best food. Such as His saying: And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever have been pure, and His saying: He has succeeded who purifies himself. And from this comes the zakat that purifies and makes money good, and it was said: more food, and from this comes the zaka of crops when they increase in number. The poet said: Our tribes are seven and you are three, and seven is better and more pleasant than three. The first is correct, because what they mean is the good and lawful, whether it is a lot or a little. And his saying, and let him be gentle, that is, in his going out, going, buying and returning. They say: And let him hide everything he can. And let no one perceive, that is, let no one know “about you. Indeed, if they gain control over you, they will stone you,” that is, if they know where you are, they will stone you or return you to their religion, meaning the followers of Decius, who fear that they will find out where they are, so they will continue to torture them with various types of torture until they return them to their religion that they are on, or they die. And if you agree with them in returning to religion, then there is no success for you in this world or in the hereafter. That is why he said: And you will never succeed then.

18:21: God the Almighty says: And thus We made them known meaning We made them known to the people so that they may know that the promise of God is true and that there is no doubt about the Hour. More than one of the predecessors mentioned that the people of that time had doubts about the resurrection and about the matter of the Day of Judgment. Ikrimah said: There was a group among them who said that bodies will be resurrected, so God sent the People of the Cave as an argument, proof and sign for that. They mentioned that when one of them wanted to go out to go to the city to buy them food, he disguised himself and went out walking in a different direction until he reached the city. They mentioned that its name was Daqsus, and he thought that he had recently come to it. The people had changed century after century, generation after generation and nation after nation, and the country and its people had changed, as the poet said: As for the houses, they are like their houses, and I see that the men of the neighborhood are not his men. He could not see any of the landmarks of the town that he knew, nor did he know any of its al-Nas 114:neither its elite nor its common people. He began to wonder to himself and say: Perhaps I am mad or possessed or dreaming, and he said: By God, there is nothing wrong with me, and I knew this town yesterday evening and it was not like this. Then he said: It is better for me to hasten to leave here. Then he went to a man who sold food, and gave him the money he had with him, and asked him to sell him food with it. When that man saw it, he denied it and denied hitting it, so he gave it to his neighbor, and they began to pass it around among themselves and say: Perhaps this man found a treasure. They asked him about his situation and where he got this money from. Perhaps he found it from a treasure, and from whom are you? He began to say: I am from the people of this town, and I saw it yesterday evening and Decius was in it, so they accused him of madness, so they took him to their ruler, who asked him about his condition and report until he informed them of his situation, and he was confused about his condition and what he was in, so when he informed them of that, they went with him to the cave - the king of the town and its people - until he reached them to the cave and said to them: Leave me so that I may go before you in entering to inform my companions, so he entered, and it is said that they do not know how he went in it, and God concealed their report from them, and it is said that they entered upon them and saw them, and the king greeted them and embraced them, and he was a Muslim, according to what was said, and his name was Tydosius, so they rejoiced at him and comforted him with words, then they bade him farewell and greeted him, and returned to their beds, and God Almighty took them, and God knows best. Qatada said: Ibn Abbas went on a military expedition with Habib bin Maslama, and they passed by a cave in the land of the Romans, and they saw bones in it. Someone said: These are the bones of the People of the Cave. Ibn Abbas said: Their bones have been rotting for more than three hundred years. Ibn Jarir narrated it. His statement: And thus We made them stumble upon means just as We made them sleep and awakened them in their forms, We made the people of that time see them so that they may know that the promise of God is true and that there is no doubt about the Hour when they dispute among themselves about their affair meaning about the matter of the Resurrection, so who would affirm it and who would deny it, so God made their appearance over the People of the Cave an argument for them and against them. “So they said, ‘Construct over them a structure. Their Lord knows best about them’” meaning they closed the door of their cave and left them in their state. Those who prevailed in their affair said, ‘We will surely build over them a mosque’ Ibn Jarir narrated two statements about those who said that one of them that they were the Muslims among them. The second are the polytheists among them, and God knows best. It appears that those who said that are the people of influence and power, but are they praiseworthy or not? There is a consideration in this, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God curse the Jews and Christians, for they took the graves of their prophets and righteous people as places of worship, warning against what they did. We have narrated from the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that when the grave of Daniel was found in his time in Iraq, he ordered that it be hidden from the people, and that the note that they found with him, in which there was something from the epics and other things, be buried.
18:22: God the Almighty says, informing about the people's disagreement over the number of the People of the Cave, so He mentioned three sayings, indicating that there is no one who says a fourth, and since He weakened the first two sayings by saying: A guess at the unseen meaning a saying without knowledge, like someone who shoots at a place he does not know, for he will hardly hit, and if he hits, it is without intent. Then He mentioned the third and was silent on it or confirmed it by saying: And their dog is the eighth of them, indicating its correctness, and that it is the reality in the matter itself. And His saying: Say, 'My Lord knows best their number' is guidance that the best thing in such a situation is to refer knowledge to God the Almighty, since there is no need to delve into such a matter without knowledge, but if we are informed of a matter, we say it, otherwise we stop. And his saying: None knows them except a few meaning from the people. Qatada said: Ibn Abbas said: I am from the few whom God Almighty excepted, they were seven. And Ibn Jarir narrated likewise on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani on his authority that he used to say: I am from those whom God Almighty excepted, and he used to say: Their number was seven. So these are authentic chains of transmission back to Ibn Abbas that they were seven, and it is in agreement with what we have presented. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid, who said: I was told that some of them had a clear complexion due to their young age. Ibn Abbas said: They were like that day and night in the worship of God, crying and seeking help from God. They were eight men: Maksalmina, the eldest of them, and he was the one who spoke to the king on their behalf, and Yamlikha, Martonus, Kastos, Berunus, Denimus, Yatbounus, and Qalush. This is how it appears in this narration. It is possible that this is from the words of Ibn Ishaq or someone in between, because the correct statement from Ibn Abbas is that they were seven, and this is the apparent meaning of the verse. It was previously reported from Shu’ayb al-Jubba’i that the name of their dog was Hamran. There is some doubt about calling them by these names and the name of their dog in its authenticity, and God knows best, because most of that was received from the People of the Book. God Almighty said: So do not dispute about them except with an apparent dispute, meaning easy and simple, because the matter of knowing that does not result in much benefit. And do not consult anyone of them about them, meaning that they have no knowledge of that except what they say of their own accord, guessing from the unseen, meaning without relying on the words of an infallible one. God has brought you, O Muhammad, the truth in which there is no doubt or uncertainty, so He is the foremost judge. For all the books and sayings you offer.
18:23: This is guidance from God the Most High to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the etiquette of when he intends to do something in the future, to refer it to the will of God the Almighty, the Knower of the Unseen, who knows what was and what will be and what would not have been, had it been, how it would have been, as was established in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Solomon, son of David, peace be upon them both, said: ‘I will go around tonight to seventy women - and in another narration: ninety women, and in another narration: one hundred women - each of whom will give birth to a boy who will fight in the way of God.’ So it was said to him - and in another narration the angel said to him: ‘Say, God willing,’ but he did not say it. So he went around to them and only one of them gave birth to half a human being. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said - ‘By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if he had said, God willing, he would not have broken his oath, and his need would have been met.’” And in another narration: And they would have fought in the way of God, all together, as horsemen. And the reason for the revelation of this verse was mentioned at the beginning of the surah in the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when He was asked about the story of the People of the Cave, Tomorrow I will answer you, and the revelation was delayed for fifteen days. We mentioned it in full at the beginning of the surah, so there is no need to repeat it. His saying: And remember your Lord if you forget. It was said that its meaning is if you forget the exception, when you remember Him. This was said by Abu Al-Aaliyah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri. Hisham said on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding a man who swears an oath: He has the right to make an exception even if it is after a year. He used to say: And remember your Lord if you forget. It was said to Al-A’mash: Did you hear that from Mujahid? He said: Layth bin Abi Sulaym told me it. He thinks that this is what my garment is made of. Al-Tabarani narrated it from the hadith of Abu Mu’awiyah on the authority of Al-A’mash. The meaning of Ibn Abbas’s saying that he makes an exception even after a year is if he forgets to say in his oath or in his speech, If God wills, and he remembers even after a year, then the Sunnah for him to say that, so that he will have fulfilled the Sunnah of exception even if it is after the oath. This was said by Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him. He stated that it is not to remove the oath of oath or cancel the expiation. This is what Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said, and it is the correct one, and it is the most appropriate to interpret the words of Ibn Abbas according to it. And God knows best. Ikrimah said, And remember your Lord when you forget, if you become angry. This is an interpretation of the necessary. Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad bin Al-Harith Al-Jabali told us, Safwan bin Saleh told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Husayn, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, “And never say of anything, ‘I will do that tomorrow,’ except, ‘If God wills. And remember your Lord when you forget,” that you say, If God wills. Al-Tabarani also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And remember your Lord when you forget, the exception, so make an exception if you remember, and he said: It is specific to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and none of us can make an exception except in connection with his oath. Then he said: Al-Walid is the only one who narrated it from Abdul Aziz bin Husayn. Another possible meaning of the verse is that God, the Most High, guided whoever forgot something in his speech to remember God, the Most High, because forgetfulness is caused by Satan, as the servant of Moses said: And nothing made me forget except Satan, that I should remember it. And remembering God, the Most High, drives away Satan, so when Satan goes away, forgetfulness goes away, so remembering God, the Most High, is a reason for remembrance, and for this reason He said, And remember your Lord when you forget, and His statement, And say, “Perhaps my Lord will guide me to something closer to right guidance than this. That is, if you are asked about something you do not know, then ask God Almighty about it, and turn to Him to guide you to what is right and right in that. Other interpretations have been said, and God knows best.

18:25: This is report from God the Most High to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the amount of time the People of the Cave stayed in their cave from the time He put them to sleep until God resurrected them and the people of that time found them, and that it was three hundred years plus nine lunar years, which is three hundred solar years. If the difference between every hundred lunar years and solar years is three years, then this is why He said: after three hundred and they added nine. And His statement: "Say: God knows best how long they stayed" means if you are asked about how long they stayed and you do not have knowledge of that and a confirmation from God the Most High, then do not advance in it with anything, rather say in such a case: "God knows best how long they stayed. To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth" meaning that no one knows that except Him and those whom He informed of it from His creation, and this is what we have said about more than one of the scholars of interpretation such as Mujahid and more than one from the predecessors and successors. Qatada said about His statement: And they remained in their cave for three hundred years verse, this is the statement of the People of the Book, and God Almighty rejected it by saying: “Say: God knows best how long they remained.” He said: And in the reading of Abdullah, they said: And they remained, meaning that the people said it, and thus he said as Qatada said Mutraf bin Abdullah, and in what Qatada claimed there is a consideration, because what is in the hands of the People of the Book is that they remained for three hundred years, not nine, meaning the solar year, and if God had narrated their statement He would not have said: And they increased by nine, and what is apparent from the verse is only a statement from God, not a narration from them, and this is the choice of Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, and Qatada’s narration of Ibn Masoud’s reading is disconnected, then it is anomalous with respect to the reading of the majority, so it cannot be used as evidence, and God knows best. And His statement: He sees and hears means that He sees and hears them. Ibn Jarir said: This is in the sense of exaggeration in praise, as if it was said: How much He sees and hears. The interpretation of this statement is that God sees everything that exists and hears everything that is heard. Nothing of that is hidden from Him. Then it was narrated from Qatada regarding His statement: He sees and hears so no one sees or hears more than God. Ibn Zayd said: He sees and hears means He sees their deeds and hears that from them, Hearing and Seeing. And His statement: They have no protector besides Him, nor does He share in His judgment anyone means that He, the Most High, is the One to Whom belongs creation and command, the One whose judgment cannot be challenged, and He has no minister, supporter, partner, or advisor. Exalted and sanctified be He.

If the difference between every hundred lunar years and solar years is three years, then this is why He said: after three hundred and they added nine. 18:27: God the Almighty says, commanding His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to recite His Noble Book and convey it to the people, There is no changing His words, meaning there is no alterer, distorter, or remover. And His statement, And you will not find besides Him a refuge, on the authority of Mujahid, retreat, he said: a refuge. And on the authority of Qatada: a guardian or a patron. Ibn Jarir said: He is saying that if you, O Muhammad, do not recite what was revealed to you from the Book of your Lord, then you will have no refuge from God, as God the Almighty said: “O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And God will protect you from the people.” And He said: Indeed, He who imposed upon you the Qur’an will return you to a place of return, meaning He will question you about what He imposed upon you of conveying the message. And His saying: And be patient with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His countenance means sit with those who remember God, glorify Him, praise Him, extol Him, magnify Him, and ask Him morning and evening, from among the servants of God, whether they are poor or rich, strong or weak. It is said that it was revealed about the nobles of Quraysh when they asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to sit with them alone, and not to sit with them with his weak companions, such as Bilal, Ammar, Suhayb, Khabbab, and Ibn Mas`ud, and to separate those people in a separate gathering. God forbade him from that and said: And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, the verse, and He ordered him to be patient in sitting with these people, so He said: And be patient with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, the verse. Muslim said in his Sahih: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Muhammad ibn `Abdullah al-Asadi told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sa`d, who is the son of Abi Waqqas, who said: “We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, six men, and he said: The polytheists said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Drive these people out, lest they dare to attack us.” He said: “I was with Ibn Masoud, a man from Hudhayl, Bilal, and two men whose names I forgot. Then something occurred to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that which God willed to happen. He spoke to himself, and God Almighty revealed: ‘And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance.’” Muslim alone transmitted it, not al-Bukhari. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu At-Tayyah, who said: I heard Abu Al-Ja`d narrating on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to a storyteller who was telling stories, and he stopped. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Storytelling, for me to sit in the morning until the sun rises is more beloved to me than freeing four slaves. Imam Ahmad also said: Hashim told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abdul-Malik ibn Maysarah, who said: I heard Kurdus ibn Qays, who was the storyteller of the common people in Kufa, say: A man from the companions of Badr told me that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: For me to sit in a gathering like this is more beloved to me than freeing four slaves. Shu`bah said: I said: Which gathering? He said: He was a storyteller. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said in his Musnad: Muhammad told us, Yazid ibn Abaan told us, on the authority of Anas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘For me to sit with people who remember God from the dawn prayer until sunrise is more beloved to me than what the sun rises upon, and for me to remember God from the afternoon prayer until sunset is more beloved to me than freeing eight of the children of Ishmael, the blood money for each one of them being twelve thousand.’ So we calculated their blood money while we were in the assembly of Anas, and it came to ninety-six thousand. And here are those who say four of the children of Ishmael, but by God he only said eight, the blood money for each one of them being twelve thousand.” Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad bin Ishaq Al-Ahwazi told us, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, Amr bin Thabit told us, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Aqmar, on the authority of Al-Aghar Abu Muslim, who is Al-Kufi, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by a man reciting Surat Al-Kahf. When he saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he was silent. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is the gathering in which I was commanded to be patient. This is how Abu Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Thabit, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Aqmar, on the authority of Al-Aghar, without a chain of transmission. Yahya bin Al-Mualla told us on the authority of Al-Mansur, Muhammad bin Al-Salt told us, Amr bin Thabit told us on the authority of Ali bin Al-Aqmar, on the authority of Al-Aghar Abu Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah and Abu Saeed, they said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and a man was reciting Surat Al-Hajj, or Surat Al-Kahf, and he was silent. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is the gathering in which I was commanded to be patient. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Bakr told us, Maymun al-Mar’i told us, Maymun bin Siyah told us, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There is no group of people who gather to remember God, intending nothing but His face, except that a caller calls out to them from the heaven: ‘Rise, you have been forgiven, your bad deeds have been replaced with good deeds.’” Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, singled out this hadith. Al-Tabarani said: Ismail bin Al-Hasan told us, Ahmad bin Saleh told us, Ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Sahl bin Hanif, who said: The verse And be patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was reciting one of his verses. So he went out to look for them, and he found people remembering God Almighty, among them were those with disheveled hair, dry skin, and those wearing only one garment. When he saw them, he sat with them and said: Praise be to God who has placed among my nation those with whom God has commanded me to be patient. This Abd Al-Rahman was mentioned by Abu Bakr bin Abi Dawud among the Companions. As for his father, he was one of the leaders of the Companions, may God be pleased with them. And His statement, And let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring adornments of the worldly life, Ibn Abbas said: And do not go beyond them to others, meaning seek instead of them people of honor and wealth, And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, meaning he is preoccupied with the worldly life and the worship of his Lord, and whose affair is ever neglected, meaning his deeds and actions are foolishness, negligence, and loss. And do not be obedient or love his way, and do not envy him for what he is in, as He said: “And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them - the splendor of the worldly life by which We test them. And the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting.”

18:29: God the Almighty says to His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And say, O Muhammad, to the people, This that I have brought to you from your Lord is the truth about which there is no doubt or uncertainty. “So whoever wills - let him believe, and whoever wills - let him disbelieve.” This is from the category of severe threat and warning, and for this reason He said: Indeed, We have prepared meaning We have set for the wrongdoers - meaning the disbelievers in God, His Messenger, and His Book - a Fire whose walls will encompass them. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan bin Musa told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Diraj told us on the authority of Abu Al-Haitham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The walls of Hellfire will have four walls, the thickness of each wall being the distance of forty years. It was included by Al-Tirmidhi in Sifat Al-Nahar, and by Ibn Jarir in his Tafsir, on the authority of Diraj Abu Al-Samh. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: Its walls will surround them meaning: a wall of fire. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Husayn ibn Nasr and Al-Abbas ibn Muhammad told me: Abu Asim told us on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umayya, Muhammad ibn Hayy ibn Ya’la told me on the authority of Safwan ibn Ya’la, on the authority of Ya’la ibn Umayya who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The sea is Hell. He was asked: How is that? So he recited this verse, or read this verse: “A fire whose walls will surround them” then he said: By God, I will never enter it, or as long as I live, not a drop of it will touch me.” And His statement: And if they call for help, they will be helped with water like molten brass, which will scald their faces the verse. Ibn Abbas said: molten brass is thick water like the dregs of oil. Mujahid said: It is like blood and pus. Ikrimah said: It is the thing whose heat has reached its utmost. Others said: It is everything that has been melted. Qatada said: Ibn Masoud melted some gold in a trench, and when it melted and foamed, he said: This is most similar to molten metal. Ad-Dahhak said: The water of Hell is black, and it is black and its people are black. None of these statements negates the other, for molten metal combines all of these vile descriptions. It is black, stinking, thick and hot. That is why he said: It burns faces, meaning from its heat. If the disbeliever wants to drink it and brings it close to his face, it burns him until the skin of his face falls off in it. As it came in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad with his chain of transmission mentioned earlier in Sardiq al-Nar on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Water like molten metal - he said - like cloudy oil, so when he brings it near to him, the scalp of his face falls into it. And thus al-Tirmidhi narrated it in Sifat al-Nar in his Jami` from the hadith of Rashdin ibn Sa`d on the authority of `Amr ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Diraj, on his authority. Then he said: We do not know it except from the hadith of Rashdin, and he spoke about it before regarding his memory like this. He said: And Imam Ahmad narrated it as mentioned earlier on the authority of Hasan al-Ashib, on the authority of Ibn Lahi`ah, on the authority of Diraj, and God knows best. Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak and Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed said: On the authority of Safwan bin Amr, on the authority of Abdullah bin Busr, on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: And he will be given to drink from a water of purulent blood, swallowing it, he said: It will be brought near to him and he will dislike it, but when it is brought near to him, it will burn his face and the scalp will fall off, and when he drinks it, it will sever his intestines. God Almighty says: “And if they call for help, they will be given water like murky oil, which will burn their faces. What an evil drink!” Saeed bin Jubair said: When the people of Hell are hungry, they will cry out for help, and they will be helped by the tree of Zaqqum, from which they will eat, and the skin of their faces will be torn off. If a passerby were to pass by them and recognize them, he would recognize the skin of their faces in it. Then thirst will be poured upon them, and they will cry out for help, and they will be helped by water like molten metal, which is the heat of which has reached its peak. When they bring it close to their mouths, its heat will burn the flesh of their faces from which the skin has fallen off. For this reason, the Almighty said, after describing this drink with these reprehensible and ugly characteristics, How evil is this drink, meaning how evil is this drink, as He said in the other verse, And they will be given to drink scalding water, so it will rupture their intestines, and the Almighty said, They will be given to drink from a hot spring, meaning hot, as He said, And between scalding water, “And evil is it to rest,” meaning evil is the Fire as a home, a resting place, a gathering place, and a place to rest, as He said in the other verse, Indeed, evil is it as a settlement and a place to stay.
18:30: When God the Almighty mentioned the state of the wretched, He followed it with mentioning the happy ones who believed in God and believed the messengers in what they brought, and did what they were commanded to do of righteous deeds, so they will have the Gardens of Eden, and Eden means residence, Underneath them rivers flow meaning beneath their rooms and homes. Pharaoh said, And these rivers flow beneath me the verse, They will be adorned meaning with adornments, Therein are bracelets of gold and He said in another place, And pearls, and their clothing therein will be silk and He detailed it here, saying, And they will wear green garments of fine silk and heavy brocade so fine silk is fine, thin clothing like shirts and what is similar to it. As for heavy brocade, it is thick brocade and has lustre. And his saying: Reclining therein on couches. It was said that reclining means lying down, and it was said that sitting cross-legged, which is more similar to what is meant here. And from this is the authentic hadith: As for me, I do not eat reclining. There are two opinions on it: Couches is the plural of arīqa, which is the bed under the hajlā, and the hajlā as people know it in our time is called bashkhāna, and God knows best. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Qatadah, On couches, he said: They are the hajjāl. Muammar said, and others said: The beds in the hajjāl. And His saying: Excellent is the reward and excellent is the resting place. That is, Paradise is an excellent reward for their deeds and an excellent resting place, that is, it is an excellent home, resting place, and abode, just as He said about Hell: Evil is the drink and evil is the resting place. And thus He contrasted between them in Surat Al-Furqan in His saying: Indeed, it is an evil settlement and a resting place. Then He mentioned the attributes of the believers, saying: “Those will be rewarded with the Chamber for what they patiently endured, and they will be met therein with greetings and peace. They will abide therein. Excellent is the settlement and the resting place.”

18:32: God the Almighty says after mentioning the polytheists who were too arrogant to sit with the weak and poor Muslims, and who boasted to them about their wealth and lineage, so He gave them an example of two men, for one of whom God gave two gardens, i.e. two orchards of grapes, surrounded by palm trees, and surrounded on their sides and in between by crops, and each of the trees and crops was fruitful and of the utmost quality, and for this reason He said: Both gardens produced their fruit i.e. produced their fruit, and did not fail in anything thereof i.e. did not decrease anything thereof, and We caused a river to gush forth within them i.e. the rivers were scattered in them here and there, and he had fruit it was said that what is meant by it is money, narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah. It was said: the fruits, and this is more apparent here and is supported by the other reading and he had fruit with a damma on the tha’ and a sukoon on the meem, so it is the plural of thamarah like khashbah and khashab. 18:37: The Almighty says, informing him of what his believing companion answered him with, admonishing him and warning him against his disbelief in God and his delusion, Have you disbelieved in Him who created you from dust? The verse, and this is a denial and glorification of what he fell into of denial of his Lord who created him, and began the creation of man from clay, which is Adam, then made his offspring from a lineage of despised water, as the Almighty said, How can you disbelieve in God when you were dead and He gave you life? The verse, meaning how can you deny your Lord while His evidence for you is clear and obvious, everyone knows it from himself, for there is no one among the creatures except that he knows that he was nonexistent, then came into existence and his existence is not from himself nor based on any of the creatures, because he is like him, so he knew that his creation was attributed to his Creator, and He is God, there is no god but Him, the Creator of all things, and for this reason the believer said, But He is God, my Lord, meaning but I do not say what you say, rather I acknowledge God’s Oneness and Lordship, and I do not associate “By my Lord, there is no one meaning, rather, He is God, the only one to be worshipped, with no partner. Then he said: And why did you not say, when you entered your garden, ‘As God wills; there is no power except with God.’ If you see me, I am less than you in wealth and children? This is an exhortation and urging to do that, meaning why did you not, when you entered it and looked at it, praise God for what He bestowed upon you and gave you of wealth and children what He did not give to anyone else, and say, ‘As God wills; there is no power except with God.’ For this reason some of the early Muslims said: Whoever is pleased with something about his condition, wealth, or children, let him say, ‘As God wills; there is no power except with God.’ This is taken from this noble verse. A hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet was narrated in it, and it was included by Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la Al-Mawsili in his Musnad: Jarrah bin Mukhallad told us, `Umar bin Yunus told us, `Isa bin `Awn told us, `Abd Al-Malik bin Zararah told us on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God does not bestow a blessing upon a servant of his, such as family, wealth, or children, and he says, ‘As God wills, there is no power except with God,’ and he sees in him a affliction less than death.” And he used to interpret this verse: And why, when you entered your garden, did you not say, ‘As God wills, there is no power except with God?’ Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Fath Al-Azdi said: `Isa bin `Awn on the authority of `Abd Al-Malik bin Zararah on the authority of Anas, his hadith is not authentic. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah and Hajjaj told us, Shu`bah told me, on the authority of Asim ibn Ubayd God, on the authority of Ubayd, the freed slave of Abu Ruhm, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Shall I not guide you to a treasure from the treasures of Paradise? There is no power except with God. Ahmad alone transmitted it. It was proven in Sahih on the authority of Abu Musa that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Shall I not guide you to a treasure from the treasures of Paradise? There is no power and no strength except with God. Imam Ahmad said: Bakr bin Isa told us, Abu Awana told us on the authority of Abu Balj on the authority of Amr bin Maymun who said: Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: O Abu Hurairah, shall I not guide you to a treasure from the treasures of Paradise under the Throne? He said: I said: Yes, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you. He said: That you say: There is no power except with God.” Abu Balj said: “And I think that he said: For God says: My servant has submitted and surrendered.” I said to Amr: Abu Balj said: Amr said: I said to Abu Hurairah: There is no power and no strength except with God. He said: No, it is in Surat al-Kahf 18:“And why, when you entered your garden, did you not say: ‘What God wills is accomplished. There is no power except with God.’” And His statement: Perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden meaning in the Hereafter and send upon it meaning upon your garden in this world which you thought would never perish or be destroyed a punishment from the sky. Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah and Malik said on the authority of Az-Zuhri: meaning a punishment from the sky. It appears that it is a heavy, disturbing rain that uproots its crops and trees. That is why He said: So it becomes a slippery ground meaning a smooth, flat soil in which no foot can stand. Ibn Abbas said: Like a barren land that does not grow anything. And His statement: Or its water becomes sunken meaning sunken into the ground. It is the opposite of a spring that seeks the surface of the earth, as sunken seeks its bottom, as God Almighty said: Say, ‘Have you considered, if your water were to become sunken, then who could bring you flowing water?’ meaning flowing and flowing. And He said here: Or its water becomes sunken so that you would not be able to seek it. And ghur is a source meaning sunken, and it is more eloquent than it, as the poet said: His horses remain Noah, his reins are tied to him in rows Meaning mourning him.

This is an exhortation and urging to do that, meaning why did you not, when you entered it and looked at it, praise God for what He bestowed upon you and gave you of wealth and children what He did not give to anyone else, and say, ‘As God wills; there is no power except with God.’ For this reason some of the early Muslims said: Whoever is pleased with something about his condition, wealth, or children, let him say, ‘As God wills; there is no power except with God.’ This is taken from this noble verse. A hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet was narrated in it, and it was included by Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la Al-Mawsili in his Musnad: Jarrah bin Mukhallad told us, `Umar bin Yunus told us, `Isa bin `Awn told us, `Abd Al-Malik bin Zararah told us on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God does not bestow a blessing upon a servant of his, such as family, wealth, or children, and he says, ‘As God wills, there is no power except with God,’ and he sees in him a affliction less than death.” And he used to interpret this verse: And why, when you entered your garden, did you not say, ‘As God wills, there is no power except with God?’ Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Fath Al-Azdi said: `Isa bin `Awn on the authority of `Abd Al-Malik bin Zararah on the authority of Anas, his hadith is not authentic. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah and Hajjaj told us, Shu`bah told me, on the authority of Asim ibn Ubayd God, on the authority of Ubayd, the freed slave of Abu Ruhm, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Shall I not guide you to a treasure from the treasures of Paradise? There is no power except with God. Ahmad alone transmitted it. It was proven in Sahih on the authority of Abu Musa that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Shall I not guide you to a treasure from the treasures of Paradise? There is no power and no strength except with God. Imam Ahmad said: Bakr bin Isa told us, Abu Awana told us on the authority of Abu Balj on the authority of Amr bin Maymun who said: Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: O Abu Hurairah, shall I not guide you to a treasure from the treasures of Paradise under the Throne? He said: I said: Yes, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you. He said: That you say: There is no power except with God.” Abu Balj said: “And I think that he said: For God says: My servant has submitted and surrendered.” I said to Amr: Abu Balj said: Amr said: I said to Abu Hurairah: There is no power and no strength except with God. He said: No, it is in Surat al-Kahf 18:“And why, when you entered your garden, did you not say: ‘What God wills is accomplished. There is no power except with God.’” And His statement: Perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden meaning in the Hereafter and send upon it meaning upon your garden in this world which you thought would never perish or be destroyed a punishment from the sky. Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah and Malik said on the authority of Az-Zuhri: meaning a punishment from the sky. It appears that it is a heavy, disturbing rain that uproots its crops and trees. That is why He said: So it becomes a slippery ground meaning a smooth, flat soil in which no foot can stand. Ibn Abbas said: Like a barren land that does not grow anything. And His statement: Or its water becomes sunken meaning sunken into the ground. It is the opposite of a spring that seeks the surface of the earth, as sunken seeks its bottom, as God Almighty said: Say, ‘Have you considered, if your water were to become sunken, then who could bring you flowing water?’ meaning flowing and flowing. And He said here: Or its water becomes sunken so that you would not be able to seek it. And ghur is a source meaning sunken, and it is more eloquent than it, as the poet said: His horses remain Noah, his reins are tied to him in rows Meaning mourning him.
18:41: The Almighty says, informing him of what his believing companion answered him with, admonishing him and warning him against his disbelief in God and his delusion, Have you disbelieved in Him who created you from dust? The verse, and this is a denial and glorification of what he fell into of denial of his Lord who created him, and began the creation of man from clay, which is Adam, then made his offspring from a lineage of despised water, as the Almighty said, How can you disbelieve in God when you were dead and He gave you life? 18:42: God the Almighty says: And his fruits were encompassed with his money or his fruits according to the other saying, and what is meant is that what the believer was afraid of was sent to him with, which was to send the reckoning on his paradise that he was deceived by and that distracted him from God the Almighty, happened to this disbeliever. So he began to turn his hands over what he had spent in it. Qatada said: He clapped his hands regretfully and longingly for the money that he had wasted on it. "And he said, 'Oh, would that I had not associated anyone with my Lord, and that he had not had a party' meaning a clan or children, as he boasted about them and was proud. 'To aid him instead of God. And he was not victorious. There, the guardianship belongs to God the Truth.'" The reciters differed here. Some of them stopped at his saying: "And he was not victorious. There," meaning in that place where God's punishment had befallen him, so there was no one to save him from it, and they began by saying: The guardianship belongs to God the Truth. Some of them stopped at And he was not victorious, and began by saying: There, the guardianship belongs to God the Truth. Then They differed in the reading of the word Wilayat. Some of them opened the waw of Wilayat, so the meaning is that there is loyalty to God, that is, there everyone, believer or disbeliever, returns to God and to His loyalty and submission to Him when the punishment occurs, like His statement: So when they saw Our punishment, they said, ‘We believe in God alone and disbelieve in that which we used to associate with Him.’ And like His statement, reporting about Pharaoh: “Until, when drowning overtook him, he said, ‘I believe that there is no god except that in whom the Children of Israel believed, and I am of the Muslims * Now, although I disobeyed before and was of the corrupters.’” Some of them broke the waw of Wilayat, that is, there the rule is for God the Truth. Then some of them raised the truth as an attribute of the Wilayat, like His statement, the Most High: Then they will be returned to God, their True Master, the verse. For this reason, the Most High said: It is better in reward, that is, the recompense, and better in outcome, that is, the deeds that are for God the Almighty, their reward is good and their outcome is praiseworthy. Rashida is all good.
