18:45: God Almighty says: And present, O Muhammad, to the people the example of the life of this world in its transience, passing away and ending as water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it meaning the grain in it, so it grows and becomes beautiful, and flowers, light and freshness cover it, then after all this it becomes dry stubble "which the winds scatter meaning they scatter it and throw it to the right and to the left, and God is over all things competent meaning He is able to do this and that, and God often presents the example of the life of this world with this example, as God Almighty said in Surat Yunus The example of the life of this world is only as water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it - from which men and livestock eat" 10:10, and He said in al-Zumar 39:"Have you not seen that God sends down water from the sky and causes it to flow as springs in the earth, then He produces thereby crops of varying colors" 10:10, and He said in Surat al-Hadid 57:"Know that the life of this world is but play and amusement and adornment and boasting to one another and competition in wealth and children - like the rain of the sun, which is like a twilight, and the winds blow on it, and the twilight is like a twilight... The disbelievers admire its vegetation” verse, and in the authentic hadith The world is green and sweet verse, and His statement Wealth and children are the adornment of the life of this world verse, like His statement: Beautified for people is the love of desires - women, children, and heaped-up sums of gold verse, and the Almighty said: Your wealth and your children are but a trial, and God has with Him a great reward verse, meaning turning to Him and devoting yourself to His worship is better for you than being preoccupied with them, gathering for them, and being excessively compassionate towards them. For this reason, He said: But the lasting righteous deeds are better in the sight of your Lord for reward and better for hope. Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubair and more than one of the early Muslims said: The lasting good deeds are the five daily prayers. Ata bin Abi Rabah and Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The lasting good deeds are: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is Great. And thus the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman bin Affan, was asked about the lasting good deeds: What are they? He said: It is La ilaha illa God, Subhan God, Al-Hamdulillah, Allahu Akbar, and La Hawla wa La Quwwata illa Billah Al-Ali Al-Azeem. Narrated by Imam Ahmad. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri told us. Haywah told us. Abu Aqil told us that he heard al-Harith, the freed slave of Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, say: Uthman sat one day and we sat with him, and the muezzin came to him. He called for water in a vessel, I think there would be a mudd in it. He performed ablution and then said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution as I do, then he said: “Whoever performs ablution as I do, then stands up and prays the noon prayer, his sins between it and the dawn will be forgiven. Then he prays the afternoon prayer, his sins between it and the afternoon will be forgiven. Then he prays the evening prayer, his sins between it and the sunset will be forgiven. Then perhaps he will spend the night wallowing in it, then if he stands up and performs the dawn prayer, his sins between it and the evening prayer will be forgiven. These are the good deeds that remove the bad deeds.” They said: These are the good deeds, so what are the lasting good deeds, O Uthman? He said: There is no god but God, glory be to God, praise be to God, God is the greatest, and there is no power or strength except with God, the Most High, the Almighty. He is unique in this. Malik narrated on the authority of Amara ibn Abdullah ibn Sayyad on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab who said: The lasting good deeds are: Subhan God, al-Hamdulillah, la ilaha illa God, Allahu Akbar, and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah. Muhammad ibn Ajlan narrated on the authority of Amara who said: Saeed ibn al-Musayyab asked me about the lasting good deeds, so I said: Prayer and fasting. He said: You did not get it right. I said: Zakat and Hajj. He said: You did not get it right, but they are the five words: La ilaha illa God, Allahu Akbar, Subhan God, al-Hamdulillah, and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah. Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khaitham informed me on the authority of Nafi’ ibn Sarjis that he told him that he asked Ibn Umar about the lasting good deeds. He said: La ilaha illa God, Allahu Akbar, Subhan God, and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah. Ibn Jurayj said: Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah said something similar. Mujahid said: The lasting good deeds are: Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is the greatest. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of al-Hasan and Qatadah regarding his statement: And the lasting good deeds, he said: There is no god but God, and God is the greatest, and praise be to God, and glory be to God, they are the lasting good deeds. Ibn Jarir said: I found in my book on the authority of al-Hasan ibn al-Sabah al-Bazzar, on the authority of Abu Nasr al-Tammar, on the authority of Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ajlan Saeed al-Maqburi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is the greatest, they are the lasting good deeds.” He said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Amr ibn al-Harith told us that Diraj Abu al-Samh told him on the authority of Abu al-Haitham on the authority of Abu Saeed that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Increase the lasting good deeds. It was said: What are they, O Messenger of God? He said: The religion. It was said: What are they, O Messenger of God? He said: The takbir and the tahlil. And glorification, praise be to God, and there is no power or strength except with God.” And thus Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of Diraj. Ibn Wahb said: Abu Sakhr informed me that Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman, the client of Salim bin Abdullah, told him: Salim sent me to Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi on an errand, and he said: Tell him to meet me at the corner of the grave, for I have a need of you. He said: So they met and one of them greeted the other, then Salim said: What do you count as lasting good deeds? He said: There is no god but God, and God is the greatest, and glory be to God, and there is no power and no strength except with God. Salim said to him: When did you include there is no power and no strength except with God in it? He said: I have not ceased to do so. He said: So he asked him twice or three times, but he did not change his mind. He said: So remain steadfast? Salim said: Yes, remain steadfast, for Abu Ayyub Al-Ansari told me that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “I was taken up to heaven and I was shown Abraham, peace be upon him, and he said: O Gabriel, who is this with you? He said: Muhammad. He welcomed me and made me happy, then he said: Tell your nation to plant many plants in Paradise, for its soil is good and its land is spacious. I said: What are the plants in Paradise? He said: There is no power and no strength except with God.” Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Yazid narrated to us on the authority of Al-Awam, a man from the Ansar from the family of Al-Nu’man bin Bashir narrated to me, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to us while we were in the mosque after the ‘Isha’ prayer, and he raised his gaze to the sky and then lowered it until we thought that something had happened in the sky, then he said: ‘As for me, there will be rulers after me who lie and oppress. Whoever believes their lies and supports them in their oppression, is not of me and I am not of him. Whoever does not believe their lies and does not support them in their oppression, is of me and I am of him. Indeed, Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is Great, are the lasting good deeds.’” Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Abaan told us, Yahya bin Abi Katheer told us, on the authority of Zaid, on the authority of Abu Salam, on the authority of a freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Blessed, blessed are five things, how heavy they are on the scale: There is no god but God, God is greatest, glory be to God, praise be to God, and a righteous son who dies and his father accepts him as a reward.” And he said: “Blessed, blessed are five things, whoever meets God with certainty of them will enter Paradise: believing in God and the Last Day, in Paradise and Hell, in the resurrection after death, and in the reckoning.” Imam Ahmad said: Ruh told us, Al-Awza’i told us on the authority of Hassan bin Atiyah, who said: Shaddad bin Aws, may God be pleased with him, was on a journey, so he stopped at a place and said to his servant: Bring us the blade so we can play with it. I objected to him, so he said: I have not spoken a word since I became Muslim except that I have stopped and restrained it except for this word of mine, so do not keep it from me, but keep what I say to you: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “When people hoard gold and silver, then hoard these words: O God, I ask You for steadfastness in the matter and determination to do what is right, and I ask You to be grateful for Your blessings, and I ask You for the best of Your worship, and I ask You for a sound heart, and I ask You for a truthful tongue, and I ask You for the best of what You know, and I seek refuge in You from the worst of what You know, and I seek Your forgiveness for what You know, for You are the Knower of the unseen.” Then Al-Nasa’i also narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Shaddad in a similar manner. Al-Tabarani said: Abdullah bin Najiyah told us, Muhammad bin Saad Al-Awfi told us, my father told me, my uncle Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yunus bin Nafi’ Al-Jadali, on the authority of Saad bin Junadah, may God be pleased with him, who said: I was among the first of the people of Taif to come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. I left my family from the Sarawat in the morning, and came to Mina at the time of the afternoon prayer. I ascended the mountain, then I descended. I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I became Muslim. He taught me Say, ‘He is God, One’ and When the Earthquake Strikes. He taught me these words: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is Great. He said: These are the lasting good deeds. And with this chain of transmission: “Whoever gets up at night, performs ablution, rinses his mouth, then says Glory be to God one hundred times, praise be to God one hundred times, God is Great one hundred times, and there is no god but God one hundred times, his sins will be forgiven except for blood, for it is not nullified.” And Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: and the lasting good deeds, he said: It is the remembrance of God, saying: There is no god but God, God is the Greatest, Glory be to God, Praise be to God, Blessed be God, There is no power and no strength except with God, I seek forgiveness from God, and may God send blessings upon the Messenger of God, fasting, prayer, Hajj, charity, freeing slaves, jihad, kinship, and all good deeds, which are the lasting good deeds that will remain for their people in Paradise as long as the heavens and the earth remain. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is good speech. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: It is all good deeds, and Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, chose this.
18:47: The Almighty tells us about the horrors of the Day of Resurrection and the great things that will happen on it, as the Almighty said: The Day when the sky will shake with a shake, and the mountains will move with a movement meaning they will leave their places and disappear, as the Almighty said: And you will see the mountains, thinking them rigid, while they will pass like the passing of clouds and the Almighty said: And the mountains will be like carded wool and He said: "And they ask you about the mountains. Say, 'My Lord will blow them away with a blast.' He will leave them as a level plain. You will see therein neither crookedness nor unevenness" The Almighty mentions that the mountains will disappear, and the beds will be leveled, and the earth will remain as a level plain, that is, a flat surface with no crookedness or unevenness, that is, no valley or mountain. For this reason the Almighty said: And you will see the earth exposed meaning, plain and apparent, with no landmarks for anyone, and no place to hide anyone, rather all of creation will be laughing for their Lord, and nothing of them will be hidden from Him. Mujahid and Qatada said, And you will see the earth barren, with no wine or vegetation in it. Qatada said, No buildings or trees. And His statement: And We gathered them together and did not leave out a single one of them means: And We gathered them, the first of them and the last, so We did not leave out a single one of them, neither young nor old, as He said: “Say: The first and the last * Will surely be gathered together for a known time on a known day” and He said: That is a day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a witnessed day. 18:50: God Almighty says, alerting the children of Adam to the enmity of Satan towards them and their father before them, and rebuking those of them who followed him and disobeyed their Creator and Master, who created them and began them and provided for them with His kindnesses and nourished them, then after all of this he turned to Satan and opposed God, so God Almighty says: And when We said to the angels meaning to all the angels as was previously stated at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah Prostrate to Adam meaning a prostration of honor, respect and glorification, as God Almighty says: “And when your Lord said to the angels, ‘Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay from altered black mud. * So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My [created] soul, then fall down to him in prostration.” And His saying: So they prostrated, except Iblis, he was from the jinn, meaning his origin betrayed him, for he was created from a smokeless fire, and the origin of the creation of the angels is from light, as was proven in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “The angels were created from light, and Iblis was created from a smokeless fire, and Adam was created from what was described to you, so when there is a need, every vessel is filled with what is in it, and his nature betrayed him when there is a need, and that is because he had imitated the actions of the angels and imitated them and worshipped and performed asceticism, so for this reason he entered into their address and disobeyed by opposing them.” And God Almighty pointed out here that he was from the jinn, meaning that he was created from fire, as He said: “I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay.” Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Iblis was never from the angels for the blink of an eye, and he is the origin of the jinn, just as Adam, peace be upon him, is the origin of mankind. Ibn Jarir narrated it with a sound chain of transmission on his authority. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Iblis was from a tribe of angels called the Jinn, they were created from poisonous fire from among the angels, and his name was Al-Harith, and he was a treasurer of the treasurers of Paradise, and the angels were created from a light other than this tribe, he said: And the Jinn who were mentioned in the Qur’an were created from a flame of fire, which is the tongue of fire that is at its edge when it flares up. Ad-Dahhak also said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Iblis was from the most noble of the angels and the most honorable of them in tribe, and he was a treasurer of Paradise, and he had authority over the lowest heaven and authority over the earth, and among what his soul suggested to him from the decree of God was that he saw that he had honor over the people of Heaven, so because of that there occurred in his heart an arrogance that only God knows, and God extracted that arrogance from him when He commanded him to prostrate to Adam, and he was arrogant and was of the disbelievers. Ibn Abbas said: His statement: He was from the jinn means from the treasurers of Paradise, as is said of a man from Mecca, Medina, Basra, or Kufa. Ibn Jurayj said something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: He is from the treasurers of Paradise, and he managed the affairs of the lowest heaven. Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Al-A’mash on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit on the authority of Saeed. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: He was the chief angel of the lowest heaven. Ibn Ishaq said on the authority of Khallad bin Ata’ on the authority of Tawus on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Before he committed the sin, Iblis was from the angels, his name was Azazel, and he was from the inhabitants of the earth, and he was one of the most diligent of the angels and the most knowledgeable of them, so that led him to arrogance, and he was from a tribe called jinn. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Salih, the client of Al-Tawaamah and Sharik bin Abi Namir, one of them or both of them on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Among the angels is a tribe of jinn, and Iblis was from them and he used to rule what is between heaven and earth, so he disobeyed, so God became angry with him and transformed him into a cursed devil, may God curse him, transformed. He said: If a man’s sin is in arrogance, do not expect him, but if it is in disobedience, expect him. And on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: He was from the jinn who work in Paradise. Many narrations have been narrated on this from the predecessors, and most of them are from the Israelite narrations that are transmitted to be looked into, and God knows best about the condition of many of them, and among them is what may be proven false because it contradicts the truth that is in our hands, and in the Qur’an there is no need for all the other previous narrations because it is almost never free of alteration, addition, and subtraction, and many things have been placed in it, and they do not have the memorizers who are skilled in preserving it and who can deny the distortion of the extremists and the fabrications of the falsifiers, just as this nation has imams, scholars, masters, pious, righteous, and noble people from The great critics and preservers of hadith who recorded the hadith, edited it, and clarified its authenticity from its goodness from its weakness from its denial, its fabrication, its abandonment, and its lies, and they identified the fabricators, liars, and unknowns and other types of men, all of that is to protect the prophetic side and the Muhammadan status, the Seal of the Messengers and Master of Mankind, may God bless him and grant him peace, from being attributed a lie or speaking about him in a way that is not from him, so may God be pleased with them and satisfy them, and make the Gardens of Paradise their abode, and He has done so. And His saying: So he disobeyed the command of his Lord means he went out of obedience to God, for disobedience is going out. It is said: The date has disobeyed if it came out of its sleeve, and The mouse has disobeyed from its hole if it came out of it to cause corruption and mischief. Then the Almighty said, rebuking and rebuking those who followed and obeyed Him: Will you then take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me? The verse, meaning instead of Me. For this reason He said: How evil is the substitute for the wrongdoers. This situation is like His saying after mentioning the Resurrection and its terrors and the fate of each of the two groups, the happy and the miserable, in Surat Ya-Sin 36:“And separate yourselves this Day, O you criminals. Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan - for indeed, he is to you a clear enemy - and that you worship Me - this is a straight path? And he has already led astray many a mountain from you. So did you not use reason?”
18:51: The Almighty says: These whom you have taken as allies other than Me are slaves like you who do not own anything, nor did I make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor were they present at that time. The Almighty says: I am the One who is independent in creating all things, managing them and determining them alone. I have no partner, minister, advisor or peer in that, as He said: “Say: Call upon those you claim besides God. They do not possess an atom’s weight in the heavens or on the earth, and they have no share in either of them, nor does He have among them any supporter. And intercession with Him does not benefit except for one whom He permits.” The verse, and for this reason He said: And I would not have taken the misguiders as supporters. Malik said: Helpers.
18:52: The Almighty says, informing about what He will address the polytheists with on the Day of Resurrection before all witnesses, as a rebuke and rebuke to them: Call upon My partners whom you claimed meaning in this worldly life, call upon them today to save you from what you are in. The Almighty says: “And you have come to Us alone as We created you the first time, and you have left behind you what We gave you. And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed were partners among you. Indeed, the relationship between you has been severed, and what you used to claim has gone astray from you.” And His statement: So call upon them, but they did not respond to them is as He said: And it was said, ‘Call upon your partners,’ so they called upon them, but they did not respond to them verse, and He said: And who is more astray than he who calls upon those besides God who do not respond to him verses, and the Almighty says: “And they have taken besides God deities that they may be for them a source of honor. No! They will disbelieve in their worship and will be against them” verses. And His statement: And We have placed between them a place of destruction verses. Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, and more than one said: Destroying. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that Omar Al-Bakkai narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: It is a deep valley that will separate the people of guidance from the people of misguidance on the Day of Resurrection. Qatada said: Destroying. It is a valley in Hell. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Sinan al-Qazzaz told me, Abd al-Samad told us, Yazid bin Dirham told us, I heard Anas bin Malik say about the statement of God Almighty: And We have made between them a place of destruction, he said: A valley in Hell of pus and blood. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: A place of destruction is enmity. What is apparent from the context here is that it is the place of destruction, and it is possible that it is a valley in Hell or something else. The meaning is that God Almighty made clear that these polytheists have no way or access to their gods that they claimed in this world, and that He will separate them from them in the Hereafter, so there is no escape for either group to the other, but rather between them is destruction, great terror, and a major matter. If the pronoun in his statement between them refers to the believers and the disbelievers, as Abdullah bin Amr said, that He distinguishes between the people of guidance and misguidance with it, then it is like the statement of God Almighty: And the Day the Hour arises, that Day they will be divided, and He said: That Day they will be split apart, and God Almighty said: And separate yourselves today, O criminals, and God Almighty said: “And the Day We shall gather them all together, then We shall say to those who associated [others], ‘Stay where you were, you and your associates,’ and We shall be removed from among them, and their associates will say, ‘It was not us that you used to worship.’ So sufficient is God as a witness between us and you, for we were, of your worship, unaware. There every soul will experience what it put forth, and they will be returned to God, their true Master, and lost from them will be that which they used to invent.” And His statement: And the criminals will see the Fire and will think that they will fall into it, but they will find no way out from it. That is, when they saw Hell when it was brought, it was being led by seventy thousand reins, with each rein being held by seventy thousand angels. And the criminals will see the Fire they will inevitably realize that they will fall into it, so that this will be a way of hastening their worry and grief, for anticipating the punishment and fearing it before it occurs is a punishment that is certain. And His statement: And they will find no way out from it means that they will have no way to turn away from it, and they will have no choice but to go to it. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Amr ibn al-Harith told me, on the authority of Darraj, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Indeed, the disbeliever sees Hell and thinks that it will fall into it from a distance of four hundred years. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Diraj told us, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The unbeliever will be tormented for the duration of fifty thousand years, just as he did not do any deeds in this world. And the unbeliever will see Hell and think that it will befall him from a distance of forty years.”
18:53: The Almighty says, informing about what He will address the polytheists with on the Day of Resurrection before all witnesses, as a rebuke and rebuke to them: Call upon My partners whom you claimed meaning in this worldly life, call upon them today to save you from what you are in. The Almighty says: “And you have come to Us alone as We created you the first time, and you have left behind you what We gave you. And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed were partners among you. Indeed, the relationship between you has been severed, and what you used to claim has gone astray from you.” And His statement: So call upon them, but they did not respond to them is as He said: And it was said, ‘Call upon your partners,’ so they called upon them, but they did not respond to them verse, and He said: And who is more astray than he who calls upon those besides God who do not respond to him verses, and the Almighty says: “And they have taken besides God deities that they may be for them a source of honor. No! They will disbelieve in their worship and will be against them” verses. And His statement: And We have placed between them a place of destruction verses. Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, and more than one said: Destroying. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that Omar Al-Bakkai narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: It is a deep valley that will separate the people of guidance from the people of misguidance on the Day of Resurrection. Qatada said: Destroying. It is a valley in Hell. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Sinan al-Qazzaz told me, Abd al-Samad told us, Yazid bin Dirham told us, I heard Anas bin Malik say about the statement of God Almighty: And We have made between them a place of destruction, he said: A valley in Hell of pus and blood. 18:54: God the Almighty says: And We have certainly made clear to the people in this Qur’an and explained matters to them and explained them in detail so that they will not go astray from the truth and deviate from the path of guidance. Despite this clarification and this distinction, man often argues and quarrels, opposing the truth with falsehood, except for he whom God guides his sight to the path of salvation. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shu’ayb told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Ali bin Al-Hussein told me that Al-Hussein bin Ali told him that Ali bin Abi Talib told him, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him and Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, one night and said: ‘Will you not pray? ’ I said: ‘O Messenger of God, our souls are in God’s hand, so if He wills to resurrect us, He will resurrect us. ’ He turned away when I said that and did not return to me at all. Then I heard him, as he was turning away, striking his thigh and saying: ‘And man is most disputatious of anything. ’” Narrated by both of them in Sahih Al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.
18:55: God Almighty tells about the rebellion of the infidels in ancient and modern times, and their denial of the clear and apparent truth despite what they saw of clear signs and evidence, and that what prevented them from following that was their request to see the punishment that they were promised with their own eyes, as those said to their prophet: Then let down upon us fragments from the sky, if you should be of the truthful. And others said: Bring us the punishment of God, if you should be of the truthful. And the Quraysh said: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment. "And they said: O you to whom the message has been sent down, indeed you are mad. Why do you not bring us angels, if you should be of the truthful?" And other verses indicating that. Then He said, Unless the punishment of the former peoples comes to them, of covering them with the punishment and seizing them to the last one, or the punishment comes to them beforehand, meaning they see it clearly, facing and confronting it. Then the Most High said, And We do not send the messengers except as bringers of good tidings and warners, meaning before the punishment, bringing good tidings to those who believed in them and believed in them, and warnings to those who denied them and opposed them. Then He informed about the disbelievers that they disputed with falsehood to refute thereby the truth, meaning to weaken thereby the truth that the messengers brought to them, and that is not what they will achieve, and they took My signs and that with which they were warned in jest, meaning they took the arguments, proofs, and extraordinary events that the messengers were sent with and that with which they were warned and frightened of the punishment in jest, meaning they mocked them in that, which is the most severe form of denial.

18:57: God Almighty says: And which of God's servants is more unjust than he who is reminded of God's verses but turns away from them, that is, forgets them and turns away from them and does not listen to them or pay attention to them, and forgets what his hands have put forth that is, of the bad deeds and ugly actions, Indeed, We have placed over their hearts that is, the hearts of these people coverings that is, coverings and veils lest they understand it that is, lest they understand this Qur'an and this statement, and in their ears is deafness that is, a spiritual deafness to right guidance and if you call them to guidance, they will never be guided then. And His statement: And your Lord is the Forgiving, the Possessor of Mercy meaning, your Lord, O Muhammad, is the Forgiving, the Possessor of vast mercy. If He were to punish them for what they have earned, He would hasten the punishment for them just as He said: And if God were to punish people for what they have earned, He would not leave a living creature on the earth’s back and He said: “And indeed, your Lord is the Possessor of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing. And indeed, your Lord is severe in penalty” and the verses on this are many and varied. Then He informed that He is patient, conceals, and forgives, and perhaps He guides some of them from error to the right path, and whoever of them persists, there is a day for him on which the newborn will turn gray, and every pregnant woman will give birth to her pregnancy. For this reason He said: Rather, for them is an appointed time from which they will find no refuge meaning, there is no escape, no escape, and no moderation from it. And His statement: And those towns - We destroyed them when they wronged meaning the previous nations and the past centuries. We destroyed them because of their disbelief and stubbornness. And We appointed for their destruction an appointed time meaning We set it for a known period and a specific time, neither more nor less. That is, likewise you, O polytheists, beware that what befell them befalls you, for you have denied the most honorable Messenger and the greatest Prophet, and you are not more honorable to Us than they are, so fear My punishment and warning.

18:60: The reason why Moses said this to his servant, Joshua bin Nun, is that he mentioned to him that there was a servant of God at the confluence of the two seas who had knowledge that Moses did not have, so he wanted to travel to him, and he said to his servant, I will not leave, meaning I will not stop walking, until I reach the confluence of the two seas, meaning this place where the two seas converge. Al-Farazdaq said: They did not leave until their women were walking in the plain of Dhi Qara'bat al-Lata'im. Qatada and others said: They are the Persian Gulf towards the east, and the Mediterranean Sea towards the west. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: The two seas meet at Tangier, meaning in the farthest parts of the Maghreb. And God knows best. And His statement: "Or I travel ages" means even if I travel ages of time. Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: Some of the scholars of Arabic speech mentioned that a haqb in the language of Qais means a year. Then it was narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr that he said: A haqb is eighty years. Mujahid said: Seventy autumns. Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas that his statement: "Or I travel ages" means: an age. Qatada and Ibn Zayd said the same. And his saying: And when they reached the junction between them, they forgot their fish, that is because he had been ordered to carry a salted fish with him, and it was said to him: Whenever you lose the fish, it is there, so they set out until they reached the junction of the two seas, and there is a spring called the Spring of Life, so they slept there, and the whale was hit by the spray of that water, so it became agitated and it was in a basket with Joshua, peace be upon him, and it jumped from the basket into the sea, so Joshua, peace be upon him, woke up and the whale fell into the sea and it began to move in the water and the water to it was like a bridge that would not heal after it, and for this reason the Almighty said: And it took its way in the sea, a tunnel, meaning like a tunnel on the earth. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: Its trace became like a stone. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The whale did not touch anything in the sea except that it dried up until it became a rock. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Abi bin Kaab, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when he mentioned the hadith of that: No water has ever flowed since people were not on the path of the fish that was in it, so it flowed like a window until Moses returned to it and saw its path, so he said: That is what we were seeking. Qatada said: It flowed from the sea until it reached the land, then it passed through it and he did not take a path in it except that it became solid water. And his saying: And when they passed meaning the place where they forgot the fish, and the forgetfulness was attributed to them even though Joshua was the one who forgot it, like the saying of God Almighty: There emerge from them pearls and coral and it only emerges from salty water according to one of the two opinions, so when they went from the place where they forgot it by a stage, Moses said “to his servant, ‘Bring us our lunch. We have certainly encountered on this journey of ours” meaning the place where they passed exhaustion meaning fatigue. “He said, ‘Have you seen when we took refuge on the rock? I forgot the fish. And none made me forget to mention it except Satan.’” Qatadah said: Ibn Mas`ud read that I should mention it, and for this reason he said, And he took his way meaning his path “in the sea, amazingly. He said, ‘That is what we were seeking.’” meaning this is what we were seeking. So they turned back meaning they returned on their tracks meaning their path recounting meaning they were recounting the tracks of their walking and following in their footsteps. And they found a servant from among Our servants to whom We had given mercy from Us and taught him knowledge from Us. And this is it. Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, as indicated by the authentic hadiths of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Bukhari said: Al-Hamidi told us, Sufyan told us, Amr bin Dinar told us, Saeed bin Jubair told me, he said: I said to Ibn Abbas: Nawf Al-Bakali claims that Moses, the companion of Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, is not Moses, the companion of the Children of Israel. Ibn Abbas said: The enemy of God lied. Abi bin Kaab, may God be pleased with him, told us that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Moses stood up to give a sermon to the Children of Israel and was asked: Who is the most knowledgeable of people? He said: I am. So God rebuked him because he did not refer the knowledge to Him. So God revealed to him: I have a servant at the confluence of the two seas who is more knowledgeable than you. Moses said: O Lord, how can I get him? He said: Take a fish with you and put it in a basket, and wherever you lose the fish, it will be there. So he took a fish and put it in a basket, then he set out and with him set out his servant Joshua bin Nun, peace be upon him, until they reached the rock and put their heads down and slept. The fish stirred in the basket, so it came out of it and fell into the sea and made its way in the sea like a tunnel. God held back the flow of water from the fish, so it became like a vault over it. When he woke up, his companion forgot to tell him about the fish, so they set out for the rest of their day and night until the next day, Moses said to his servant: ‘Bring us our lunch. We have certainly suffered much fatigue on this journey of ours.’” Moses found the monument until he passed the place that God had commanded him to go to. His servant said to him, "Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the fish - and none made me forget to mention it except Satan - and it took its way into the sea, a wonder. He said, The fish was a school, and it was a wonder to Moses and his servant. He said, That is what we were seeking." So they returned, retracing their tracks until they reached the rock, and there was a man covered with a garment. Moses greeted him. Al-Khidr said, "And how can I be at peace in your land? He said, I am Moses. He said, Moses, the children of Israel? He said, Yes. He said, I have come to you so that you may teach me of what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said, Indeed, you will never be able to have patience with me. O Moses, I have knowledge of the knowledge of God that He has taught me which you do not know, and you have knowledge of the knowledge of God that God has taught you which I do not know. Moses said, You will find me, God willing, patient, and I will not disobey you in anything. Al-Khidr said to him, But if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I mention it to you. So they set out walking on the seashore, and a ship passed by, so they spoke to them to carry them, and they recognized Al-Khidr, so they carried them without a reason. When they boarded the ship, they were surprised to find Al-Khidr had torn off one of the ship’s planks with an axe. Moses said to him: They carried us without a reason, and you went to their ship and ripped it open to drown its people? You have certainly done a terrible thing. He said: Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? He said: Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with my affair with hardship. He said: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, said - and the first was forgetfulness from Moses. He said: A bird came and landed on the edge of the ship, and pecked in the sea once or twice, so Al-Khidr said to him: My knowledge and your knowledge compared to God’s knowledge is only like what this bird has taken from this sea. Then they got out of the ship, and while they were walking on the shore, Al-Khidr saw a boy playing with the boys, so Al-Khidr took his head and tore it off with his hand and killed him. Moses said to him, Have you killed a pure soul without a soul? You have certainly done a horrible thing. He said, Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? He said, This is more severe than the first. He said, "If I ask you about anything after this, do not accompany me. You have received an excuse from me." So they set out until, when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to offer them hospitality. They found therein a wall about to collapse." That is, leaning, so Al-Khidr held out his hand and straightened it. Moses said, "A people we came to, and they did not give us food or hospitality." If you had wished, you could have taken payment for it. He said, "This is a parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience." The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, "We wish that Moses had been patient so that God could relate to us their story." Sa`id ibn Jubayr said: Ibn Abbas used to recite, "And behind them was a king who seized Every ship was seized by force. And he was reading, As for the boy, his parents were believers. Then Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, and he mentioned something similar to it, and in it: So Moses went out with his servant Joshua ibn Nun and the fish with them, until they reached the rock, and they dismounted near it. He said: So Moses put his head down and slept. Sufyan said: And in a hadith on the authority of Umar, he said: And at the base of the rock there is a spring called Al-Hayat, and nothing touches its water except that it comes to life. So the fish touched the water of that spring, and it moved and slipped out of the container and entered the sea. So when it awoke, Moses said to his servant, Bring us our lunch. He said: And he continued the hadith, and a bird landed on the edge of the ship, and dipped its beak in the sea, so Al-Khidr said to Moses: My knowledge and your knowledge and the knowledge of creation compared to the knowledge of God is nothing but the amount that this bird dipped its beak in. And he mentioned the rest of it in a similar manner. Al-Bukhari also said: Ibrahim bin Musa told us, Hisham bin Yusuf told us that Ibn Jurayj told them, he said: Ya`la bin Muslim and `Amr bin Dinar told me on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr, one of them adding more than the other, and others I heard him narrating on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr, he said: We were with Ibn Abbas in his house when he said: Ask me, so I said: O Abu Abbas, may God make me your ransom, in Kufa there is a storyteller called Nawf who claims that he is not the Moses of the Children of Israel. As for `Amr, he said to me: The enemy of God has lied. As for Ya`la, he said to me: Ibn Abbas said: Ubayy bin Ka`b told me: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Moses, the Messenger of God, mentioned the people one day until tears filled the eyes and hearts softened, then he turned away. A man caught up with him and said: O Messenger of God, is there anyone on earth more knowledgeable than you? He said: No. So God rebuked him because he did not refer knowledge to God. It was said: Yes. He said: O Lord, and where? He said: At the confluence of the two seas. He said: O Lord, grant me knowledge by which I may know that. `Amr said to me: He said: Where the fish leaves you.” And Ya`la said to me: Take a dead whale where the soul is breathed into it. So he took a whale and put it in a basket and said to his servant: I will not charge you except that you inform me so that the whale may leave you. He said: I have not charged you a great thing. That is what he said: And when Moses said to his servant Joshua bin Nun is not with Sa`id bin Jubayr. He said: While he was in the shade of a rock in a place of threshing, the whale struck and Moses was asleep. His servant said: I will not wake him up. Then when he woke up, he forgot to tell him, and the whale struck until he entered the sea, and God stopped the flow of water from him until it was as if his mark was on a stone. He said: Amr said to me: This is how it is as if his mark was on a stone, and he circled between his thumbs and the ones next to them. He said: Indeed, we have suffered fatigue in this journey of ours. He said: And God has cut off fatigue from you. This is not with Sa`id bin Jubayr. He told him. So they returned and found green. He said: Uthman bin Abi Sulayman said: On a green rug in the middle of the sea. Sa`id bin Jubayr said: Covered with a garment that had been made. One end was under his feet and the other was at his head. Moses greeted him and he uncovered his face and said: Is there peace in my land? Who are you? He said: I am Moses. He said: Moses of the Children of Israel? He said: Yes. He said: What is the matter with you? He said: I have come to you so that you may teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said: Is it not enough for you that the Torah is in your hands and that revelation comes to you, O Moses? I have knowledge that you should not know, and you have knowledge that I should not know. Then a bird took hold of the sea with its beak and said: By God, my knowledge and your knowledge are not comparable to the knowledge of God except as this bird took hold of the sea with its beak. When they boarded the ship, they found small passages carrying the people of this coast to this other coast. They recognized him and said: Abdullah Al-Salih. He said: So we said to Saeed bin Jubair Al-Khidr. He said: Yes, we will not carry him for a fee. So he tore it open and stuck a peg in it. Moses said: You tore it open to drown its people. You have certainly done a terrible thing. Mujahid said: It was strange. He said: Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? The first was forgetfulness, the second was a condition, and the third was deliberate. He said: Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with my task with difficulty. So they set out until they met a boy and killed him. Ya’la said: Saeed said: He found some boys playing, so he took a charming, unbelieving boy, laid him down, and slaughtered him with a knife. He said, Have you killed a pure soul who did not commit perjury? Ibn Abbas read it as Zakiya Muslima, as you would say, a pure young man. So they set out and found a wall about to collapse, so he straightened it. Saeed said: With his hand like this, and he pushed it with his hand and it straightened. He said: If you wished, you could have taken a wage for it. Ya’la said: I thought that Saeed said: So he wiped it with his hand and it straightened. He said: If you wished, you could have taken a wage for it. Saeed said: A wage that we could eat. And behind them was a king, and in front of them. Ibn Abbas read it: In front of them is a king, they claim, from someone other than Saeed, that he was Hadad bin Baddad, and the name of the murdered young man, they claim, was Jaysur, a king who took every ship by force. So I wanted, when it passed by him, for him to leave it with its defect, and when they passed, they repaired it and benefited from it. Some of them say, they sealed it with a bottle, and some of them say, with tar. His parents were believers, and he was a disbeliever, so we feared that he would overburden them with transgression and disbelief, that his love for him would lead them to follow him in his religion. So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him in purity, like His saying: Did you kill a pure soul? And His saying: And nearer of kinship. They are more merciful to him than they were to the first one who killed Khidr. And others besides Sa`id ibn Jubayr claimed that they substituted a slave girl. As for Dawud ibn Abi `Asim, he said on the authority of more than one: It is a slave girl. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Moses, peace be upon him, addressed the Children of Israel and said: No one knows God and His command better than me. So he was ordered to meet this man and he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above with additions and omissions, and God knows best. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Amara on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Utaybah on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair who said: I sat with Ibn Abbas and with him were a group of the People of the Book. Some of them said: O Abu Al-Abbas, Nawf, the son of Kaab’s wife, claims on the authority of Kaab that Moses, the prophet who sought knowledge, is in fact Moses bin Misha. Saeed said: Ibn Abbas said: Does Nawf say this, O Saeed? I said to him: Yes, I heard Nawf say that. He said: Did you hear him, O Saeed? He said: Yes. He said: Nawf lied. Then Ibn Abbas said: My father bin Kaab told me on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that Moses, the son of Israel, asked his Lord, saying: O Lord, if there is one among your servants who is more knowledgeable than me, then guide me to him. He said to him: Yes, among my servants is one who is more knowledgeable than you. Then he described his place to him and gave him permission to meet him. So Moses went out with his young man and with him was a beautiful fish. It was said to him: If this fish revives in a place, then your companion is there and you have fulfilled your need. So Moses went out with his young man and with him was that fish carrying him. He walked until he was exhausted and reached the rock and that water. That water is the water of life. Whoever drinks from it will be immortal and nothing dead will compare to it except that it will be revived. So when they came down and the fish touched the water, it revived and took its path in the sea, a tunnel. So they set off. When they had passed the crossroads, Moses said to his young man: Bring us our lunch. We have indeed encountered fatigue on this journey of ours. The young man said and mentioned: Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the fish and nothing made me forget to mention it except Satan. And he took his way in the sea in a strange way. Ibn Abbas said: So Moses appeared on the rock until they reached it, and there was a man wrapped in his cloak. Moses greeted him and he returned his greeting, then he said to him: What brought you if you have a job among your people? Moses said to him: I have come to you to teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said: You will not be able to have patience with me. And he was a man who knew the knowledge of the unseen, and he knew that. Moses said: Yes. He said: And how can you be patient about that of which you have no knowledge? That is, you only know the outward appearance of what you see of justice, and you have not known the unseen as much as I know. “He said: ‘You will find me, if God wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter. ’” And if you see something that contradicts me, he said: Then if you follow me, do not ask me about anything. And if you deny it, until I mention it to you. So they set out walking on the shore of the sea, circling people and seeking someone to carry them, until a new, secure ship passed by them, the kindest, most beautiful, and most secure of which no ship had ever passed by. He asked its people to carry them, so they carried them. When they were secure in it and it entered with its people, he took out his beak and a hammer, then he went to a corner and struck it with the beak until he tore it open. Then he took a board and closed it over it, then he sat on it to patch it up. So Moses said to him and saw something more horrific than that: “You have torn it open to drown its people. You have certainly done a terrible thing. He said: “Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me?” He said: Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot. That is, for what He left from your covenant And do not burden me with my affair with hardship. Then they got out of the ship, and set out until they came to the people of a town, and behold, boys were playing behind it, among them was a boy who was not more charming than any of the boys, nor richer nor more radiant than him, so he took him in his hand and took a stone and struck his head with it until he crushed it and killed him. He said: Moses saw a terrible thing that he could not bear, a young boy he killed for no reason, he said: Have you killed a pure soul meaning a young one for no reason? You have certainly done a horrible thing. He said: Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? He said: If I ask you about anything after this, do not accompany me. You have received from Me an excuse." Meaning, you have excused yourself regarding my affair. "So they set out until they came to the people of a town, and they asked its people for food, but they refused to host them. They found in it a wall about to collapse. So he demolished it and sat down to build it. Moses was annoyed by what he saw him doing of the obligation and what he could not bear, so he erected it. He said: "If you wished He said: “This is a parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience. As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working at sea. I intended to fault it, and behind them was a king who seized every ship by force.” In Ibn Ka’b’s reading, every ship by force. I only faulted it to prevent him from it, but it was safe from him when he saw the fault that I had made with it. “As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them through transgression and disbelief. So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him, purer in purity and nearer in kinship.” “And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them. Their father had been a righteous man. So your Lord intended that they should reach maturity and extract their treasure as a mercy from your Lord. And I did not do it of my own accord.” That is, I did it of my own accord. That is the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience. Ibn Abbas used to say: The treasure was nothing but knowledge. Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas that they said: When Moses and his people prevailed over Egypt, he settled his people in Egypt. When they settled in the house, God revealed to them that He would remind them of the days of God. So he addressed his people and mentioned what God had given them of goodness and blessings, and he mentioned to them when God saved them from the people of Pharaoh, and he mentioned to them the destruction of their enemy and that God had made them successors on the earth. He said: God spoke to your Prophet directly and chose me for Himself, and sent down upon me love from Him, and God has given you of all that you asked of Him. So your Prophet is the best of the people of the earth, and you read the Torah. So he did not leave a blessing that God had bestowed upon them without making it known to them. A man from the Children of Israel said to him: They are like that, O Prophet. God has made known to us what you are saying: Is there anyone on earth more knowledgeable than you, O Prophet of God? He said: No. Then God sent Gabriel to Moses, peace be upon him, and said: God says: How do you know where I will place my knowledge? Yes, I have on the seashore a man who is more knowledgeable than you. Ibn Abbas said: He is Al-Khidr. Moses asked his Lord to show him to him, and He revealed to him: Go to the sea, and you will find a whale on the seashore, so take it and give it to your servant, then stick to the seashore, and if you forget the whale and it perishes from you, then you will find the righteous servant you are looking for. When the journey of Moses, the Prophet of God, became long and he was tired, he asked his servant about the fish. His servant, who was his young man, said to him, Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the fish, and none made me forget to mention it except Satan. The young man said, I saw the fish when it took its way in the sea, forming a school, and I was amazed by that. So Moses returned until he came to the rock and found the fish. The fish began to strike the sea and Moses followed it. Moses advanced his staff, clearing the water from it, following the fish. The fish did not touch anything in the sea except that the water dried up from it until it became a rock. The Prophet of God was amazed by that until the fish reached an island in the sea and met Al-Khidr there. He greeted him and Al-Khidr said, “And upon you be peace. How can there be peace on this land? And who are you?” He said, I am Moses. Al-Khidr said, The companion of the Children of Israel? He said, Yes. So he welcomed him and said, What brought you? He said, I have come to you so that you may teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said, Indeed, you will never be able to have patience with me. He said, You will find me, God willing, patient, and I will not disobey you in anything. He said, So he went with him and said to him, ‘Do not ask me about anything I do until I explain its nature.’ That is what he said, ‘until I make mention of it to you.’ Al-Zuhri said on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Mas`ud on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he and Al-Har ibn Qays ibn Hisn Al-Fazari had a dispute about the companion of Moses. Ibn Abbas said: He is Al-Khidr. Then Abi ibn Ka`b passed by them and Ibn Abbas called him and said: My companion and I have a dispute about the companion of Moses who asked for the way to meet him. Have you heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mention his affair? He said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “While Moses was in a gathering of the Children of Israel, a man came to him and said: Do you know the location of a man who is more knowledgeable than you? He said: No. So God revealed to Moses: Yes, our servant Khidr. Moses asked how to meet him, so God made the whale a sign for him, and it was said to him: If you miss the whale, go back, for you will meet him. So Moses followed the traces of the whale in the sea, and Moses’ servant said to Moses: Did you see when we took refuge on the rock, for I forgot the whale? Moses said: That is what we were seeking. So they returned, following their traces, and found our servant Khidr, and what happened to them was what God has narrated in His Book.”
18:61: The reason why Moses said this to his servant, Joshua bin Nun, is that he mentioned to him that there was a servant of God at the confluence of the two seas who had knowledge that Moses did not have, so he wanted to travel to him, and he said to his servant, I will not leave, meaning I will not stop walking, until I reach the confluence of the two seas, meaning this place where the two seas converge. Al-Farazdaq said: They did not leave until their women were walking in the plain of Dhi Qara'bat al-Lata'im. Qatada and others said: They are the Persian Gulf towards the east, and the Mediterranean Sea towards the west. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: The two seas meet at Tangier, meaning in the farthest parts of the Maghreb. And God knows best. And His statement: Or I travel ages means even if I travel ages of time. Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: Some of the scholars of Arabic speech mentioned that a haqb in the language of Qais means a year. Then it was narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr that he said: A haqb is eighty years. Mujahid said: Seventy autumns. Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas that his statement: Or I travel ages means: an age. Qatada and Ibn Zayd said the same. And his saying: And when they reached the junction between them, they forgot their fish, that is because he had been ordered to carry a salted fish with him, and it was said to him: Whenever you lose the fish, it is there, so they set out until they reached the junction of the two seas, and there is a spring called the Spring of Life, so they slept there, and the whale was hit by the spray of that water, so it became agitated and it was in a basket with Joshua, peace be upon him, and it jumped from the basket into the sea, so Joshua, peace be upon him, woke up and the whale fell into the sea and it began to move in the water and the water to it was like a bridge that would not heal after it, and for this reason the Almighty said: And it took its way in the sea, a tunnel, meaning like a tunnel on the earth. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: Its trace became like a stone. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The whale did not touch anything in the sea except that it dried up until it became a rock. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Abi bin Kaab, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when he mentioned the hadith of that: No water has ever flowed since people were not on the path of the fish that was in it, so it flowed like a window until Moses returned to it and saw its path, so he said: That is what we were seeking. Qatada said: It flowed from the sea until it reached the land, then it passed through it and he did not take a path in it except that it became solid water. And his saying: And when they passed meaning the place where they forgot the fish, and the forgetfulness was attributed to them even though Joshua was the one who forgot it, like the saying of God Almighty: There emerge from them pearls and coral and it only emerges from salty water according to one of the two opinions, so when they went from the place where they forgot it by a stage, Moses said “to his servant, ‘Bring us our lunch. We have certainly encountered on this journey of ours” meaning the place where they passed exhaustion meaning fatigue. “He said, ‘Have you seen when we took refuge on the rock? I forgot the fish. And none made me forget to mention it except Satan.’” Qatadah said: Ibn Mas`ud read that I should mention it, and for this reason he said, And he took his way meaning his path “in the sea, amazingly. He said, ‘That is what we were seeking.’” meaning this is what we were seeking. So they turned back meaning they returned on their tracks meaning their path recounting meaning they were recounting the tracks of their walking and following in their footsteps. And they found a servant from among Our servants to whom We had given mercy from Us and taught him knowledge from Us. And this is it. Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, as indicated by the authentic hadiths of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Bukhari said: Al-Hamidi told us, Sufyan told us, Amr bin Dinar told us, Saeed bin Jubair told me, he said: I said to Ibn Abbas: Nawf Al-Bakali claims that Moses, the companion of Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, is not Moses, the companion of the Children of Israel. Ibn Abbas said: The enemy of God lied. Abi bin Kaab, may God be pleased with him, told us that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Moses stood up to give a sermon to the Children of Israel and was asked: Who is the most knowledgeable of people? He said: I am. So God rebuked him because he did not refer the knowledge to Him. So God revealed to him: I have a servant at the confluence of the two seas who is more knowledgeable than you. Moses said: O Lord, how can I get him? He said: Take a fish with you and put it in a basket, and wherever you lose the fish, it will be there. So he took a fish and put it in a basket, then he set out and with him set out his servant Joshua bin Nun, peace be upon him, until they reached the rock and put their heads down and slept. The fish stirred in the basket, so it came out of it and fell into the sea and made its way in the sea like a tunnel. God held back the flow of water from the fish, so it became like a vault over it. When he woke up, his companion forgot to tell him about the fish, so they set out for the rest of their day and night until the next day, Moses said to his servant: ‘Bring us our lunch. We have certainly suffered much fatigue on this journey of ours.’” Moses found the monument until he passed the place that God had commanded him to go to. His servant said to him, Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the fish - and none made me forget to mention it except Satan - and it took its way into the sea, a wonder. He said, The fish was a school, and it was a wonder to Moses and his servant. He said, That is what we were seeking. So they returned, retracing their tracks until they reached the rock, and there was a man covered with a garment. Moses greeted him. Al-Khidr said, "And how can I be at peace in your land?" He said, I am Moses. He said, Moses, the children of Israel? He said, Yes. He said, I have come to you so that you may teach me of what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said, Indeed, you will never be able to have patience with me. O Moses, I have knowledge of the knowledge of God that He has taught me which you do not know, and you have knowledge of the knowledge of God that God has taught you which I do not know. Moses said, You will find me, God willing, patient, and I will not disobey you in anything. Al-Khidr said to him, But if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I mention it to you." So they set out walking on the seashore, and a ship passed by, so they spoke to them to carry them, and they recognized Al-Khidr, so they carried them without a reason. When they boarded the ship, they were surprised to find Al-Khidr had torn off one of the ship’s planks with an axe. Moses said to him: They carried us without a reason, and you went to their ship and ripped it open to drown its people? You have certainly done a terrible thing. He said: Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? He said: Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with my affair with hardship. He said: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, said - and the first was forgetfulness from Moses. He said: A bird came and landed on the edge of the ship, and pecked in the sea once or twice, so Al-Khidr said to him: My knowledge and your knowledge compared to God’s knowledge is only like what this bird has taken from this sea. Then they got out of the ship, and while they were walking on the shore, Al-Khidr saw a boy playing with the boys, so Al-Khidr took his head and tore it off with his hand and killed him. Moses said to him, "Have you killed a pure soul without a soul? You have certainly done a horrible thing. He said, Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? He said, This is more severe than the first. He said, If I ask you about anything after this, do not accompany me. You have received an excuse from me." So they set out until, when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to offer them hospitality. They found therein a wall about to collapse."
