He said to him: Yes, among my servants is one who is more knowledgeable than you. Then he described his place to him and gave him permission to meet him. So Moses went out with his young man and with him was a beautiful fish. It was said to him: If this fish revives in a place, then your companion is there and you have fulfilled your need. So Moses went out with his young man and with him was that fish carrying him. He walked until he was exhausted and reached the rock and that water. That water is the water of life. Whoever drinks from it will be immortal and nothing dead will compare to it except that it will be revived. So when they came down and the fish touched the water, it revived and took its path in the sea, a tunnel. So they set off. When they had passed the crossroads, Moses said to his young man: Bring us our lunch. We have indeed encountered fatigue on this journey of ours. The young man said and mentioned: Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the fish and nothing made me forget to mention it except Satan. And he took his way in the sea in a strange way. Ibn Abbas said: So Moses appeared on the rock until they reached it, and there was a man wrapped in his cloak. Moses greeted him and he returned his greeting, then he said to him: What brought you if you have a job among your people? Moses said to him: I have come to you to teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said: You will not be able to have patience with me. And he was a man who knew the knowledge of the unseen, and he knew that. Moses said: Yes. He said: And how can you be patient about that of which you have no knowledge? That is, you only know the outward appearance of what you see of justice, and you have not known the unseen as much as I know. “He said: ‘You will find me, if God wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter. ’” And if you see something that contradicts me, he said: Then if you follow me, do not ask me about anything. And if you deny it, until I mention it to you. So they set out walking on the shore of the sea, circling people and seeking someone to carry them, until a new, secure ship passed by them, the kindest, most beautiful, and most secure of which no ship had ever passed by. He asked its people to carry them, so they carried them. When they were secure in it and it entered with its people, he took out his beak and a hammer, then he went to a corner and struck it with the beak until he tore it open. Then he took a board and closed it over it, then he sat on it to patch it up. So Moses said to him and saw something more horrific than that: “You have torn it open to drown its people. You have certainly done a terrible thing. He said: “Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me?” He said: Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot. That is, for what He left from your covenant "And do not burden me with my affair with hardship." Then they got out of the ship, and set out until they came to the people of a town, and behold, boys were playing behind it, among them was a boy who was not more charming than any of the boys, nor richer nor more radiant than him, so he took him in his hand and took a stone and struck his head with it until he crushed it and killed him. He said: Moses saw a terrible thing that he could not bear, a young boy he killed for no reason, he said: "Have you killed a pure soul meaning a young one for no reason? You have certainly done a horrible thing." He said: Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? He said: If I ask you about anything after this, do not accompany me. You have received from Me an excuse." Meaning, you have excused yourself regarding my affair. "So they set out until they came to the people of a town, and they asked its people for food, but they refused to host them. They found in it a wall about to collapse. So he demolished it and sat down to build it. Moses was annoyed by what he saw him doing of the obligation and what he could not bear, so he erected it. He said: "If you wished He said: “This is a parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience. As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working at sea. I intended to fault it, and behind them was a king who seized every ship by force.” In Ibn Ka’b’s reading, every ship by force. I only faulted it to prevent him from it, but it was safe from him when he saw the fault that I had made with it. “As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them through transgression and disbelief. So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him, purer in purity and nearer in kinship.” “And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them. Their father had been a righteous man. So your Lord intended that they should reach maturity and extract their treasure as a mercy from your Lord. And I did not do it of my own accord.” That is, I did it of my own accord. That is the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience. Ibn Abbas used to say: The treasure was nothing but knowledge. Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas that they said: When Moses and his people prevailed over Egypt, he settled his people in Egypt. When they settled in the house, God revealed to them that He would remind them of the days of God. So he addressed his people and mentioned what God had given them of goodness and blessings, and he mentioned to them when God saved them from the people of Pharaoh, and he mentioned to them the destruction of their enemy and that God had made them successors on the earth. He said: God spoke to your Prophet directly and chose me for Himself, and sent down upon me love from Him, and God has given you of all that you asked of Him. So your Prophet is the best of the people of the earth, and you read the Torah. So he did not leave a blessing that God had bestowed upon them without making it known to them. A man from the Children of Israel said to him: They are like that, O Prophet. God has made known to us what you are saying: Is there anyone on earth more knowledgeable than you, O Prophet of God? He said: No. Then God sent Gabriel to Moses, peace be upon him, and said: God says: How do you know where I will place my knowledge? Yes, I have on the seashore a man who is more knowledgeable than you. Ibn Abbas said: He is Al-Khidr. Moses asked his Lord to show him to him, and He revealed to him: Go to the sea, and you will find a whale on the seashore, so take it and give it to your servant, then stick to the seashore, and if you forget the whale and it perishes from you, then you will find the righteous servant you are looking for. When the journey of Moses, the Prophet of God, became long and he was tired, he asked his servant about the fish. His servant, who was his young man, said to him, Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the fish, and none made me forget to mention it except Satan. The young man said, I saw the fish when it took its way in the sea, forming a school, and I was amazed by that. So Moses returned until he came to the rock and found the fish. The fish began to strike the sea and Moses followed it. Moses advanced his staff, clearing the water from it, following the fish. The fish did not touch anything in the sea except that the water dried up from it until it became a rock. The Prophet of God was amazed by that until the fish reached an island in the sea and met Al-Khidr there. He greeted him and Al-Khidr said, “And upon you be peace. How can there be peace on this land? And who are you?” He said, I am Moses. Al-Khidr said, The companion of the Children of Israel? He said, Yes. So he welcomed him and said, What brought you? He said, I have come to you so that you may teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said, Indeed, you will never be able to have patience with me. He said, You will find me, God willing, patient, and I will not disobey you in anything. He said, So he went with him and said to him, ‘Do not ask me about anything I do until I explain its nature.’ That is what he said, ‘until I make mention of it to you.’ Al-Zuhri said on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Mas`ud on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he and Al-Har ibn Qays ibn Hisn Al-Fazari had a dispute about the companion of Moses. Ibn Abbas said: He is Al-Khidr. Then Abi ibn Ka`b passed by them and Ibn Abbas called him and said: My companion and I have a dispute about the companion of Moses who asked for the way to meet him. Have you heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mention his affair? He said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “While Moses was in a gathering of the Children of Israel, a man came to him and said: Do you know the location of a man who is more knowledgeable than you? He said: No. So God revealed to Moses: Yes, our servant Khidr. Moses asked how to meet him, so God made the whale a sign for him, and it was said to him: If you miss the whale, go back, for you will meet him. So Moses followed the traces of the whale in the sea, and Moses’ servant said to Moses: Did you see when we took refuge on the rock, for I forgot the whale? Moses said: That is what we were seeking. So they returned, following their traces, and found our servant Khidr, and what happened to them was what God has narrated in His Book.”
18:62: The reason why Moses said this to his servant, Joshua bin Nun, is that he mentioned to him that there was a servant of God at the confluence of the two seas who had knowledge that Moses did not have, so he wanted to travel to him, and he said to his servant, I will not leave, meaning I will not stop walking, until I reach the confluence of the two seas, meaning this place where the two seas converge. Al-Farazdaq said: They did not leave until their women were walking in the plain of Dhi Qara'bat al-Lata'im. Qatada and others said: They are the Persian Gulf towards the east, and the Mediterranean Sea towards the west. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: The two seas meet at Tangier, meaning in the farthest parts of the Maghreb. And God knows best. And His statement: Or I travel ages means even if I travel ages of time. Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: Some of the scholars of Arabic speech mentioned that a haqb in the language of Qais means a year. Then it was narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr that he said: A haqb is eighty years. Mujahid said: Seventy autumns. Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas that his statement: Or I travel ages means: an age. Qatada and Ibn Zayd said the same. And his saying: And when they reached the junction between them, they forgot their fish, that is because he had been ordered to carry a salted fish with him, and it was said to him: Whenever you lose the fish, it is there, so they set out until they reached the junction of the two seas, and there is a spring called the Spring of Life, so they slept there, and the whale was hit by the spray of that water, so it became agitated and it was in a basket with Joshua, peace be upon him, and it jumped from the basket into the sea, so Joshua, peace be upon him, woke up and the whale fell into the sea and it began to move in the water and the water to it was like a bridge that would not heal after it, and for this reason the Almighty said: And it took its way in the sea, a tunnel, meaning like a tunnel on the earth. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: Its trace became like a stone. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The whale did not touch anything in the sea except that it dried up until it became a rock. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Abi bin Kaab, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when he mentioned the hadith of that: No water has ever flowed since people were not on the path of the fish that was in it, so it flowed like a window until Moses returned to it and saw its path, so he said: That is what we were seeking. Qatada said: It flowed from the sea until it reached the land, then it passed through it and he did not take a path in it except that it became solid water. And his saying: And when they passed meaning the place where they forgot the fish, and the forgetfulness was attributed to them even though Joshua was the one who forgot it, like the saying of God Almighty: There emerge from them pearls and coral and it only emerges from salty water according to one of the two opinions, so when they went from the place where they forgot it by a stage, Moses said “to his servant, ‘Bring us our lunch. We have certainly encountered on this journey of ours” meaning the place where they passed exhaustion meaning fatigue. “He said, ‘Have you seen when we took refuge on the rock? I forgot the fish. And none made me forget to mention it except Satan.’” Qatadah said: Ibn Mas`ud read that I should mention it, and for this reason he said, And he took his way meaning his path “in the sea, amazingly. He said, ‘That is what we were seeking.’” meaning this is what we were seeking. So they turned back meaning they returned on their tracks meaning their path recounting meaning they were recounting the tracks of their walking and following in their footsteps. And they found a servant from among Our servants to whom We had given mercy from Us and taught him knowledge from Us. And this is it. Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, as indicated by the authentic hadiths of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Bukhari said: Al-Hamidi told us, Sufyan told us, Amr bin Dinar told us, Saeed bin Jubair told me, he said: I said to Ibn Abbas: Nawf Al-Bakali claims that Moses, the companion of Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, is not Moses, the companion of the Children of Israel. Ibn Abbas said: The enemy of God lied. Abi bin Kaab, may God be pleased with him, told us that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Moses stood up to give a sermon to the Children of Israel and was asked: Who is the most knowledgeable of people? He said: I am. So God rebuked him because he did not refer the knowledge to Him. So God revealed to him: I have a servant at the confluence of the two seas who is more knowledgeable than you. Moses said: O Lord, how can I get him? He said: Take a fish with you and put it in a basket, and wherever you lose the fish, it will be there. So he took a fish and put it in a basket, then he set out and with him set out his servant Joshua bin Nun, peace be upon him, until they reached the rock and put their heads down and slept. The fish stirred in the basket, so it came out of it and fell into the sea and made its way in the sea like a tunnel. God held back the flow of water from the fish, so it became like a vault over it. When he woke up, his companion forgot to tell him about the fish, so they set out for the rest of their day and night until the next day, Moses said to his servant: ‘Bring us our lunch. We have certainly suffered much fatigue on this journey of ours.’” Moses found the monument until he passed the place that God had commanded him to go to. His servant said to him, Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the fish - and none made me forget to mention it except Satan - and it took its way into the sea, a wonder. He said, The fish was a school, and it was a wonder to Moses and his servant. He said, That is what we were seeking. So they returned, retracing their tracks until they reached the rock, and there was a man covered with a garment. Moses greeted him. Al-Khidr said, "And how can I be at peace in your land?" He said, I am Moses. He said, Moses, the children of Israel? He said, Yes. He said, I have come to you so that you may teach me of what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said, Indeed, you will never be able to have patience with me. O Moses, I have knowledge of the knowledge of God that He has taught me which you do not know, and you have knowledge of the knowledge of God that God has taught you which I do not know. Moses said, You will find me, God willing, patient, and I will not disobey you in anything. Al-Khidr said to him, But if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I mention it to you." So they set out walking on the seashore, and a ship passed by, so they spoke to them to carry them, and they recognized Al-Khidr, so they carried them without a plank. When they boarded the ship, they were surprised to find Al-Khidr had torn off one of the ship’s planks with an axe. Moses said to him: They carried us without a plank, and you went to their ship and ripped it open to drown its people? You have certainly done a terrible thing. He said: Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? He said: Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with my affair with hardship. He said: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, said - and the first was forgetfulness from Moses. He said: A bird came and landed on the edge of the ship, and pecked in the sea once or twice, so Al-Khidr said to him: My knowledge and your knowledge compared to God’s knowledge is only like what this bird has taken from this sea. Then they got out of the ship, and while they were walking on the shore, Al-Khidr saw a boy playing with the boys, so Al-Khidr took his head and tore it off with his hand and killed him. Moses said to him, "Have you killed a pure soul without a soul? You have certainly done a horrible thing. He said, Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? He said, This is more severe than the first. He said, If I ask you about anything after this, do not accompany me. You have received an excuse from me." So they set out until, when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to offer them hospitality. They found therein a wall about to collapse." That is, leaning, so Al-Khidr held out his hand and straightened it. Moses said, A people we came to, and they did not give us food or hospitality. If you had wished, you could have taken payment for it. He said, "This is a parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience." The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, We wish that Moses had been patient so that God could relate to us their story. Sa`id ibn Jubayr said: Ibn Abbas used to recite, "And behind them was a king who seized Every ship was seized by force. And he was reading, As for the boy, his parents were believers. Then Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, and he mentioned something similar to it, and in it: So Moses went out with his servant Joshua ibn Nun and the fish with them, until they reached the rock, and they dismounted near it. He said: So Moses put his head down and slept. Sufyan said: And in a hadith on the authority of Umar, he said: And at the base of the rock there is a spring called Al-Hayat, and nothing touches its water except that it comes to life. So the fish touched the water of that spring, and it moved and slipped out of the container and entered the sea. So when it awoke, Moses said to his servant, Bring us our lunch. He said: And he continued the hadith, and a bird landed on the edge of the ship, and dipped its beak in the sea, so Al-Khidr said to Moses: My knowledge and your knowledge and the knowledge of creation compared to the knowledge of God is nothing but the amount that this bird dipped its beak in. And he mentioned the rest of it in a similar manner. Al-Bukhari also said: Ibrahim bin Musa told us, Hisham bin Yusuf told us that Ibn Jurayj told them, he said: Ya`la bin Muslim and `Amr bin Dinar told me on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr, one of them adding more than the other, and others I heard him narrating on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr, he said: We were with Ibn Abbas in his house when he said: Ask me, so I said: O Abu Abbas, may God make me your ransom, in Kufa there is a storyteller called Nawf who claims that he is not the Moses of the Children of Israel. As for `Amr, he said to me: The enemy of God has lied. As for Ya`la, he said to me: Ibn Abbas said: Ubayy bin Ka`b told me: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Moses, the Messenger of God, mentioned the people one day until tears filled the eyes and hearts softened, then he turned away. A man caught up with him and said: O Messenger of God, is there anyone on earth more knowledgeable than you? He said: No. So God rebuked him because he did not refer knowledge to God. It was said: Yes. He said: O Lord, and where? He said: At the confluence of the two seas. He said: O Lord, grant me knowledge by which I may know that. `Amr said to me: He said: Where the fish leaves you.” And Ya`la said to me: Take a dead whale where the soul is breathed into it. So he took a whale and put it in a basket and said to his servant: I will not charge you except that you inform me so that the whale may leave you. He said: I have not charged you a great thing. That is what he said: And when Moses said to his servant Joshua bin Nun is not with Sa`id bin Jubayr. He said: While he was in the shade of a rock in a place of threshing, the whale struck and Moses was asleep. His servant said: I will not wake him up. Then when he woke up, he forgot to tell him, and the whale struck until he entered the sea, and God stopped the flow of water from him until it was as if his mark was on a stone. He said: Amr said to me: This is how it is as if his mark was on a stone, and he circled between his thumbs and the ones next to them. He said: Indeed, we have suffered fatigue in this journey of ours. He said: And God has cut off fatigue from you. This is not with Sa`id bin Jubayr. He told him. So they returned and found green. He said: Uthman bin Abi Sulayman said: On a green rug in the middle of the sea. Sa`id bin Jubayr said: Covered with a garment that had been made. One end was under his feet and the other was at his head. Moses greeted him and he uncovered his face and said: Is there peace in my land? Who are you? He said: I am Moses. He said: Moses of the Children of Israel? He said: Yes. He said: What is the matter with you? He said: I have come to you so that you may teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said: Is it not enough for you that the Torah is in your hands and that revelation comes to you, O Moses? I have knowledge that you should not know, and you have knowledge that I should not know. Then a bird took hold of the sea with its beak and said: By God, my knowledge and your knowledge are not comparable to the knowledge of God except as this bird took hold of the sea with its beak. When they boarded the ship, they found small passages carrying the people of this coast to this other coast. They recognized him and said: Abdullah Al-Salih. He said: So we said to Saeed bin Jubair Al-Khidr. He said: Yes, we will not carry him for a fee. So he tore it open and stuck a peg in it. Moses said: You tore it open to drown its people. You have certainly done a terrible thing. Mujahid said: It was strange. He said: Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? The first was forgetfulness, the second was a condition, and the third was deliberate. He said: Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with my task with difficulty. So they set out until they met a boy and killed him. Ya’la said: Saeed said: He found some boys playing, so he took a charming, unbelieving boy, laid him down, and slaughtered him with a knife. He said, Have you killed a pure soul who did not commit perjury? Ibn Abbas read it as Zakiya Muslima, as you would say, a pure young man. So they set out and found a wall about to collapse, so he straightened it. Saeed said: With his hand like this, and he pushed it with his hand and it straightened. He said: If you wished, you could have taken a wage for it. Ya’la said: I thought that Saeed said: So he wiped it with his hand and it straightened. He said: If you wished, you could have taken a wage for it. Saeed said: A wage that we could eat. And behind them was a king, and in front of them. Ibn Abbas read it: In front of them is a king, they claim, from someone other than Saeed, that he was Hadad bin Baddad, and the name of the murdered young man, they claim, was Jaysur, a king who took every ship by force. So I wanted, when it passed by him, for him to leave it with its defect, and when they passed, they repaired it and benefited from it. Some of them say, they sealed it with a bottle, and some of them say, with tar. His parents were believers, and he was a disbeliever, so we feared that he would overburden them with transgression and disbelief, that his love for him would lead them to follow him in his religion. So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him in purity, like His saying: Did you kill a pure soul? And His saying: And nearer of kinship. They are more merciful to him than they were to the first one who killed Khidr. And others besides Sa`id ibn Jubayr claimed that they substituted a slave girl. As for Dawud ibn Abi `Asim, he said on the authority of more than one: It is a slave girl. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Moses, peace be upon him, addressed the Children of Israel and said: No one knows God and His command better than me. So he was ordered to meet this man and he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above with additions and omissions, and God knows best. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Amara on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Utaybah on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair who said: I sat with Ibn Abbas and with him were a group of the People of the Book. Some of them said: O Abu Al-Abbas, Nawf, the son of Kaab’s wife, claims on the authority of Kaab that Moses, the prophet who sought knowledge, is in fact Moses bin Misha. Saeed said: Ibn Abbas said: Does Nawf say this, O Saeed? I said to him: Yes, I heard Nawf say that. He said: Did you hear him, O Saeed? He said: Yes. He said: Nawf lied. Then Ibn Abbas said: My father bin Kaab told me on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that Moses, the son of Israel, asked his Lord, saying: O Lord, if there is one among your servants who is more knowledgeable than me, then guide me to him. He said to him: Yes, among my servants is one who is more knowledgeable than you. Then he described his place to him and gave him permission to meet him. So Moses went out with his young man and with him was a beautiful fish. It was said to him: If this fish revives in a place, then your companion is there and you have fulfilled your need. So Moses went out with his young man and with him was that fish carrying him. He walked until he was exhausted and reached the rock and that water. That water is the water of life. Whoever drinks from it will be immortal and nothing dead will compare to it except that it will be revived. So when they came down and the fish touched the water, it revived and took its path in the sea, a tunnel. So they set off. When they had passed the crossroads, Moses said to his young man: Bring us our lunch. We have indeed encountered fatigue on this journey of ours. The young man said and mentioned: Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the fish and nothing made me forget to mention it except Satan. And he took his way in the sea in a strange way. Ibn Abbas said: So Moses appeared on the rock until they reached it, and there was a man wrapped in his cloak. Moses greeted him and he returned his greeting, then he said to him: What brought you if you have a job among your people? Moses said to him: I have come to you to teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said: You will not be able to have patience with me. And he was a man who knew the knowledge of the unseen, and he knew that. Moses said: Yes. He said: And how can you be patient about that of which you have no knowledge? That is, you only know the outward appearance of what you see of justice, and you have not known the unseen as much as I know. “He said: ‘You will find me, if God wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter. ’” And if you see something that contradicts me, he said: Then if you follow me, do not ask me about anything. And if you deny it, until I mention it to you. He said: Moses saw a terrible thing that he could not bear, a young boy he killed for no reason, he said: "Have you killed a pure soul meaning a young one for no reason? You have certainly done a horrible thing." He said: Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? He said: If I ask you about anything after this, do not accompany me. You have received from Me an excuse." Meaning, you have excused yourself regarding my affair. So he demolished it and sat down to build it. Moses was annoyed by what he saw him doing of the obligation and what he could not bear, so he erected it. As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working at sea. I intended to fault it, and behind them was a king who seized every ship by force.” In Ibn Ka’b’s reading, every ship by force. I only faulted it to prevent him from it, but it was safe from him when he saw the fault that I had made with it. “As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them through transgression and disbelief. So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him, purer in purity and nearer in kinship.” “And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them. Their father had been a righteous man. So your Lord intended that they should reach maturity and extract their treasure as a mercy from your Lord. And I did not do it of my own accord.” That is, I did it of my own accord. That is the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience. Ibn Abbas used to say: The treasure was nothing but knowledge. Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas that they said: When Moses and his people prevailed over Egypt, he settled his people in Egypt. When they settled in the house, God revealed to them that He would remind them of the days of God. So he addressed his people and mentioned what God had given them of goodness and blessings, and he mentioned to them when God saved them from the people of Pharaoh, and he mentioned to them the destruction of their enemy and that God had made them successors on the earth. He said: God spoke to your Prophet directly and chose me for Himself, and sent down upon me love from Him, and God has given you of all that you asked of Him. So your Prophet is the best of the people of the earth, and you read the Torah. So he did not leave a blessing that God had bestowed upon them without making it known to them. A man from the Children of Israel said to him: They are like that, O Prophet. God has made known to us what you are saying: Is there anyone on earth more knowledgeable than you, O Prophet of God? He said: No. Then God sent Gabriel to Moses, peace be upon him, and said: God says: How do you know where I will place my knowledge? Yes, I have on the seashore a man who is more knowledgeable than you. Ibn Abbas said: He is Al-Khidr. Moses asked his Lord to show him to him, and He revealed to him: Go to the sea, and you will find a whale on the seashore, so take it and give it to your servant, then stick to the seashore, and if you forget the whale and it perishes from you, then you will find the righteous servant you are looking for. When the journey of Moses, the Prophet of God, became long and he was tired, he asked his servant about the fish. His servant, who was his young man, said to him, Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the fish, and none made me forget to mention it except Satan. The young man said, I saw the fish when it took its way in the sea, forming a school, and I was amazed by that. So Moses returned until he came to the rock and found the fish. The fish began to strike the sea and Moses followed it. Moses advanced his staff, clearing the water from it, following the fish. The fish did not touch anything in the sea except that the water dried up from it until it became a rock. The Prophet of God was amazed by that until the fish reached an island in the sea and met Al-Khidr there. He greeted him and Al-Khidr said, “And upon you be peace. How can there be peace on this land? And who are you?” He said, I am Moses. Al-Khidr said, The companion of the Children of Israel? He said, Yes. So he welcomed him and said, What brought you? He said, I have come to you so that you may teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said, Indeed, you will never be able to have patience with me. He said, You will find me, God willing, patient, and I will not disobey you in anything. He said, So he went with him and said to him, ‘Do not ask me about anything I do until I explain its nature.’ That is what he said, ‘until I make mention of it to you.’ Al-Zuhri said on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Mas`ud on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he and Al-Har ibn Qays ibn Hisn Al-Fazari had a dispute about the companion of Moses. Ibn Abbas said: He is Al-Khidr. Then Abi ibn Ka`b passed by them and Ibn Abbas called him and said: My companion and I have a dispute about the companion of Moses who asked for the way to meet him. Have you heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mention his affair? He said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “While Moses was in a gathering of the Children of Israel, a man came to him and said: Do you know the location of a man who is more knowledgeable than you? He said: No. So God revealed to Moses: Yes, our servant Khidr. Moses asked how to meet him, so God made the whale a sign for him, and it was said to him: If you miss the whale, go back, for you will meet him. So Moses followed the traces of the whale in the sea, and Moses’ servant said to Moses: Did you see when we took refuge on the rock, for I forgot the whale? Moses said: That is what we were seeking. So they returned, following their traces, and found our servant Khidr, and what happened to them was what God has narrated in His Book.”
18:63: The reason why Moses said this to his servant, Joshua bin Nun, is that he mentioned to him that there was a servant of God at the confluence of the two seas who had knowledge that Moses did not have, so he wanted to travel to him, and he said to his servant, I will not leave, meaning I will not stop walking, until I reach the confluence of the two seas, meaning this place where the two seas converge. Al-Farazdaq said: They did not leave until their women were walking in the plain of Dhi Qara'bat al-Lata'im. Qatada and others said: They are the Persian Gulf towards the east, and the Mediterranean Sea towards the west. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: The two seas meet at Tangier, meaning in the farthest parts of the Maghreb. And God knows best. And His statement: Or I travel ages means even if I travel ages of time. Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: Some of the scholars of Arabic speech mentioned that a haqb in the language of Qais means a year. Then it was narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr that he said: A haqb is eighty years. Mujahid said: Seventy autumns. Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas that his statement: Or I travel ages means: an age. Qatada and Ibn Zayd said the same. And his saying: And when they reached the junction between them, they forgot their fish, that is because he had been ordered to carry a salted fish with him, and it was said to him: Whenever you lose the fish, it is there, so they set out until they reached the junction of the two seas, and there is a spring called the Spring of Life, so they slept there, and the whale was hit by the spray of that water, so it became agitated and it was in a basket with Joshua, peace be upon him, and it jumped from the basket into the sea, so Joshua, peace be upon him, woke up and the whale fell into the sea and it began to move in the water and the water to it was like a bridge that would not heal after it, and for this reason the Almighty said: And it took its way in the sea, a tunnel, meaning like a tunnel on the earth. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: Its trace became like a stone. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The whale did not touch anything in the sea except that it dried up until it became a rock. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Abi bin Kaab, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when he mentioned the hadith of that: No water has ever flowed since people were not on the path of the fish that was in it, so it flowed like a window until Moses returned to it and saw its path, so he said: That is what we were seeking. Qatada said: It flowed from the sea until it reached the land, then it passed through it and he did not take a path in it except that it became solid water. And his saying: And when they passed meaning the place where they forgot the fish, and the forgetfulness was attributed to them even though Joshua was the one who forgot it, like the saying of God Almighty: There emerge from them pearls and coral and it only emerges from salty water according to one of the two opinions, so when they went from the place where they forgot it by a stage, Moses said “to his servant, ‘Bring us our lunch. We have certainly encountered on this journey of ours” meaning the place where they passed exhaustion meaning fatigue. “He said, ‘Have you seen when we took refuge on the rock? I forgot the fish. And none made me forget to mention it except Satan.’” Qatadah said: Ibn Mas`ud read that I should mention it, and for this reason he said, And he took his way meaning his path “in the sea, amazingly. He said, ‘That is what we were seeking.’” meaning this is what we were seeking. So they turned back meaning they returned on their tracks meaning their path recounting meaning they were recounting the tracks of their walking and following in their footsteps. And they found a servant from among Our servants to whom We had given mercy from Us and taught him knowledge from Us. And this is it. Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, as indicated by the authentic hadiths of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Bukhari said: Al-Hamidi told us, Sufyan told us, Amr bin Dinar told us, Saeed bin Jubair told me, he said: I said to Ibn Abbas: Nawf Al-Bakali claims that Moses, the companion of Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, is not Moses, the companion of the Children of Israel. Ibn Abbas said: The enemy of God lied. Abi bin Kaab, may God be pleased with him, told us that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Moses stood up to give a sermon to the Children of Israel and was asked: Who is the most knowledgeable of people? He said: I am. So God rebuked him because he did not refer the knowledge to Him. So God revealed to him: I have a servant at the confluence of the two seas who is more knowledgeable than you. Moses said: O Lord, how can I get him? He said: Take a fish with you and put it in a basket, and wherever you lose the fish, it will be there. So he took a fish and put it in a basket, then he set out and with him set out his servant Joshua bin Nun, peace be upon him, until they reached the rock and put their heads down and slept. The fish stirred in the basket, so it came out of it and fell into the sea and made its way in the sea like a tunnel. God held back the flow of water from the fish, so it became like a vault over it. When he woke up, his companion forgot to tell him about the fish, so they set out for the rest of their day and night until the next day, Moses said to his servant: ‘Bring us our lunch. We have certainly suffered much fatigue on this journey of ours.’” Moses found the monument until he passed the place that God had commanded him to go to. His servant said to him, Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the fish - and none made me forget to mention it except Satan - and it took its way into the sea, a wonder. He said, The fish was a school, and it was a wonder to Moses and his servant. He said, That is what we were seeking. So they returned, retracing their tracks until they reached the rock, and there was a man covered with a garment. Moses greeted him. Al-Khidr said, "And how can I be at peace in your land?" He said, I am Moses. He said, Moses, the children of Israel? He said, Yes. He said, I have come to you so that you may teach me of what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said, Indeed, you will never be able to have patience with me. O Moses, I have knowledge of the knowledge of God that He has taught me which you do not know, and you have knowledge of the knowledge of God that God has taught you which I do not know. Moses said, You will find me, God willing, patient, and I will not disobey you in anything. Al-Khidr said to him, But if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I mention it to you." So they set out walking on the seashore, and a ship passed by, so they spoke to them to carry them, and they recognized Al-Khidr, so they carried them without a reason. When they boarded the ship, they were surprised to find Al-Khidr had torn off one of the ship’s planks with an axe. Moses said to him: They carried us without a reason, and you went to their ship and ripped it open to drown its people? You have certainly done a terrible thing. He said: Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? He said: Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with my affair with hardship. He said: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, said - and the first was forgetfulness from Moses. He said: A bird came and landed on the edge of the ship, and pecked in the sea once or twice, so Al-Khidr said to him: My knowledge and your knowledge compared to God’s knowledge is only like what this bird has taken from this sea. Then they got out of the ship, and while they were walking on the shore, Al-Khidr saw a boy playing with the boys, so Al-Khidr took his head and tore it off with his hand and killed him. Moses said to him, "Have you killed a pure soul without a soul? You have certainly done a horrible thing. He said, Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? He said, This is more severe than the first. He said, If I ask you about anything after this, do not accompany me. You have received an excuse from me." So they set out until, when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to offer them hospitality. They found therein a wall about to collapse." That is, leaning, so Al-Khidr held out his hand and straightened it. Moses said, A people we came to, and they did not give us food or hospitality. If you had wished, you could have taken payment for it. He said, "This is a parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience." The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, We wish that Moses had been patient so that God could relate to us their story. Sa`id ibn Jubayr said: Ibn Abbas used to recite, "And behind them was a king who seized Every ship was seized by force. And he was reading, As for the boy, his parents were believers. Then Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, and he mentioned something similar to it, and in it: So Moses went out with his servant Joshua ibn Nun and the fish with them, until they reached the rock, and they dismounted near it. He said: So Moses put his head down and slept. Sufyan said: And in a hadith on the authority of Umar, he said: And at the base of the rock there is a spring called Al-Hayat, and nothing touches its water except that it comes to life. So the fish touched the water of that spring, and it moved and slipped out of the container and entered the sea. So when it awoke, Moses said to his servant, Bring us our lunch. He said: And he continued the hadith, and a bird landed on the edge of the ship, and dipped its beak in the sea, so Al-Khidr said to Moses: My knowledge and your knowledge and the knowledge of creation compared to the knowledge of God is nothing but the amount that this bird dipped its beak in. And he mentioned the rest of it in a similar manner. Al-Bukhari also said: Ibrahim bin Musa told us, Hisham bin Yusuf told us that Ibn Jurayj told them, he said: Ya`la bin Muslim and `Amr bin Dinar told me on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr, one of them adding more than the other, and others I heard him narrating on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr, he said: We were with Ibn Abbas in his house when he said: Ask me, so I said: O Abu Abbas, may God make me your ransom, in Kufa there is a storyteller called Nawf who claims that he is not the Moses of the Children of Israel. As for `Amr, he said to me: The enemy of God has lied. As for Ya`la, he said to me: Ibn Abbas said: Ubayy bin Ka`b told me: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Moses, the Messenger of God, mentioned the people one day until tears filled the eyes and hearts softened, then he turned away. A man caught up with him and said: O Messenger of God, is there anyone on earth more knowledgeable than you? He said: No. So God rebuked him because he did not refer knowledge to God. It was said: Yes. He said: O Lord, and where? He said: At the confluence of the two seas. He said: O Lord, grant me knowledge by which I may know that. `Amr said to me: He said: Where the fish leaves you.” And Ya`la said to me: Take a dead whale where the soul is breathed into it. So he took a whale and put it in a basket and said to his servant: I will not charge you except that you inform me so that the whale may leave you. He said: I have not charged you a great thing. That is what he said: And when Moses said to his servant Joshua bin Nun is not with Sa`id bin Jubayr. He said: While he was in the shade of a rock in a place of threshing, the whale struck and Moses was asleep. His servant said: I will not wake him up. Then when he woke up, he forgot to tell him, and the whale struck until he entered the sea, and God stopped the flow of water from him until it was as if his mark was on a stone. He said: Amr said to me: This is how it is as if his mark was on a stone, and he circled between his thumbs and the ones next to them. He said: Indeed, we have suffered fatigue in this journey of ours. He said: And God has cut off fatigue from you. This is not with Sa`id bin Jubayr. He told him. So they returned and found green. He said: Uthman bin Abi Sulayman said: On a green rug in the middle of the sea. Sa`id bin Jubayr said: Covered with a garment that had been made. One end was under his feet and the other was at his head. Moses greeted him and he uncovered his face and said: Is there peace in my land? Who are you? He said: I am Moses. He said: Moses of the Children of Israel? He said: Yes. He said: What is the matter with you? He said: I have come to you so that you may teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said: Is it not enough for you that the Torah is in your hands and that revelation comes to you, O Moses? I have knowledge that you should not know, and you have knowledge that I should not know. Then a bird took hold of the sea with its beak and said: By God, my knowledge and your knowledge are not comparable to the knowledge of God except as this bird took hold of the sea with its beak. When they boarded the ship, they found small passages carrying the people of this coast to this other coast. They recognized him and said: Abdullah Al-Salih. He said: So we said to Saeed bin Jubair Al-Khidr. He said: Yes, we will not carry him for a fee. So he tore it open and stuck a peg in it. Moses said: You tore it open to drown its people. You have certainly done a terrible thing. Mujahid said: It was strange. He said: Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? The first was forgetfulness, the second was a condition, and the third was deliberate. He said: Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with my task with difficulty. So they set out until they met a boy and killed him. Ya’la said: Saeed said: He found some boys playing, so he took a charming, unbelieving boy, laid him down, and slaughtered him with a knife. He said, Have you killed a pure soul who did not commit perjury? Ibn Abbas read it as Zakiya Muslima, as you would say, a pure young man. So they set out and found a wall about to collapse, so he straightened it. Saeed said: With his hand like this, and he pushed it with his hand and it straightened. He said: If you wished, you could have taken a wage for it. Ya’la said: I thought that Saeed said: So he wiped it with his hand and it straightened. He said: If you wished, you could have taken a wage for it. Saeed said: A wage that we could eat. And behind them was a king, and in front of them. Ibn Abbas read it: In front of them is a king, they claim, from someone other than Saeed, that he was Hadad bin Baddad, and the name of the murdered young man, they claim, was Jaysur, a king who took every ship by force. So I wanted, when it passed by him, for him to leave it with its defect, and when they passed, they repaired it and benefited from it. Some of them say, they sealed it with a bottle, and some of them say, with tar. His parents were believers, and he was a disbeliever, so we feared that he would overburden them with transgression and disbelief, that his love for him would lead them to follow him in his religion. So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him in purity, like His saying: Did you kill a pure soul? And His saying: And nearer of kinship. They are more merciful to him than they were to the first one who killed Khidr. And others besides Sa`id ibn Jubayr claimed that they substituted a slave girl. As for Dawud ibn Abi `Asim, he said on the authority of more than one: It is a slave girl. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Moses, peace be upon him, addressed the Children of Israel and said: No one knows God and His command better than me. So he was ordered to meet this man and he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above with additions and omissions, and God knows best. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Amara on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Utaybah on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair who said: I sat with Ibn Abbas and with him were a group of the People of the Book. Some of them said: O Abu Al-Abbas, Nawf, the son of Kaab’s wife, claims on the authority of Kaab that Moses, the prophet who sought knowledge, is in fact Moses bin Misha. Saeed said: Ibn Abbas said: Does Nawf say this, O Saeed? I said to him: Yes, I heard Nawf say that. He said: Did you hear him, O Saeed? He said: Yes. He said: Nawf lied. Then Ibn Abbas said: My father bin Kaab told me on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that Moses, the son of Israel, asked his Lord, saying: O Lord, if there is one among your servants who is more knowledgeable than me, then guide me to him. He said to him: Yes, among my servants is one who is more knowledgeable than you. Then he described his place to him and gave him permission to meet him. So Moses went out with his young man and with him was a beautiful fish. It was said to him: If this fish revives in a place, then your companion is there and you have fulfilled your need. So Moses went out with his young man and with him was that fish carrying him. He walked until he was exhausted and reached the rock and that water. That water is the water of life. Whoever drinks from it will be immortal and nothing dead will compare to it except that it will be revived. So when they came down and the fish touched the water, it revived and took its path in the sea, a tunnel. So they set off. When they had passed the crossroads, Moses said to his young man: Bring us our lunch. We have indeed encountered fatigue on this journey of ours. The young man said and mentioned: Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the fish and nothing made me forget to mention it except Satan. And he took his way in the sea in a strange way. Ibn Abbas said: So Moses appeared on the rock until they reached it, and there was a man wrapped in his cloak. Moses greeted him and he returned his greeting, then he said to him: What brought you if you have a job among your people? Moses said to him: I have come to you to teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said: You will not be able to have patience with me. And he was a man who knew the knowledge of the unseen, and he knew that. Moses said: Yes. He said: And how can you be patient about that of which you have no knowledge? That is, you only know the outward appearance of what you see of justice, and you have not known the unseen as much as I know. “He said: ‘You will find me, if God wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter. ’” And if you see something that contradicts me, he said: Then if you follow me, do not ask me about anything. And if you deny it, until I mention it to you. So they set out walking on the shore of the sea, circling people and seeking someone to carry them, until a new, secure ship passed by them, the kindest, most beautiful, and most secure of which no ship had ever passed by. He asked its people to carry them, so they carried them. When they were secure in it and it entered with its people, he took out his beak and a hammer, then he went to a corner and struck it with the beak until he tore it open. Then he took a board and closed it over it, then he sat on it to patch it up. So Moses said to him and saw something more horrific than that: “You have torn it open to drown its people. You have certainly done a terrible thing. He said: “Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me?” He said: Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot. That is, for what He left from your covenant "And do not burden me with my affair with hardship." Then they got out of the ship, and set out until they came to the people of a town, and behold, boys were playing behind it, among them was a boy who was not more charming than any of the boys, nor richer nor more radiant than him, so he took him in his hand and took a stone and struck his head with it until he crushed it and killed him. He said: Moses saw a terrible thing that he could not bear, a young boy he killed for no reason, he said: "Have you killed a pure soul meaning a young one for no reason? You have certainly done a horrible thing." He said: Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? He said: If I ask you about anything after this, do not accompany me. You have received from Me an excuse." Meaning, you have excused yourself regarding my affair. "So they set out until they came to the people of a town, and they asked its people for food, but they refused to host them. They found in it a wall about to collapse. So he demolished it and sat down to build it. Moses was annoyed by what he saw him doing of the obligation and what he could not bear, so he erected it. He said: "If you wished He said: “This is a parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience. As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working at sea. I intended to fault it, and behind them was a king who seized every ship by force.” In Ibn Ka’b’s reading, every ship by force. I only faulted it to prevent him from it, but it was safe from him when he saw the fault that I had made with it. “As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them through transgression and disbelief. So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him, purer in purity and nearer in kinship.” “And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them. Their father had been a righteous man. So your Lord intended that they should reach maturity and extract their treasure as a mercy from your Lord. And I did not do it of my own accord.” That is, I did it of my own accord. That is the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience. Ibn Abbas used to say: The treasure was nothing but knowledge. Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas that they said: When Moses and his people prevailed over Egypt, he settled his people in Egypt. When they settled in the house, God revealed to them that He would remind them of the days of God. So he addressed his people and mentioned what God had given them of goodness and blessings, and he mentioned to them when God saved them from the people of Pharaoh, and he mentioned to them the destruction of their enemy and that God had made them successors on the earth. He said: God spoke to your Prophet directly and chose me for Himself, and sent down upon me love from Him, and God has given you of all that you asked of Him. So your Prophet is the best of the people of the earth, and you read the Torah. So he did not leave a blessing that God had bestowed upon them without making it known to them. A man from the Children of Israel said to him: They are like that, O Prophet. God has made known to us what you are saying: Is there anyone on earth more knowledgeable than you, O Prophet of God? He said: No. Then God sent Gabriel to Moses, peace be upon him, and said: God says: How do you know where I will place my knowledge? Yes, I have on the seashore a man who is more knowledgeable than you. Ibn Abbas said: He is Al-Khidr. Moses asked his Lord to show him to him, and He revealed to him: Go to the sea, and you will find a whale on the seashore, so take it and give it to your servant, then stick to the seashore, and if you forget the whale and it perishes from you, then you will find the righteous servant you are looking for. When the journey of Moses, the Prophet of God, became long and he was tired, he asked his servant about the fish. His servant, who was his young man, said to him, Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the fish, and none made me forget to mention it except Satan. The young man said, I saw the fish when it took its way in the sea, forming a school, and I was amazed by that. So Moses returned until he came to the rock and found the fish.
