The fish did not touch anything in the sea except that the water dried up from it until it became a rock. The Prophet of God was amazed by that until the fish reached an island in the sea and met Al-Khidr there. He greeted him and Al-Khidr said, “And upon you be peace. How can there be peace on this land? And who are you?” He said, I am Moses. Al-Khidr said, The companion of the Children of Israel? He said, Yes. So he welcomed him and said, What brought you? He said, I have come to you so that you may teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said, Indeed, you will never be able to have patience with me. He said, You will find me, God willing, patient, and I will not disobey you in anything. He said, So he went with him and said to him, ‘Do not ask me about anything I do until I explain its nature.’ That is what he said, ‘until I make mention of it to you.’ Al-Zuhri said on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Mas`ud on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he and Al-Har ibn Qays ibn Hisn Al-Fazari had a dispute about the companion of Moses. Ibn Abbas said: He is Al-Khidr. Then Abi ibn Ka`b passed by them and Ibn Abbas called him and said: My companion and I have a dispute about the companion of Moses who asked for the way to meet him. Have you heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mention his affair? He said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “While Moses was in a gathering of the Children of Israel, a man came to him and said: Do you know the location of a man who is more knowledgeable than you? He said: No. So God revealed to Moses: Yes, our servant Khidr. Moses asked how to meet him, so God made the whale a sign for him, and it was said to him: If you miss the whale, go back, for you will meet him. So Moses followed the traces of the whale in the sea, and Moses’ servant said to Moses: Did you see when we took refuge on the rock, for I forgot the whale? Moses said: That is what we were seeking. So they returned, following their traces, and found our servant Khidr, and what happened to them was what God has narrated in His Book.”
18:64: The reason why Moses said this to his servant, Joshua bin Nun, is that he mentioned to him that there was a servant of God at the confluence of the two seas who had knowledge that Moses did not have, so he wanted to travel to him, and he said to his servant, I will not leave, meaning I will not stop walking, until I reach the confluence of the two seas, meaning this place where the two seas converge. Al-Farazdaq said: They did not leave until their women were walking in the plain of Dhi Qara'bat al-Lata'im. Qatada and others said: They are the Persian Gulf towards the east, and the Mediterranean Sea towards the west. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: The two seas meet at Tangier, meaning in the farthest parts of the Maghreb. And God knows best. And His statement: Or I travel ages means even if I travel ages of time. Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: Some of the scholars of Arabic speech mentioned that a haqb in the language of Qais means a year. Then it was narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr that he said: A haqb is eighty years. Mujahid said: Seventy autumns. Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas that his statement: Or I travel ages means: an age. Qatada and Ibn Zayd said the same. And his saying: And when they reached the junction between them, they forgot their fish, that is because he had been ordered to carry a salted fish with him, and it was said to him: Whenever you lose the fish, it is there, so they set out until they reached the junction of the two seas, and there is a spring called the Spring of Life, so they slept there, and the whale was hit by the spray of that water, so it became agitated and it was in a basket with Joshua, peace be upon him, and it jumped from the basket into the sea, so Joshua, peace be upon him, woke up and the whale fell into the sea and it began to move in the water and the water to it was like a bridge that would not heal after it, and for this reason the Almighty said: And it took its way in the sea, a tunnel, meaning like a tunnel on the earth. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: Its trace became like a stone. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The whale did not touch anything in the sea except that it dried up until it became a rock. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Abi bin Kaab, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when he mentioned the hadith of that: No water has ever flowed since people were not on the path of the fish that was in it, so it flowed like a window until Moses returned to it and saw its path, so he said: That is what we were seeking. Qatada said: It flowed from the sea until it reached the land, then it passed through it and he did not take a path in it except that it became solid water. And his saying: And when they passed meaning the place where they forgot the fish, and the forgetfulness was attributed to them even though Joshua was the one who forgot it, like the saying of God Almighty: There emerge from them pearls and coral and it only emerges from salty water according to one of the two opinions, so when they went from the place where they forgot it by a stage, Moses said “to his servant, ‘Bring us our lunch. We have certainly encountered on this journey of ours” meaning the place where they passed exhaustion meaning fatigue. “He said, ‘Have you seen when we took refuge on the rock? I forgot the fish. And none made me forget to mention it except Satan.’” Qatadah said: Ibn Mas`ud read that I should mention it, and for this reason he said, And he took his way meaning his path “in the sea, amazingly. He said, ‘That is what we were seeking.’” meaning this is what we were seeking. So they turned back meaning they returned on their tracks meaning their path recounting meaning they were recounting the tracks of their walking and following in their footsteps. And they found a servant from among Our servants to whom We had given mercy from Us and taught him knowledge from Us. And this is it. Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, as indicated by the authentic hadiths of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Bukhari said: Al-Hamidi told us, Sufyan told us, Amr bin Dinar told us, Saeed bin Jubair told me, he said: I said to Ibn Abbas: Nawf Al-Bakali claims that Moses, the companion of Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, is not Moses, the companion of the Children of Israel. Ibn Abbas said: The enemy of God lied. Abi bin Kaab, may God be pleased with him, told us that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Moses stood up to give a sermon to the Children of Israel and was asked: Who is the most knowledgeable of people? He said: I am. So God rebuked him because he did not refer the knowledge to Him. So God revealed to him: I have a servant at the confluence of the two seas who is more knowledgeable than you. Moses said: O Lord, how can I get him? He said: Take a fish with you and put it in a basket, and wherever you lose the fish, it will be there. So he took a fish and put it in a basket, then he set out and with him set out his servant Joshua bin Nun, peace be upon him, until they reached the rock and put their heads down and slept. The fish stirred in the basket, so it came out of it and fell into the sea and made its way in the sea like a tunnel. God held back the flow of water from the fish, so it became like a vault over it. When he woke up, his companion forgot to tell him about the fish, so they set out for the rest of their day and night until the next day, Moses said to his servant: ‘Bring us our lunch. We have certainly suffered much fatigue on this journey of ours.’” Moses found the monument until he passed the place that God had commanded him to go to. His servant said to him, Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the fish - and none made me forget to mention it except Satan - and it took its way into the sea, a wonder. He said, The fish was a school, and it was a wonder to Moses and his servant. He said, That is what we were seeking. So they returned, retracing their tracks until they reached the rock, and there was a man covered with a garment. Moses greeted him. Al-Khidr said, "And how can I be at peace in your land?" He said, I am Moses. He said, Moses, the children of Israel? He said, Yes. He said, I have come to you so that you may teach me of what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said, Indeed, you will never be able to have patience with me. O Moses, I have knowledge of the knowledge of God that He has taught me which you do not know, and you have knowledge of the knowledge of God that God has taught you which I do not know. Moses said, You will find me, God willing, patient, and I will not disobey you in anything. Al-Khidr said to him, But if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I mention it to you." So they set out walking on the seashore, and a ship passed by, so they spoke to them to carry them, and they recognized Al-Khidr, so they carried them without a plank. When they boarded the ship, they were surprised to find Al-Khidr had torn off one of the ship’s planks with an axe. Moses said to him: They carried us without a plank, and you went to their ship and ripped it open to drown its people? You have certainly done a terrible thing. He said: Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? He said: Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with my affair with hardship. He said: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, said - and the first was forgetfulness from Moses. He said: A bird came and landed on the edge of the ship, and pecked in the sea once or twice, so Al-Khidr said to him: My knowledge and your knowledge compared to God’s knowledge is only like what this bird has taken from this sea. Then they got out of the ship, and while they were walking on the shore, Al-Khidr saw a boy playing with the boys, so Al-Khidr took his head and tore it off with his hand and killed him. Moses said to him, "Have you killed a pure soul without a soul? You have certainly done a horrible thing. He said, Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? He said, This is more severe than the first. He said, If I ask you about anything after this, do not accompany me. You have received an excuse from me." So they set out until, when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to offer them hospitality. They found therein a wall about to collapse." That is, leaning, so Al-Khidr held out his hand and straightened it. Moses said, A people we came to, and they did not give us food or hospitality. If you had wished, you could have taken payment for it. He said, "This is a parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience." The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, We wish that Moses had been patient so that God could relate to us their story. Sa`id ibn Jubayr said: Ibn Abbas used to recite, "And behind them was a king who seized Every ship was seized by force. And he was reading, As for the boy, his parents were believers. Then Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, and he mentioned something similar to it, and in it: So Moses went out with his servant Joshua ibn Nun and the fish with them, until they reached the rock, and they dismounted near it. He said: So Moses put his head down and slept. Sufyan said: And in a hadith on the authority of Umar, he said: And at the base of the rock there is a spring called Al-Hayat, and nothing touches its water except that it comes to life. So the fish touched the water of that spring, and it moved and slipped out of the container and entered the sea. So when it awoke, Moses said to his servant, Bring us our lunch. He said: And he continued the hadith, and a bird landed on the edge of the ship, and dipped its beak in the sea, so Al-Khidr said to Moses: My knowledge and your knowledge and the knowledge of creation compared to the knowledge of God is nothing but the amount that this bird dipped its beak in. And he mentioned the rest of it in a similar manner. Al-Bukhari also said: Ibrahim bin Musa told us, Hisham bin Yusuf told us that Ibn Jurayj told them, he said: Ya`la bin Muslim and `Amr bin Dinar told me on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr, one of them adding more than the other, and others I heard him narrating on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr, he said: We were with Ibn Abbas in his house when he said: Ask me, so I said: O Abu Abbas, may God make me your ransom, in Kufa there is a storyteller called Nawf who claims that he is not the Moses of the Children of Israel. As for `Amr, he said to me: The enemy of God has lied. As for Ya`la, he said to me: Ibn Abbas said: Ubayy bin Ka`b told me: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Moses, the Messenger of God, mentioned the people one day until tears filled the eyes and hearts softened, then he turned away. A man caught up with him and said: O Messenger of God, is there anyone on earth more knowledgeable than you? He said: No. So God rebuked him because he did not refer knowledge to God. It was said: Yes. He said: O Lord, and where? He said: At the confluence of the two seas. He said: O Lord, grant me knowledge by which I may know that. `Amr said to me: He said: Where the fish leaves you.” And Ya`la said to me: Take a dead whale where the soul is breathed into it. So he took a whale and put it in a basket and said to his servant: I will not charge you except that you inform me so that the whale may leave you. He said: I have not charged you a great thing. That is what he said: And when Moses said to his servant Joshua bin Nun is not with Sa`id bin Jubayr. He said: While he was in the shade of a rock in a place of threshing, the whale struck and Moses was asleep. His servant said: I will not wake him up. Then when he woke up, he forgot to tell him, and the whale struck until he entered the sea, and God stopped the flow of water from him until it was as if his mark was on a stone. He said: Amr said to me: This is how it is as if his mark was on a stone, and he circled between his thumbs and the ones next to them. He said: Indeed, we have suffered fatigue in this journey of ours. He said: And God has cut off fatigue from you. This is not with Sa`id bin Jubayr. He told him. So they returned and found green. He said: Uthman bin Abi Sulayman said: On a green rug in the middle of the sea. Sa`id bin Jubayr said: Covered with a garment that had been made. One end was under his feet and the other was at his head. Moses greeted him and he uncovered his face and said: Is there peace in my land? Who are you? He said: I am Moses. He said: Moses of the Children of Israel? He said: Yes. He said: What is the matter with you? He said: I have come to you so that you may teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said: Is it not enough for you that the Torah is in your hands and that revelation comes to you, O Moses? I have knowledge that you should not know, and you have knowledge that I should not know. Then a bird took hold of the sea with its beak and said: By God, my knowledge and your knowledge are not comparable to the knowledge of God except as this bird took hold of the sea with its beak. When they boarded the ship, they found small passages carrying the people of this coast to this other coast. They recognized him and said: Abdullah Al-Salih. He said: So we said to Saeed bin Jubair Al-Khidr. He said: Yes, we will not carry him for a fee. So he tore it open and stuck a peg in it. Moses said: You tore it open to drown its people. You have certainly done a terrible thing. Mujahid said: It was strange. He said: Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? The first was forgetfulness, the second was a condition, and the third was deliberate. He said: Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with my task with difficulty. So they set out until they met a boy and killed him. Ya’la said: Saeed said: He found some boys playing, so he took a charming, unbelieving boy, laid him down, and slaughtered him with a knife. He said, Have you killed a pure soul who did not commit perjury? Ibn Abbas read it as Zakiya Muslima, as you would say, a pure young man. So they set out and found a wall about to collapse, so he straightened it. Saeed said: With his hand like this, and he pushed it with his hand and it straightened. He said: If you wished, you could have taken a wage for it. Ya’la said: I thought that Saeed said: So he wiped it with his hand and it straightened. He said: If you wished, you could have taken a wage for it. Saeed said: A wage that we could eat. And behind them was a king, and in front of them. Ibn Abbas read it: In front of them is a king, they claim, from someone other than Saeed, that he was Hadad bin Baddad, and the name of the murdered young man, they claim, was Jaysur, a king who took every ship by force. So I wanted, when it passed by him, for him to leave it with its defect, and when they passed, they repaired it and benefited from it. Some of them say, they sealed it with a bottle, and some of them say, with tar. His parents were believers, and he was a disbeliever, so we feared that he would overburden them with transgression and disbelief, that his love for him would lead them to follow him in his religion. So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him in purity, like His saying: Did you kill a pure soul? And His saying: And nearer of kinship. They are more merciful to him than they were to the first one who killed Khidr. And others besides Sa`id ibn Jubayr claimed that they substituted a slave girl. As for Dawud ibn Abi `Asim, he said on the authority of more than one: It is a slave girl. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Moses, peace be upon him, addressed the Children of Israel and said: No one knows God and His command better than me. So he was ordered to meet this man and he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above with additions and omissions, and God knows best. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Amara on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Utaybah on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair who said: I sat with Ibn Abbas and with him were a group of the People of the Book. Some of them said: O Abu Al-Abbas, Nawf, the son of Kaab’s wife, claims on the authority of Kaab that Moses, the prophet who sought knowledge, is in fact Moses bin Misha. Saeed said: Ibn Abbas said: Does Nawf say this, O Saeed? I said to him: Yes, I heard Nawf say that. He said: Did you hear him, O Saeed? He said: Yes. He said: Nawf lied. Then Ibn Abbas said: My father bin Kaab told me on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that Moses, the son of Israel, asked his Lord, saying: O Lord, if there is one among your servants who is more knowledgeable than me, then guide me to him. He said to him: Yes, among my servants is one who is more knowledgeable than you. Then he described his place to him and gave him permission to meet him. So Moses went out with his young man and with him was a beautiful fish. It was said to him: If this fish revives in a place, then your companion is there and you have fulfilled your need. So Moses went out with his young man and with him was that fish carrying him. He walked until he was exhausted and reached the rock and that water. That water is the water of life. Whoever drinks from it will be immortal and nothing dead will compare to it except that it will be revived. So when they came down and the fish touched the water, it revived and took its path in the sea, a tunnel. So they set off. When they had passed the crossroads, Moses said to his young man: Bring us our lunch. We have indeed encountered fatigue on this journey of ours. The young man said and mentioned: Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the fish and nothing made me forget to mention it except Satan. And he took his way in the sea in a strange way. Ibn Abbas said: So Moses appeared on the rock until they reached it, and there was a man wrapped in his cloak. Moses greeted him and he returned his greeting, then he said to him: What brought you if you have a job among your people? Moses said to him: I have come to you to teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said: You will not be able to have patience with me. And he was a man who knew the knowledge of the unseen, and he knew that. Moses said: Yes. He said: And how can you be patient about that of which you have no knowledge? That is, you only know the outward appearance of what you see of justice, and you have not known the unseen as much as I know. “He said: ‘You will find me, if God wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter. ’” And if you see something that contradicts me, he said: Then if you follow me, do not ask me about anything. And if you deny it, until I mention it to you. So they set out walking on the shore of the sea, circling people and seeking someone to carry them, until a new, secure ship passed by them, the kindest, most beautiful, and most secure of which no ship had ever passed by. He asked its people to carry them, so they carried them. When they were secure in it and it entered with its people, he took out his beak and a hammer, then he went to a corner and struck it with the beak until he tore it open. Then he took a board and closed it over it, then he sat on it to patch it up. So Moses said to him and saw something more horrific than that: “You have torn it open to drown its people. You have certainly done a terrible thing. He said: “Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me?” He said: Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot. That is, for what He left from your covenant "And do not burden me with my affair with hardship." Then they got out of the ship, and set out until they came to the people of a town, and behold, boys were playing behind it, among them was a boy who was not more charming than any of the boys, nor richer nor more radiant than him, so he took him in his hand and took a stone and struck his head with it until he crushed it and killed him. He said: Moses saw a terrible thing that he could not bear, a young boy he killed for no reason, he said: "Have you killed a pure soul meaning a young one for no reason? You have certainly done a horrible thing." He said: Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? He said: If I ask you about anything after this, do not accompany me. You have received from Me an excuse." Meaning, you have excused yourself regarding my affair. "So they set out until they came to the people of a town, and they asked its people for food, but they refused to host them. They found in it a wall about to collapse. So he demolished it and sat down to build it. Moses was annoyed by what he saw him doing of the obligation and what he could not bear, so he erected it. He said: "If you wished He said: “This is a parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience. As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working at sea. I intended to fault it, and behind them was a king who seized every ship by force.” In Ibn Ka’b’s reading, every ship by force. I only faulted it to prevent him from it, but it was safe from him when he saw the fault that I had made with it. “As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them through transgression and disbelief. So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him, purer in purity and nearer in kinship.” “And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them. Their father had been a righteous man. So your Lord intended that they should reach maturity and extract their treasure as a mercy from your Lord. And I did not do it of my own accord.” That is, I did it of my own accord. That is the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience. Ibn Abbas used to say: The treasure was nothing but knowledge. Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas that they said: When Moses and his people prevailed over Egypt, he settled his people in Egypt. When they settled in the house, God revealed to them that He would remind them of the days of God. So he addressed his people and mentioned what God had given them of goodness and blessings, and he mentioned to them when God saved them from the people of Pharaoh, and he mentioned to them the destruction of their enemy and that God had made them successors on the earth. He said: God spoke to your Prophet directly and chose me for Himself, and sent down upon me love from Him, and God has given you of all that you asked of Him. So your Prophet is the best of the people of the earth, and you read the Torah. So he did not leave a blessing that God had bestowed upon them without making it known to them. A man from the Children of Israel said to him: They are like that, O Prophet. God has made known to us what you are saying: Is there anyone on earth more knowledgeable than you, O Prophet of God? He said: No. Then God sent Gabriel to Moses, peace be upon him, and said: God says: How do you know where I will place my knowledge? Yes, I have on the seashore a man who is more knowledgeable than you. Ibn Abbas said: He is Al-Khidr. Moses asked his Lord to show him to him, and He revealed to him: Go to the sea, and you will find a whale on the seashore, so take it and give it to your servant, then stick to the seashore, and if you forget the whale and it perishes from you, then you will find the righteous servant you are looking for. When the journey of Moses, the Prophet of God, became long and he was tired, he asked his servant about the fish. His servant, who was his young man, said to him, Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the fish, and none made me forget to mention it except Satan. The young man said, I saw the fish when it took its way in the sea, forming a school, and I was amazed by that. So Moses returned until he came to the rock and found the fish. The fish began to strike the sea and Moses followed it. Moses advanced his staff, clearing the water from it, following the fish. The fish did not touch anything in the sea except that the water dried up from it until it became a rock. The Prophet of God was amazed by that until the fish reached an island in the sea and met Al-Khidr there. He greeted him and Al-Khidr said, “And upon you be peace. How can there be peace on this land? And who are you?” He said, I am Moses. Al-Khidr said, The companion of the Children of Israel? He said, Yes. So he welcomed him and said, What brought you? He said, I have come to you so that you may teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said, Indeed, you will never be able to have patience with me. He said, You will find me, God willing, patient, and I will not disobey you in anything. He said, So he went with him and said to him, ‘Do not ask me about anything I do until I explain its nature.’ That is what he said, ‘until I make mention of it to you.’ Al-Zuhri said on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Mas`ud on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he and Al-Har ibn Qays ibn Hisn Al-Fazari had a dispute about the companion of Moses. Ibn Abbas said: He is Al-Khidr. Then Abi ibn Ka`b passed by them and Ibn Abbas called him and said: My companion and I have a dispute about the companion of Moses who asked for the way to meet him. Have you heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mention his affair? He said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “While Moses was in a gathering of the Children of Israel, a man came to him and said: Do you know the location of a man who is more knowledgeable than you? He said: No. So God revealed to Moses: Yes, our servant Khidr. Moses asked how to meet him, so God made the whale a sign for him, and it was said to him: If you miss the whale, go back, for you will meet him. So they returned, following their traces, and found our servant Khidr, and what happened to them was what God has narrated in His Book.”

So each of us is charged with matters from God without his companion, and you are not able to accompany me and how can you be patient with what you do not have knowledge of? So I know that you will deny me what you are excused for, but I have not learned of His wisdom and His inner benefit that I have learned of but you have not learned of. He meaning Moses You will find me, God willing, patient meaning with what I see of your affairs and I will not disobey you in anything meaning I will not disagree with you in anything. Then Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, made a condition with him He said, ‘Then if you follow me, do not ask me about anything’ meaning at first. Until I tell you about it means until I tell you about it before you ask me. Ibn Jarir said: Humayd ibn Jubayr narrated to us, Yaqub narrated to us, on the authority of Harun ibn Antara, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Moses, peace be upon him, asked his Lord, the Almighty, and said: O Lord, which of Your servants is most beloved to You? He said: He who remembers Me and does not forget Me. He said: Which of Your servants is the most just? He said: He who judges with truth and does not follow desire. He said: O Lord, which of Your servants is the most knowledgeable? He said: He who seeks the knowledge of the people to His knowledge, perhaps he may find a word that will guide him to guidance or turn him away from ruin. He said: O Lord, is there anyone on Your earth who is more knowledgeable than me? He said: Yes. He said: Who is he? He said: Al-Khidr. He said: Where can I look for him? He said: On the shore, near the rock where the fish escapes. He said: So Moses went out looking for him until what God had mentioned happened, and Moses reached him at the rock, and each of them greeted the other, and Moses said to him: I would like to be your companion. He said: You will not be able to bear my company. He said: Yes. He said: If you accompany me, do not ask me about anything until I mention it to you. He said: So he sailed with him in the sea until he reached the junction of the two seas, and there is no place on earth with more water than it. He said: And God sent the swallow, and it began to draw water from it with its beak, and it said to Moses: How much of this water do you think this swallow has drawn? He said: How little it has drawn. He said: O Moses, my knowledge and your knowledge in God’s knowledge are like the amount of water this swallow has drawn from this water. Moses had thought to himself that no one was more knowledgeable than him or spoke about it, so he was ordered to go to Al-Khidr, and he mentioned the entire story about the breach in the ship, the killing of the boy, and the repair of the wall, and his interpretation of that to him.

18:71: The Almighty says, informing about Moses and his companion, who is Al-Khidr, that they set out when they agreed and accompanied each other, and he stipulated that he would not ask him about something that he denied until he was the one who initiated it on his own by explaining and clarifying it, so they boarded the ship. It was mentioned in the hadith how they boarded the ship, and that they knew Al-Khidr, so they carried them without a fee, meaning without a wage, as an honor to Al-Khidr. So when the ship took them to sea and became agitated, that is, entered the depths, Al-Khidr stood up and made a hole in it, and took out a plank from its planks and patched it up, so Moses, peace be upon him, could not control himself and said, denouncing him, You made a hole in it to drown its people. This lam is the lam of consequence, not the lam of reason, as the poet said: They were born for death and built for destruction You have certainly done something very bitter. Mujahid said: It is strange. Qatada said: It is strange. Then Al-Khidr said to him, reminding him of the previous condition: Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? meaning, I did this deed intentionally, and it is one of the things that I stipulated with you that you would not criticize me for, because you did not have complete knowledge of it and it had an interest that you did not know. He said, meaning Moses, Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot and do not burden me with my task with difficulty, meaning do not make things difficult for me or make things hard for me. This is why it was mentioned in the hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The first thing Moses forgot.

18:74: God Almighty says: So they set out meaning after that until they met a boy and killed him and it was mentioned that he was playing with the boys in a village, and that he went to him from among them, and he was the best, most beautiful and brightest of them, and killed him, and it was narrated that he cut off his head, and it was said that he crushed it with a stone, and in another narration he pulled it out with his hand, and God knows best, so when Moses, peace be upon him, saw this, he disapproved of it more than the first time, and he hastened and said: Have you killed a pure soul meaning a young one who had not committed perjury or sinned after that, so you killed him for no reason meaning without a basis for killing him You have certainly done a thing reprehensible meaning apparently reprehensible He said, Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me so he also emphasized the reminder with the first condition, so for this reason Moses said to him: If I ask you about anything after this meaning if I object to you about something after this time do not accompany me, you have already received an excuse from me meaning you have excused me time after time, Ibn Jarir: Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad told us, Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Hamza al-Zayyat, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Abi bin Kaab, who said: Whenever the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned someone and prayed for him, he would start with himself. One day he said: “May God’s mercy be upon us and upon Moses. If he had stayed with his companion, he would have seen the wonder. But he said: If I ask you about anything after this, do not keep company with me, for you have received an excuse from me.”

18:77: God Almighty says, informing about them that they set out after the first two times until, when they came to the people of a town Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Sirin that it was Al-Aylah, and in the hadith until, when they came to the people of a town, mean meaning stingy they asked its people for food but they refused to host them, and they found therein a wall about to collapse The attribution of the will here to the wall is by way of metaphor, for the will in new things means inclination, and collapsing is falling. And his saying: So he straightened him up means he restored him to a state of uprightness. It was mentioned in the hadith that he restored him with his hands and supported him until he returned his inclination, and this is extraordinary. At that time, Moses said to him: If you had wanted, you could have taken a wage for it meaning because they did not host us, it was not appropriate for you to work for them for free. “He said: This is a parting between me and you” meaning because you stipulated when killing the boy that if you asked me about anything after that, do not accompany me, so it is a parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation meaning the explanation of that about which you were not able to have patience.

18:79: This is an explanation of what was unclear to Moses, peace be upon him, and what he denied on the surface. God showed Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, an inner wisdom, and he said: I only punctured the ship to make it defective because they were passing by a king of oppressors who seizes every good ship, meaning good by force. So I wanted to make it defective to return it to him because of its defect, so that its poor owners who had nothing to benefit from other than it would benefit from it. It has been said that they were orphans. Ibn Jurayj narrated on the authority of Wahb bin Sulayman, on the authority of Shu'ayb Al-Jubba'i, that the name of the king was Hadad bin Badad, and it was also mentioned in the narration of Al-Bukhari, and he is mentioned in the Torah in the descendants of Esau bin Isaac, and he is one of the kings mentioned in the Torah, and God knows best.
18:80: It was mentioned earlier that this boy's name was Jessor. In this hadith, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Abi bin Kaab, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: The boy whom Al-Khidr killed was born a disbeliever on the day he was born. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir from the hadith of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and for this reason he said: His parents were believers, so we feared that he would burden them with transgression and disbelief, meaning that their love for him would lead them to follow him in disbelief. Qatada said: His parents were happy with him when he was born, and they were sad about him when he was killed, and if he had lived, it would have led to their destruction. So let a person be satisfied with the decree of God, for God’s decree for a believer in what he dislikes is better for him than His decree for what he likes. It is authentically stated in the hadith: God does not decree for a believer a decree except that it is good for him. And God Almighty said: And perhaps you dislike a thing while it is good for you. And His statement: So We intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him in purity and nearer of kinship, meaning a child purer than this one, and they are more merciful to him than him, as Ibn Jurayj said. Qatada said: He was dutiful to his parents, and it was previously mentioned that they were a substitute for a slave girl. It was said: When Al-Khidr killed him, his mother was pregnant with a Muslim boy, as Ibn Jurayj said.

18:82: In this verse is evidence that the word village refers to the city, because He first said, Until, when they came to the people of a city, and He said here, And there were two orphan boys in the city, as God Almighty said, And how many a city was stronger than your city which expelled you? "And they said, 'Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from the two cities?'" meaning Mecca and Taif. The meaning of the verse is that this wall was repaired because it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and there was a treasure under it for them. Ikrimah, Qatadah, and more than one said: And there was buried money for them under it, and this is the apparent context of the verse, and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: There was a treasure of knowledge beneath it. Saeed bin Jubair said the same. Mujahid said: Pages containing knowledge. There is a hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet that supports this. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Amr bin Abdul Khaliq Al-Bazzar said in his famous Musnad: Ibrahim bin Saeed Al-Jawhari told us, Bishr bin Al-Mundhir told us, Al-Harith bin Abdullah Al-Yahsabi told us, on the authority of Ayyash bin Abbas Al-Ghani, on the authority of Ibn Hujaira, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: “The treasure that God mentioned in His Book is a solid gold tablet, on which is written: I am amazed at the one who is certain of destiny, why is he afflicted? I am amazed at the one who remembers Hell, why does he laugh? I am amazed at the one who remembers death, why is he heedless. There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God.” This Bishr bin Al-Mundhir was called the judge of Misisa. Al-Hafiz Abu Ja`far al-`Uqayli said in his hadith that they were mistaken, and there are traces of this narrated from the predecessors. Ibn Jarir said in his interpretation: Ya`qub told me, al-Hasan ibn Habib ibn Nudbah told us, Salamah told us on the authority of Na`im al-`Anbari, who was one of al-Hasan’s companions, he said: I heard al-Hasan, meaning al-Basri, say regarding his statement: And beneath it was a treasure for them both, he said: A tablet of gold on which was written: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. I am amazed at the one who believes in destiny, how he is sad, and I am amazed at the one who believes in death, how he is happy, and I am amazed at the one who knows the world and its vicissitudes with its people, how he is reassured by it. There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God. Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Abdullah bin Ayyash told me, on the authority of Omar, the freed slave of Ghafra, who said: The treasure that God mentioned in the Surah in which the cave is mentioned, And beneath it was a treasure for them, was a solid gold tablet, on which was written: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. I am amazed at the one who knew the Fire and then laughed. I am amazed at the one who was certain of destiny and then became weary. I am amazed at the one who was certain of death and then felt secure. I bear witness that there is no god but God and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. Ahmad bin Hazim al-Ghifari told me, Hanada bint Malik al-Shaibaniyyah told us, she said: I heard my companion Hammad bin al-Walid al-Thaqafi say: I heard Ja’far bin Muhammad say regarding the statement of God, the Most High, And beneath it was a treasure for them, he said: Two and a half lines, the third is not complete: I am amazed at the one who is certain of provision, how he tires himself out, I am amazed at the one who believes in the reckoning, how he is heedless, and I am amazed at the one who believes in death, how he rejoices. And God said: And if it be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth, and sufficient are We as reckoners. She said: And it was mentioned that they were preserved by the righteousness of their father, and no righteousness was mentioned from them, and between them and the father by whom they were preserved were seven fathers, and he was a weaver. And what these imams mentioned and the previous hadith was narrated by it, even if it is authentic, does not contradict the statement of Ikrimah that it was wealth, because they mentioned that it was a tablet of gold, and in it was a great deal of wealth, and what they added most of all was that knowledge was deposited in it, and it was wisdom and sermons, and God knows best. His saying: And their father was a righteous man is evidence that a righteous man is preserved in his offspring and the blessing of his worship includes them in this world and the hereafter through his intercession for them, and raising their status to the highest status in Paradise, so that his eyes may be comforted by them, as stated in the Qur’an and the Sunnah. Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They were preserved by the righteousness of their father, and he did not mention righteousness for them, and it was mentioned previously that he was the previous father, and God knows best. His saying: And your Lord intended that they should reach maturity and extract their treasure here He attributed the will to God Almighty, because their reaching maturity is not within the power of anyone except God. He said about the boy: So We intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him as purity and He said about the ship: So I intended to damage it and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: “A mercy from your Lord. And I did not do it of my own accord.” That is, what I did in these three situations is from the mercy of God to those we mentioned from the people of the ship, the father of the boy, and the son of the righteous man. And I did not do it of my own accord, that is, I was commanded to do it and I was informed about it. And in it is evidence for those who say that al-Khidr, peace be upon him, was a prophet, along with what came before from His saying: And they found a servant from among Our servants to whom We had given mercy from Us and had taught him knowledge from Us. And others said: He was a messenger. And it was said: Rather, he was an angel, as al-Mawardi mentioned in his interpretation. And many went to the view that he was not a prophet, but rather a saint, and God knows best. Ibn Qutaybah mentioned in Al-Ma’arif that Al-Khidr’s name was Baliya bin Malkan bin Faligh bin Aamer bin Shalih bin Arfakhshad bin Sam bin Noah, peace be upon him. They said: He was called Abu Al-Abbas and was nicknamed Al-Khidr. He was one of the sons of kings. Al-Nawawi mentioned him in Tahdhib Al-Asma’. He and others narrated two opinions about his remaining until now, then until the Day of Resurrection. He and Ibn Al-Salah tended towards his remaining. They mentioned stories and traces from the predecessors and others about that. He was mentioned in some hadiths, but none of that is authentic. The most famous of them is the hadith of condolence, and its chain of transmission is weak. Others from the hadith scholars and others preferred the opposite of that, and they cited as evidence the words of God Almighty: And We have not granted to any human being before You immortality and the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr: O God, if this group is destroyed, You will not be worshipped on the earth. And that it was not reported that he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor was he present with him nor fought with him. If he had been alive, he would have been among the followers of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, because he, peace be upon him, was… Sent to all of mankind and jinn, he said: If Moses and Jesus were alive, they would have no choice but to follow me. And he informed us shortly before his death that no one on the face of the earth would remain for a hundred years from that night, not even an eye would blink, and other evidence. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Adam told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding Al-Khidr, he said: He was called Al-Khidr because he sat on a white fur, and suddenly it began to shake green beneath him. He also narrated it on the authority of Abd Al-Razzaq, and it has also been proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He was called Al-Khidr because he sat on a fur, and suddenly it began to shake green beneath him. What is meant by fur here is dry grass, which is the stubble of plants, as Abd Al-Razzaq said. It was also said that what is meant by it is the surface of the earth. And His saying: That is the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience. That is, this is the interpretation of that over which you were unable to bear it, and you could not have patience until He informed you of it from the beginning. And when He explained it to him and clarified it and made it clear and removed the difficulty, He said that it shines. And before that, the difficulty was strong and heavy, so He said: I will inform you of the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience. So He compared the heavier with the heavier, and the lighter with the lighter, as He said: And they were not able to ascend it, which is to climb to its top, nor were they able to tunnel into it, which is more difficult than that, so He compared each with what suited it in wording and meaning, and God knows best. If it is said: Why was the young man of Moses mentioned at the beginning of the story and then not mentioned after that? The answer is that what is meant by the context is the story of Moses with Al-Khidr and the mention of what happened between them, and the young man of Moses with him was Tubba, and it was stated in the previous hadiths in the Sahihs and others that he was Joshua bin Nun, and he was the one who ruled the Children of Israel after Moses, peace be upon him. This indicates the weakness of what Ibn Jarir mentioned in his interpretation where he said: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us: Ibn Ishaq told me on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Ammarah on the authority of his father on the authority of Ikrimah who said: It was said to Ibn Abbas: We have not heard any mention of the young man of Moses in a hadith, and he was with him? Ibn Abbas said in what is mentioned in the hadith of the young man, he said: The young man drank from the water and became immortal, so the scholar took him and put him in a ship, then he sent him into the sea, and it will surge with him until the Day of Resurrection, and that is because he was not allowed to drink from it so he drank. Its chain of transmission is weak, and Al-Hasan is rejected, and his father is unknown.
18:83: God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, "And they ask you, O Muhammad, about Dhul-Qarnayn", meaning about his story. We have already mentioned that the infidels of Mecca sent to the People of the Book to ask them what they could test the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with. They said: Ask him about a man who travels around the earth, and about young men who do not know what they did, and about the soul. So Surat Al-Kahf was revealed. Ibn Jarir mentioned here and Al-Umawi in his Maghazi a hadith with a chain of transmission, and it is weak, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir that a group of Jews came to ask the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Dhul-Qarnayn, so he informed them of what they had come for in the beginning. Among what he informed them of was that he was a young man from the Romans, and that he built Alexandria, and that an angel ascended with him to the heavens and took him to the dam, and he saw people whose faces were like the faces of dogs, and in it is length and strangeness, and his ascension is not correct, and most of what it contains is that it is from the stories of the Children of Israel. It is strange that Abu Zar’ah al-Razi, with his great stature, included it in full in his book, Dala’il al-Nubuwwah, which is strange of him, and it is strange that he was from the Romans. The one who was from the Romans was Alexander II, the son of Philip the Macedonian, by whom the Romans date their history. As for the first, al-Azraqi and others mentioned that he circumambulated the Kaaba with Abraham, peace be upon him, when it was first built, and believed in it and followed it, and his minister was al-Khidr, peace be upon him. As for the second, he is Alexander the son of Philip the Macedonian Greek, and his minister was the famous philosopher Aristotle. And God knows best. He is the one from whose kingdom the Roman religion dates, and he was about three hundred years before Christ, peace be upon him. As for the first mentioned in the Qur’an, he was in the time of Abraham, as al-Azraqi and others mentioned, and that he circumambulated the ancient Kaaba with Abraham, peace be upon him, when it was built, and he offered himself as a sacrifice to God. We have mentioned a good portion of his stories in the book Al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya which is sufficient, and praise be to God. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: He was a king, and he was called Dhul-Qarnayn because the two sides of his head were made of copper. He said: Some of the People of the Book said: Because he was the king of the Romans and the Persians. Some of them said: There was something like two horns on his head. Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl who said: Ali, may God be pleased with him, was asked about Dhul-Qarnayn. He said: He was a sincere servant of God, so he advised him. He called his people to God, so they struck him on his horn, so he died, then God revived him. He called his people to God, so they struck him on his horn, so he died, so he was called Dhul-Qarnayn. Shu`bah narrated it likewise on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl who heard Ali say that. It is said that he was called Dhul-Qarnayn because he reached the East and the West from where the horn of the sun rises and sets. And His statement: "Indeed, We established him in the land" means We gave him a great kingdom in which he was able to have all that is given to kings of empowerment, soldiers, war machines and sieges. For this reason, he ruled the East and the West of the earth, and the countries submitted to him, and the kings of the servants submitted to him, and the nations of the Arabs and the non-Arabs served him. For this reason, some of them mentioned that he was called Dhul-Qarnayn because he reached the two horns of the sun, its east and its west. And His statement: "And We gave him a reason for everything" Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ikrimah, As-Suddi, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and others said: It means knowledge. Qatadah also said regarding His statement: "And We gave him a reason for everything" He said: The stations of the earth and its landmarks. Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said about his statement: And We gave him a means of everything he said: Teaching languages. He said: He would not fight a people except that he spoke to them in their language. Ibn Lahi’ah said: Salim bin Ghailan told me on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Hilal that Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan said to Ka’b al-Ahbar: Do you say that Dhul-Qarnayn used to tie his horses to the Pleiades? Ka’b said to him: If you said that, then God the Most High said: And We gave him a means of everything and this is what Muawiyah, may God be pleased with him, denied about Ka’b al-Ahbar is correct, and the truth is with Muawiyah in that denial, for Muawiyah used to say about Ka’b: We would test him for lying, meaning in what he transmitted, not that he deliberately transmitted what was not in his scrolls, but the matter with his scrolls was that they were from the Israelite stories, most of which were altered, distorted and fabricated Qur’ans, and we have no need for any of it at all with the report of God the Most High and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for much evil and widespread corruption entered the people from it. Ka'b's interpretation of God's statement, "And We gave him a means of everything," and his citing as evidence for that what he finds in his books that he used to tie his horses to the Pleiades is not correct and does not match, because there is no way for humans to do any of that, nor to ascend in the means of the heavens. God said about Bilqis, "And she has been given of everything," that is, what is given to the likes of her from the kings. And so it is with Dhul-Qarnayn, God made the means easy for him, that is, the paths and means to conquer regions, districts, countries and lands, and to defeat the enemies and subdue the kings of the earth and humiliate the people of polytheism. He was given of everything that someone like him needs, a means, and God knows best. And in Al-Mukhtara by Al-Hafiz Al-Dhiya Al-Maqdisi, on the authority of Qutaybah, on the authority of Abu Uwanah, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Habib bin Hamaz, he said: I was with Ali, may God be pleased with him, and a man asked him about Dhul-Qarnayn, how did he reach the east and the west? He said, "Glory be to God, He subjected the clouds to him, and decreed the means for him, and extended His hand to him."

18:85: Ibn Abbas said, So he followed a path, meaning by the path the house. Mujahid said, So he followed a path, a house and a path between the east and the west. In a narration from Mujahid, a path, he said, a path on the earth. Qatada said, that is, he followed the houses and landmarks of the earth. Ad-Dahhak said, So he followed a path, meaning the houses. Saeed bin Jubayr said, in his statement, So he followed a path, he said, a mark. This is what Ikrimah, Ubayd bin Ya'la, and As-Suddi said. Matar said, landmarks and traces that were before that. And his saying: Until he reached the setting of the sun means that he took a path until he reached the furthest point of the earth that can be traveled from the direction of the west, which is the west of the earth. As for reaching the setting of the sun from the sky, that is impossible. And what the storytellers and narrators mention about him walking on the earth for a period of time, and the sun setting behind him, is something that has no truth to it, and most of that is from the superstitions of the People of the Book and the differences of their heretics and their lies. And his saying: He found it setting in a hot spring means that he saw the sun in his view setting in the surrounding sea, and this is the case of everyone who reaches its shore, he sees it as if it is setting in it, and it does not leave the fourth sphere in which it is fixed and does not leave it. And hot is derived according to one of the two readings from hammah, which is clay, as God Almighty said: Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay from black mud altered meaning smooth clay, and its explanation has been presented. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Nafi’ bin Abi Na’im told us, I heard Abd al-Rahman al-A’raj say: Ibn Abbas used to say about a hot spring, then he explained it as having hot mud. Nafi’ said: Ka’b al-Ahbar was asked about it, and he said: You know the Qur’an better than me, but I find it in the Book that it disappears in black mud. This is what more than one person narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Mujahid and more than one person said the same. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Muhammad bin Dinar told us, on the authority of Sa’d bin Aws, on the authority of Musadd’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to him hot mud. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He found it disappearing in a hot spring, meaning hot. This is what al-Hasan al-Basri said. Ibn Jarir said: The correct view is that they are two well-known readings, and whichever one the reader recites is correct. I said: There is no contradiction between their two meanings, as it could be hot due to its proximity to the sun’s blazing rays at sunset and its rays meeting them without a barrier, or hot in water and black mud, as Ka’b al-Ahbar and others said. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Yazid ibn Harun told us: al-Awam told us: a client of Abdullah ibn Amr told me: Abdullah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at the sun when it set and said: In the blazing fire of God, were it not for the command of God that restrains it, it would have burned everything on the earth. I said: Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Yazid ibn Harun, and there is doubt about the authenticity of this hadith, and perhaps it is from the words of Abdullah ibn Amr from his two companions whom he found on the day of Yarmouk, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Hajjaj ibn Hamza told us: Muhammad, meaning Ibn Bishr, told us: Amr ibn Maymun told us: Ibn Hadir informed us that Ibn Abbas mentioned to him that Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan recited the verse in Surat al-Kahf 18:It sets in a hot spring. Ibn Abbas said to Muawiyah: We do not recite it except as hot. So Muawiyah asked Abdullah ibn Amr: How do you recite it? He said: Abdullah, as you read it. Ibn Abbas said: I said to Muawiyah, the Qur’an was revealed in my house, so he sent for Ka’b and said to him: Where do you find the sun setting in the Torah? Ka’b said to him: Ask the Arabs, for they are more knowledgeable about it. As for me, I find the sun setting in the Torah in water and mud, and he pointed with his hand to the west. Ibn Hazir said: If I were with you, I would benefit you with words that would increase your insight in the mud. Ibn Abbas said: Then what is it? I said: In what is attributed to the saying of Tubba’ in what Dhul-Qarnayn mentioned about his adopting knowledge and following it: He reached the East and the West, seeking the means of command from a wise guide. He saw the setting of the sun at sunset in the spring of Dhi Khalab and Thaat Harmad. Ibn Abbas said: What is Khalab? I said: Mud, according to their speech. He said: What is Thaat? I said: Mud. He said: What is Harmad? I said: The black one. He said: So Ibn Abbas called a man or a boy and said: Write down what this man says. Saeed bin Jubair said: While Ibn Abbas was reciting Surat Al-Kahf, he recited: He found it setting in a hot spring. Ka’b said: By the One in Whose Hand is Ka’b’s soul, I have not heard anyone recite it as it was revealed in the Torah except Ibn Abbas, for we find it in the Torah: setting in a black mud. Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili said: Ishaq bin Abi Israel told us, Hisham bin Yusuf told us. He said in the interpretation of Ibn Jurayj: And he found near it a people. He said: A city with twelve thousand gates. If it were not for the voices of its people, people would hear the setting of the sun when it sets. His statement: And he found near it a people means a nation from among the nations. They mentioned that it was a great nation from the children of Adam. His statement: “We said: O Dhul-Qarnayn, either you punish or you treat them with good.” The meaning of this is that God Almighty empowered him over them and made him rule over them and gave him victory over them and gave him the choice if he wished to kill and take captive, and if he wished to send someone, so he knew his justice and faith in what he said. He showed His justice and His statement in His saying: But as for him who wronged meaning he persisted in his disbelief and polytheism with his Lord We will punish him Qatadah said: With killing. Al-Suddi said: He used to protect copper cows for them and put them in them until they melted. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: He used to send darkness so that it would enter their stomachs and their homes and cover them from all sides. And God knows best. And His saying: Then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment meaning severe, profound, painful and agonizing. In this is proof of the Resurrection and recompense. And His saying: But as for he who believed meaning he followed us in what we called him to of worshipping God alone with no partner. He will have the best reward meaning in the Hereafter with God the Almighty. And We will speak to him from Our command with ease Mujahid said: Well-known.

I said: Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Yazid ibn Harun, and there is doubt about the authenticity of this hadith, and perhaps it is from the words of Abdullah ibn Amr from his two companions whom he found on the day of Yarmouk, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Hajjaj ibn Hamza told us: Muhammad, meaning Ibn Bishr, told us: Amr ibn Maymun told us: Ibn Hadir informed us that Ibn Abbas mentioned to him that Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan recited the verse in Surat al-Kahf 18:It sets in a hot spring. Ibn Abbas said to Muawiyah: We do not recite it except as hot. So Muawiyah asked Abdullah ibn Amr: How do you recite it? He said: Abdullah, as you read it. Ibn Abbas said: I said to Muawiyah, the Qur’an was revealed in my house, so he sent for Ka’b and said to him: Where do you find the sun setting in the Torah? Ka’b said to him: Ask the Arabs, for they are more knowledgeable about it. As for me, I find the sun setting in the Torah in water and mud, and he pointed with his hand to the west. Ibn Hazir said: If I were with you, I would benefit you with words that would increase your insight in the mud. Ibn Abbas said: Then what is it? I said: In what is attributed to the saying of Tubba’ in what Dhul-Qarnayn mentioned about his adopting knowledge and following it: He reached the East and the West, seeking the means of command from a wise guide. He saw the setting of the sun at sunset in the spring of Dhi Khalab and Thaat Harmad. Ibn Abbas said: What is Khalab? I said: Mud, according to their speech. He said: What is Thaat? I said: Mud. He said: What is Harmad? I said: The black one. He said: So Ibn Abbas called a man or a boy and said: Write down what this man says. Saeed bin Jubair said: While Ibn Abbas was reciting Surat Al-Kahf, he recited: He found it setting in a hot spring. Ka’b said: By the One in Whose Hand is Ka’b’s soul, I have not heard anyone recite it as it was revealed in the Torah except Ibn Abbas, for we find it in the Torah: setting in a black mud. Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili said: Ishaq bin Abi Israel told us, Hisham bin Yusuf told us. He said in the interpretation of Ibn Jurayj: And he found near it a people. He said: A city with twelve thousand gates. If it were not for the voices of its people, people would hear the setting of the sun when it sets. His statement: And he found near it a people means a nation from among the nations. They mentioned that it was a great nation from the children of Adam. His statement: “We said: O Dhul-Qarnayn, either you punish or you treat them with good.” The meaning of this is that God Almighty empowered him over them and made him rule over them and gave him victory over them and gave him the choice if he wished to kill and take captive, and if he wished to send someone, so he knew his justice and faith in what he said. He showed His justice and His statement in His saying: But as for him who wronged meaning he persisted in his disbelief and polytheism with his Lord We will punish him Qatadah said: With killing. Al-Suddi said: He used to protect copper cows for them and put them in them until they melted. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: He used to send darkness so that it would enter their stomachs and their homes and cover them from all sides. And God knows best. He will have the best reward meaning in the Hereafter with God the Almighty. And We will speak to him from Our command with ease Mujahid said: Well-known.

18:89: The Almighty says: Then he took a path and traveled from the west to the east. Every time he passed by a nation, he would subdue and overcome them and call them to God Almighty. If they obeyed him, otherwise he would humiliate them and crush their noses and take their money and possessions and use from each nation what would help his armies fight the regions adjacent to them. It was mentioned in the report of the Children of Israel that he lived for one thousand nine hundred years, traversing the length and breadth of the earth until he reached the east and the west. When he reached the sunrise on the earth, as the Almighty said: He found it rising on a people meaning a nation We had not made for them against it a cover meaning they had no building to shelter them nor trees to shade them and cover them from the heat of the sun. Saeed bin Jubair said: They were short, red people whose dwellings were in the open areas and most of their livelihood was from fish. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Sahl ibn Abi al-Salt told us that I heard al-Hasan being asked about the statement of God the Almighty: We have not made for them any shelter besides it. He said: Their land cannot support a building, so when the sun rises they sink into the water, and when it sets they come out to graze as animals graze. Al-Hasan said: This is the hadith of Samurah. Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that they are in a land that does not grow anything for them, so when the sun rises they enter into flocks until when the sun declines they come out to their homes and livelihoods. And on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl that he said: They have no shelters, when the sun rises it rises upon them, so each of them has two ears, he spreads one out and wears the other. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: He found it rising on a people for whom We had not made any cover against it, he said: They are the Zanj. Ibn Jarir said regarding his statement: He found it rising on a people for whom We had not made any cover against it, he said: They had never built a building in it and no building had ever been built over them. When the sun rose, they would enter their groups until the sun declined or they would enter the sea. This is because their land had no mountains. An army came to them once and its people said to them: Do not let the sun rise on you while you are in it. They said: We will not leave until the sun rises. What are these bones? They said: These are the corpses of an army upon which the sun rose here... so they died. He said: So they fled on the earth. His statement: Likewise, and We have encompassed what is with him in knowledge, Mujahid and As-Suddi said: Knowledge, meaning that we are aware of all his conditions and the conditions of his army. Nothing of them is hidden from us, even if their nations are dispersed and the earth is cut off from them, for God, the Most High, Nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden from Him.

18:92: God Almighty says, informing about Dhul-Qarnayn, Then he followed a way, meaning, then he took a path from the east of the earth until he reached between the two dams, which are two mountains facing each other, between which there is a gap from which Gog and Magog emerge into the land of the Turks, and they spread corruption there and destroy the crops and the offspring. Gog and Magog are from the lineage of Adam, peace be upon him, as proven in the two Sahihs, "God Almighty says: O Adam, and he says, At your service and your pleasure. He says: Send the people of Hell. He says: What are the people of Hell? He says: From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine will go to Hell and one to Paradise. Then the young will turn gray and every pregnant woman will give birth to her child. He said, There are two nations among you who were not in anything except that they increased it: Gog and Magog." An-Nawawi, may God have mercy on him, narrated in his explanation of Muslim from some people that Gog and Magog were created from semen that came out of Adam and mixed with the dust, so they were created from that. Based on this, they were created from Adam. They are not from Eve. This is a very strange statement for which there is no evidence, neither from reason nor from transmission. It is not permissible to rely here on what some of the People of the Book narrate, because they have fabricated hadiths. And God knows best. In Musnad of Imam Ahmad, on the authority of Samurah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Noah had three sons: Sam, the father of the Arabs, Ham, the father of the blacks, and Japheth, the father of the Turks.” Some scholars said that these are from the lineage of Japheth, the father of the Turks. He said that these were called Turks because they were left behind the dam from this side, otherwise they would be relatives of those, but those were tyrants, corrupt, and bold. Ibn Jarir mentioned here on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih a long and amazing account of the life of Dhul-Qarnayn and his building of the dam and how it happened to him. It contains length, strangeness, and oddity in their forms, descriptions, their height, the shortness of some of them, and their ears. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated strange hadiths on this matter, whose chains of transmission are not authentic, and God knows best. And his saying: And he found besides them a people who could hardly understand a word meaning because of the difficulty of their speech and their distance from the people They said, ‘O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are corrupters in the land, so shall we make for you a great reward?’ Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas a great reward meaning that they wanted to collect for them money from among themselves to give him so that he would create a barrier between him and them, so Dhul-Qarnayn said with chastity, religion, righteousness and intent for good What my Lord has empowered me in is better meaning that what God has given me of kingship and empowerment is better for me than what you are collecting as Solomon, peace be upon him, said Do you provide me with wealth? What God has given me is better than what He has given you the verse, and thus Dhul-Qarnayn said: What I am in is better than what you are spending, but help me with strength, meaning with your work and building tools I will make between you and them a barrier * Bring me sheets of iron and zabar is the plural of zabra, which is a piece of it, said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah, and it is like a brick.
