18:97: The Almighty says, informing about Gog and Magog, that they were not able to climb over this dam, nor were they able to tunnel through it from below. Since it was easier to climb over it than to tunnel through it, He responded to each with what was appropriate for it, saying, But they were not able to climb over it, nor were they able to tunnel through it. This is evidence that they were not able to tunnel through it or anything in it. As for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, Ruh narrated to us, Saeed bin Abi Arubah narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to us, Abu Rafi’ narrated to us, Abu Hurairah narrated to us, from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Gog and Magog will dig the dam every day until they can almost see the rays of the sun. The one who is over them will say, ‘Go back, you will dig it tomorrow.’ So they will return to it as intense as ever, until when their time has come and God wants to send them against the people, they will dig until they can almost see the rays of the sun. The one who is over them will say, ‘Go back, you will dig it tomorrow, God willing.’ So they will return to it as it was when they left it. So they will dig it and come out to the people, drying up the water, and the people will take refuge from them in their fortresses. They will shoot their arrows into the sky, and they will return with something like blood on them, and they will say, ‘We have defeated the people of the earth and have overcome the people of the heavens.’ So God will send a plague on their necks and kill them with it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, the beasts of the earth will grow fat and thank you for their flesh and blood.’” Ahmad also narrated it on the authority of Hasan, who is Ibn Musa. Al-Ashhab narrated from Sufyan from Qatada with it, and Ibn Majah narrated it likewise from Azhar bin Marwan from Abd al-A’la from Saeed bin Abi Arooba from Qatada who said: Abu Rafi’ narrated and al-Tirmidhi included it from the hadith of Abu Awanah from Qatada, then he said: It is strange and is not known except from this source, and its chain of transmission is good and strong, but its text is strange in its being raised, because the apparent meaning of the verse requires that they were not able to climb it or penetrate it due to its perfect construction, solidity and strength. However, this has been narrated from Ka’b al-Ahbar that before their departure, they would come to it and lick it until nothing remained of it except a little, and they would say, Tomorrow we will conquer it. So they would come the next day and it had returned to how it was, and they would lick it until nothing remained of it except a little, and they would say, So that is it. So they would wake up and it would be as it was, and they would lick it and say, Tomorrow we will conquer it. They would be inspired to say, Insha God, and they would wake up and it would be as they left it, and they would conquer it. This is valid, and perhaps Abu Hurairah received it from Ka’b, because he often used to sit with him and talk to him, so Abu Hurairah narrated it, and some of the narrators were mistaken. It was narrated on his authority that it was raised, so he raised it, and God knows best. What we have said is supported by the fact that they were not able to dig it or dig anything from it, and by the strangeness of this chain of transmission, which is narrated by Imam Ahmad: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Zainab bint Abi Salma, on the authority of Habeeba bint Umm Habeeba bint Abi Sufyan, on the authority of her mother Umm Habeeba, on the authority of Zainab bint Jahsh, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace - Sufyan said: Four women - she said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, woke up from his sleep with his face red and he said: There is no god but God. Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near. Today a hole has been opened in the barrier of Gog and Magog like this.” And he said: “I said: O Messenger of God, will we perish while there are righteous people among us?” He said: Yes, if evil increases. This is a sound hadith, and Al-Bukhari and Muslim agreed to include it in the hadith of Al-Zuhri, but the mention of Habeeba was omitted in Al-Bukhari’s narration, and Muslim confirmed it. It contains few, rare things that occur in the art of chain of transmission, including the narration of Al-Zuhri from Urwah, and they are both followers, and including the meeting of four women in its chain of transmission, all of them narrating from one another, then each of them is a female companion, then two. Two stepdaughters and two wives, may God be pleased with them. Something similar to this was also narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah. Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Marzuq told us, Muammil ibn Ismail told us, Wahib told us on the authority of Ibn Tawus on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Today a barrier like this has been opened in the dam of Gog and Magog, and he counted ninety. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it on the authority of Wahib with it. His statement: He said, ‘This is a mercy from my Lord,’ means when Dhul-Qarnayn built it. He said, ‘This is a mercy from my Lord,’ means to the people, as he placed a barrier between them and Gog and Magog to prevent them from causing corruption on earth. So when the promise of my Lord comes to pass, meaning when the true promise draws near, He will make it level, meaning He will level it with the ground. The Arabs say: a she-camel is level if its back is flat and it has no humps. God Almighty said: But when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it level, meaning level with the ground. And Ikrimah said about His statement: So when the promise of my Lord comes to pass, He will make it level, he said: a path as it was, and the promise of my Lord is true, meaning it will inevitably happen. And His statement: And We will leave some of them, meaning the people on that Day, meaning the Day when this dam is destroyed and these people emerge and surge among the people and corrupt the people’s wealth and destroy their things. And thus Al-Suddi said about His statement: And We will leave some of them that Day surging against others, he said: that is when they emerge against the people, and all of this is before the Resurrection and after the Antichrist, as will be explained when He said: Until, when Gog and Magog are let loose and they rush from every height * And the true promise draws near, the verse. And thus he said here: And We will leave some of them that Day surging against others, he said: this is the beginning of the Resurrection. And the Trumpet will be blown, after that, and We will gather them together, and others said: rather what is meant by His statement: And We will leave some of them that Day surging against others, he said: when the jinn and mankind surge on the Day of Resurrection, mankind and jinn will mix. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Hamid on the authority of Yaqub al-Qummi on the authority of Harun ibn Antara, on the authority of a sheikh from Banu Fazara, regarding his statement, And We will let some of them surge against others on that Day, he said: When mankind and jinn surge, Iblis will say: I know for you the knowledge of this matter. So he will set out to the east and find that the angels have covered the earth. Then he will set out to the west and find that the angels have covered the earth, so he will say: There is no escape. Then he will set out to the right and to the left to the farthest end of the earth and find that the angels have covered the earth, so he will say: There is no escape. While he is like this, a path will appear to him like a trap, so he and his offspring will be seized by it. While they are on it, they will attack the Fire, so God will bring out a keeper from the keeper of the Fire, and he will say: O Iblis, did you not have a position with your Lord, were you not in Paradise? He says: This is not a day of reproach. If God had imposed on me an obligation, I would have worshipped Him in it in a way that none of His creation has worshipped Him like. He says: Then God has imposed on you an obligation. He says: What is it? He says: He commands you to enter the Fire. So he lingers over him, and he says: With him and his offspring with his wings. So he throws them into the Fire, and the Fire sighs a sigh that will not leave any close angel or sent prophet except that he will kneel on his knees. And thus Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Ya`qub al-Qummi with it, then he narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ya`qub on the authority of Harun on the authority of `Antarah on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn `Abbas: And We will leave some of them that Day surging against others. He said: The humans and the jinn surging against each other. Al-Tabarani said: Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Al-Abbas Al-Isfahani told us, Abu Masoud Ahmad bin Al-Furat told us, Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi told us, Al-Mughirah bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Wahb bin Jaber, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Gog and Magog are from the children of Adam, and if they were sent forth, they would corrupt the livelihoods of the people, and not a single man of them would die without leaving behind a thousand or more of his descendants, and behind them are three nations: Tawil, Tais, and Mansak.” This is a strange hadith, rather it is a weak and reprehensible one. An-Nasa'i narrated from the hadith of Shu'bah from An-Nu'man ibn Salim from Amr ibn Aws from his father from his grandfather Aws ibn Abi Aws with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: "Yajuj and Majuj will have women with whom they may have intercourse, and trees which they may pollinate as they may wish. No man will die except that he will leave behind a thousand or more descendants." And his statement, And the Trumpet will be blown. The Trumpet, as mentioned in the hadith, means a horn that will be blown, and the one who will be blown is Israfil, peace be upon him, as mentioned earlier in the hadith in its entirety. There are many hadiths on this subject. And in the hadith from Atiyyah from Ibn Abbas and Abu Sa'id with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: "How can I enjoy myself while the companion of the horn has taken hold of the horn, bent his forehead, and listened to when he will be commanded? They said: What should we say? He said: Say: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. In God we trust." And his statement, Then We will gather them all together, means We will bring them all to account. "Say: The first and the last * Will surely be gathered to an appointed time on a known Day." And We will gather them together, not leaving behind a single one of them.
18:98: The Almighty says, informing about Gog and Magog, that they were not able to climb over this dam, nor were they able to tunnel through it from below. Since it was easier to climb over it than to tunnel through it, He responded to each with what was appropriate for it, saying, But they were not able to climb over it, nor were they able to tunnel through it. This is evidence that they were not able to tunnel through it or anything in it. As for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, Ruh narrated to us, Saeed bin Abi Arubah narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to us, Abu Rafi’ narrated to us, Abu Hurairah narrated to us, from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Gog and Magog will dig the dam every day until they can almost see the rays of the sun. The one who is over them will say, ‘Go back, you will dig it tomorrow.’ So they will return to it as intense as ever, until when their time has come and God wants to send them against the people, they will dig until they can almost see the rays of the sun. The one who is over them will say, ‘Go back, you will dig it tomorrow, God willing.’ So they will return to it as it was when they left it. So they will dig it and come out to the people, drying up the water, and the people will take refuge from them in their fortresses. They will shoot their arrows into the sky, and they will return with something like blood on them, and they will say, ‘We have defeated the people of the earth and have overcome the people of the heavens.’ So God will send a plague on their necks and kill them with it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, the beasts of the earth will grow fat and thank you for their flesh and blood.’” Ahmad also narrated it on the authority of Hasan, who is Ibn Musa. Al-Ashhab narrated from Sufyan from Qatada with it, and Ibn Majah narrated it likewise from Azhar bin Marwan from Abd al-A’la from Saeed bin Abi Arooba from Qatada who said: Abu Rafi’ narrated and al-Tirmidhi included it from the hadith of Abu Awanah from Qatada, then he said: It is strange and is not known except from this source, and its chain of transmission is good and strong, but its text is strange in its being raised, because the apparent meaning of the verse requires that they were not able to climb it or penetrate it due to its perfect construction, solidity and strength. However, this has been narrated from Ka’b al-Ahbar that before their departure, they would come to it and lick it until nothing remained of it except a little, and they would say, Tomorrow we will conquer it. So they would come the next day and it had returned to how it was, and they would lick it until nothing remained of it except a little, and they would say, So that is it. So they would wake up and it would be as it was, and they would lick it and say, Tomorrow we will conquer it. They would be inspired to say, Insha God, and they would wake up and it would be as they left it, and they would conquer it. This is valid, and perhaps Abu Hurairah received it from Ka’b, because he often used to sit with him and talk to him, so Abu Hurairah narrated it, and some of the narrators were mistaken. It was narrated on his authority that it was raised, so he raised it, and God knows best. What we have said is supported by the fact that they were not able to dig it or dig anything from it, and by the strangeness of this chain of transmission, which is narrated by Imam Ahmad: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Zainab bint Abi Salma, on the authority of Habeeba bint Umm Habeeba bint Abi Sufyan, on the authority of her mother Umm Habeeba, on the authority of Zainab bint Jahsh, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace - Sufyan said: Four women - she said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, woke up from his sleep with his face red and he said: There is no god but God. Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near. Today a hole has been opened in the barrier of Gog and Magog like this.” And he said: “I said: O Messenger of God, will we perish while there are righteous people among us?” He said: Yes, if evil increases. This is a sound hadith, and Al-Bukhari and Muslim agreed to include it in the hadith of Al-Zuhri, but the mention of Habeeba was omitted in Al-Bukhari’s narration, and Muslim confirmed it. It contains few, rare things that occur in the art of chain of transmission, including the narration of Al-Zuhri from Urwah, and they are both followers, and including the meeting of four women in its chain of transmission, all of them narrating from one another, then each of them is a female companion, then two. Two stepdaughters and two wives, may God be pleased with them. Something similar to this was also narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah. Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Marzuq told us, Muammil ibn Ismail told us, Wahib told us on the authority of Ibn Tawus on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Today a barrier like this has been opened in the dam of Gog and Magog, and he counted ninety. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it on the authority of Wahib with it. His statement: He said, ‘This is a mercy from my Lord,’ means when Dhul-Qarnayn built it. He said, ‘This is a mercy from my Lord,’ means to the people, as he placed a barrier between them and Gog and Magog to prevent them from causing corruption on earth. So when the promise of my Lord comes to pass, meaning when the true promise draws near, He will make it level, meaning He will level it with the ground. The Arabs say: a she-camel is level if its back is flat and it has no humps. God Almighty said: But when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it level, meaning level with the ground. And Ikrimah said about His statement: So when the promise of my Lord comes to pass, He will make it level, he said: a path as it was, and the promise of my Lord is true, meaning it will inevitably happen. 18:100: God Almighty says, informing about what He will do to the infidels on the Day of Resurrection, that He will show them Hell, that is, He will expose it to them and make it apparent so that they can see the torment and punishment in it before they enter it, so that this will be more effective in hastening their worry and grief. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Hell will be brought forth on the Day of Resurrection, led by seventy thousand reins, with each rein seventy thousand angels.’ Then he said, informing about them: ‘Those whose eyes were covered from My remembrance.’ That is, they were heedless, blind, and turned a deaf ear to accepting guidance and following the truth, as He said: ‘And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful - We appoint for him a devil, who is to him a companion.’ And here He said: ‘And they were unable to hear.’ That is, they did not understand God’s commands and prohibitions. Then He said: ‘Do those who disbelieve think that they can take My servants as allies other than Me?’ That is, they believed that this would be good for them and that they would benefit from it. ‘No! They will deny their worship and will be against them.’ That is why God, the Most High, informed us that He has prepared Hell for them on the Day of Resurrection as a home.

He said: No, they are the Jews and Christians. As for the Jews, they denied Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. 18:107: God the Almighty tells us about His happy servants, who are those who believed in God and His Messenger, and believed in what the Messengers brought, that they will have the Gardens of Paradise. Mujahid said: Paradise is the garden in Roman. Ka'b, As-Suddi and Ad-Dahhak said: It is the garden in which there are grape trees. Abu Umamah said: Paradise is the navel of Paradise. Qatada said: Paradise is the highest, middle and best part of Paradise. This has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatada, from Al-Hasan, from Samurah, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Firdaws is the highest, middle and best part of Paradise. Ismail ibn Muslim narrated it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and Qatada narrated it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), from Anas ibn Malik with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), similarly. Ibn Jarir may God have mercy on him narrated all of this. In the two Sahihs: If you ask God for Paradise, ask Him for Paradise, for it is the highest part of Paradise and the middle part of Paradise, and from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth. And the Almighty’s saying: A lodging means hospitality, for hospitality is hospitality. And His saying: They will abide therein means they will reside and dwell therein, never leaving it. They will not desire to leave it means they will not choose anything else from it and they will not love anything else, as the poet said: My heart has become dark, I do not desire anyone but her, nor will I turn away from her love In His saying: They do not desire to be away from it is an indication of their desire for it and their love for it, even though it might be imagined that someone who is permanently residing in a place might become bored or tired of it. So He informed that with this permanence and eternal eternity, they do not choose to change, move, depart, journey, or replace their place.

18:109: The Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, if the water of the sea were ink for the pen with which the words of God, His wisdom, and His verses indicating Him are written, the sea would be exhausted before it could finish writing that. And if We brought the like of it, meaning another sea like it, then another, and so on, seas that support it and with which it is written, the words of God would not be exhausted, as the Almighty said: “And if all the trees on the earth were pens, and the sea were replenished thereafter by seven more seas, the Words of God would not be exhausted. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise.” Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: The likeness of the knowledge of all the servants in the knowledge of God is like a drop of water from all the seas, and God revealed that: “Say, ‘If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted. ’” He says that if those seas were ink for the words of God, and all the trees were pens, the pens would be broken, the water of the sea would be exhausted, and the words of God would remain standing, nothing would destroy them, because no one can estimate His value or praise Him as He should be, until He is the one who praises Himself. Indeed, our Lord, as He says, and above what we say, that the example of the pleasures of this world, its beginning and its end, in comparison to the pleasures of the Hereafter is like a mustard seed in the midst of the entire earth.
18:110: At-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Hisham bin Ammar on the authority of Ismail bin Ayyash, on the authority of Amr bin Qais Al-Kufi that he heard Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan say: This is the last verse that was revealed. God Almighty says to His Messenger Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, Say to these polytheists who denied your message to them, I am only a human being like you. So whoever claims that I am a liar, let him come with something like what I have come with, for I do not know the unseen in what I have told you of the past about what you asked about the story of the People of the Cave and the story of Dhul-Qarnayn, which is identical in essence, and were it not for what God has informed me of, and I only informed you that your god whom I call you to worship is one God with no partner so whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord meaning His reward and righteous recompense let him do righteous work meaning what is in accordance with God’s law and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone which is what is intended for the sake of God alone with no partner, and these are the two pillars of work. The recipient must be sincere to God and in accordance with the law of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Muammar from Abdul Karim Al-Jazari from Tawus who said: A man said: O Messenger of God, I stand at the stations seeking the face of God and I love to see my homeland. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not answer him anything until this verse was revealed: So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone. This is how Mujahid and others transmitted this. Al-A’mash said: Hamza Abu Amara, a client of Banu Hashim, told us from Shahr bin Hawshab who said: A man came to Ubadah bin As-Samit and said: Tell me about what I am asking you about. Have you seen a man who prays seeking the face of God and loves to be praised, who fasts seeking the face of God and loves to be praised, who gives charity seeking the face of God and loves to be praised, who performs Hajj seeking the face of God and loves to be praised? Ubadah said: He has nothing. God the Most High says: I am the best partner, so whoever has a partner with Me, he is all his, I have no need of him. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr told us, Kathir ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Rabih ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Saeed al-Khudri, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: We used to take turns with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we would spend the night with him. If he had a need or something came to him at night, he would send us. The people who were waiting for the reward and the people who were on duty increased in number, so we would talk. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to us and said: What is this whispering? He said: We said: We have repented to God, O Prophet of God, we were only mentioning the Messiah and we were afraid of him. He said: Shall I not tell you of what I fear for you more than the Messiah? We said: Yes. He said: Hidden polytheism is that a man stands up to pray in the place of another man. Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr told us, Abdul Hamid, meaning Ibn Bahram, told us: Shahr Ibn Hawshab said: Ibn Ghanem said: When Abu al-Darda’ and I entered the mosque of al-Jabiyah, we met Ubadah Ibn al-Samit, so he took my right with his left, and Abu al-Darda’s left with his right, and he came out walking between us while we were whispering, and God knows best what we were whispering. Ubadah Ibn al-Samit said: If the life of one of you or both of you is long, you will soon see a man from the ranks of the Muslims, meaning from among the reciters of the Qur’an on the tongue of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he repeated it and began it and made lawful what it permitted and made unlawful what it prohibited and placed it in its proper places, and it will not be distorted among you except as the head of a dead donkey is distorted. He said: While we were like that, Shaddad bin Aws may God be pleased with him and Awf bin Malik came out and sat with us. Shaddad said: What I fear most for you, O people, is what I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: Of hidden desire and polytheism. Ubadah bin as-Samit and Abu ad-Darda’ said: O God, forgive us! Did not the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) tell us that Satan had despaired of being worshipped in the Arabian Peninsula? As for hidden desire, we know it is the desires of this world, its women and its lusts. So what is this polytheism that you are frightening us with, O Shaddad? Shaddad said: Tell me, if you saw a man praying for a man, or fasting for a man, or giving charity on his behalf, would you think that he has committed polytheism? They said: Yes, by God, whoever prays for a man or fasts or gives charity on his behalf has committed shirk. Shaddad said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever prays to show off has committed shirk, whoever fasts to show off has committed shirk, and whoever gives charity to show off has committed shirk. Awf ibn Malik said at that: Shouldn’t he do all of that work for his own sake, so he does what is purely for him and leaves what he has associated with? Shaddad said at that: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “God says: I am the best partner for whoever associates with Me. Whoever associates something with Me, his work, whether little or much, is for his partner with whom he associated. I am independent of him.” Another chain of transmission for some of it Imam Ahmad said: Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad told me, Ubadah bin Nassi told us on the authority of Shaddad bin Aws, may God be pleased with him, that he cried, and it was said to him: What makes you cry? He said: Something I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that made me cry. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: I fear for my nation polytheism and hidden desire. I said: O Messenger of God, will your nation associate partners with God after you? He said: Yes, for they do not worship the sun, nor the moon, nor a stone, nor an idol, but they show off with their actions, and hidden desire is that one of them fasts in the morning and a desire from his desires is presented to him, so he abandons his fast. Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Dhakwan on the authority of Ubadah bin Nassi, and Ubadah is weak, and there is a problem with his hearing it from Shaddad. Another hadith Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Al-Husayn bin Ali bin Ja`far Al-Ahmar told us, Ali bin Thabit told us, Qays bin Abi Hasin told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God will say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:I am the best partner. Whoever associates anyone with Me, it is all his.” Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, I heard Al-`Ala’ narrating on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrating it on the authority of God, the Almighty, that He said: “I am the best partner. Whoever does an action in which he associates someone with Me, I am innocent of it, and it is for the one he associated.” He is the only one who narrated it from this source. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yunus told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Yazid, meaning Ibn Al-Haad, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mahmoud Ibn Labid, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What I fear most for you is minor polytheism. They said: What is minor polytheism, O Messenger of God? He said: “Hypocrisy. God will say on the Day of Resurrection when people are rewarded for their deeds: ‘Go to those for whom you were showing off in this world, and see if you find any reward with them.’” Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Bakir told us, Abdul Hamid, meaning Ibn Ja`far, told us, my father told me, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Mina`, on the authority of Abu Sa`id ibn Abi Fadala al-Ansari, who was one of the Companions, that he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “When God gathers the first and the last for a day about which there is no doubt, a caller will call out: Whoever associated anyone with a deed he did for God, let him seek his reward from other than God, for God is the most independent of partners from association.” Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Muhammad, who is al-Barsani, with it. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Malik told us, Bakkar told us, my father told me - meaning Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Bakra - on the authority of Abi Bakra, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever listens, God will listen to him, and whoever shows off, God will show off to him. Imam Ahmad said: Muawiyah told us, Shaiban told us on the authority of Firas on the authority of Atiyah on the authority of Abu Saeed al-Khudri, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever shows off, God will show off to him, and whoever shows off, God will hear him. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed told us on the authority of Shu’bah, Amr bin Marra told me: I heard a man in the house of Abu Ubaidah who heard Abdullah bin Amr telling Ibn Umar that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever makes people hear about his deeds, God will hear about them, and his character will be bad, he will be belittled and despised. Then Abdullah’s eyes welled up with tears. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Amr bin Yahya Al-Aili told us, Al-Harith bin Ghassan told us, Abu Imran Al-Joni told us on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The deeds of the sons of Adam will be presented before God Almighty on the Day of Resurrection in sealed records. God will say: Throw this away and accept this. The angels will say: O Lord, by God, we have seen nothing from him but good. He will say: His work was not for My sake, and I do not accept any work today except that which is intended for My sake.” Then he said: Al-Harith bin Ghassan was narrated by a group of people, and he is a trustworthy Basran, and there is nothing wrong with him. Ibn Wahb said: Yazid bin Ayyad told me on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman Al-Araj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Qais Al-Khuza’i, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever stands for show and to be heard will continue to be in the hatred of God until he sits down. Abu Ya`la said: Muhammad bin Abi Bakr told us, Muhammad bin Dinar told us, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Hijri, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Awf bin Malik, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever prays well when people can see him and prays poorly when he is alone, that is an act of disdain with which he disdains his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. Ibn Jarir said: Abu `Amir Isma`il bin `Amr al-Sakuni told us, Hisham bin `Ammar told us, Ibn `Ayyash told us, `Amr bin Qais al-Kindi told us that he heard Mu`awiyah bin Abi Sufyan recite this verse: So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord 1:13, and he said: It is the last verse revealed from the Qur’an. This is a problematic trace, for this verse is the last verse of Surat al-Kahf, and the entirety of Surat al-Kahf is Meccan. Perhaps Mu`awiyah meant that no verse was revealed after it that would abrogate it or change its ruling, but rather it is confirmed and decisive, so some of the narrators were confused about that and narrated it according to the meaning as he understood it, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hasan bin Shaqiq told us, Al-Nadr bin Shumayl told us, Abu Qurrah told us on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites at night, ‘So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord’ the verse, will have a light from Aden Abyan to Mecca, the angels filling that light. Very strange, the last interpretation of Surat Al-Kahf.
